stories.title: Dalit-Muslim votes could shape UP's power equation:How challenging is the Owaisi-Chandrashekhar DM combination for the grand alliance and BSP?
stories.summary: A fresh attempt to consolidate Dalit and Muslim voters is taking shape in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The newly formed alliance between Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar is also based on this electoral strategy. With BSP chief Mayawati's political influence weakening, sections of the Dalit community are looking for new leadership. Although the BSP has expressed confidence in repeating its 2007 electoral performance, it has so far failed to inspire confidence even among its core voters. The BSP is hoping for a turnaround through the rally scheduled for December 6 to mark the death anniversary of Dr BR Ambedkar. Meanwhile, Chandrashekhar is trying to fill the political space left by the party's declining influence through his Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram). Jatav voters are also moving away from Mayawati In the 2017 Assembly elections, the BSP secured 87% of Jatav votes and 44% of non-Jatav Dalit votes. The voting pattern changed in 2022. Among Jatavs, 65% voted for the BSP, 9% for the SP, 20% for the BJP and 1% for the Congress. Among non-Jatav Dalits, 40% voted for the BJP, 27% for the BSP, 23% for the SP and 4% for the Congress. This showed a shift in Dalit voters' preferences within just five years. Between the two elections, the BJP gained the support of 22% of Jatav voters and 17% of non-Jatav voters, as indicated by the figures. The 2024 Lok Sabha elections brought another shift in Dalit voting patterns, driven by the narrative that the Constitution was under threat. Around 56% of Dalit votes went to the INDIA bloc, while the NDA secured 29% and the BSP 15%. The impact of the SP's PDA (Backward Classes, Dalits and Minorities) formula was also visible. However, the BSP remained the leading choice among Jatav voters, securing 44% of their votes. The INDIA bloc received 25%, while the NDA got 24%. This indicated that even among Jatavs, parties other than the BSP had begun finding support. In effect, 20% of Jatav voters and 11% of non-Jatav voters who had supported the BJP moved towards the SP-Congress alliance within two years. This shift helped the SP-Congress alliance bridge a gap of 70–80 lakh votes and move ahead in Uttar Pradesh. Muslim voters remain firmly aligned with the SP In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, around 79% of Muslim voters supported the Samajwadi Party (SP), while the BSP received 6% and the Congress 3%. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, 92% of Muslim voters backed the SP-Congress alliance. This indicates that a large section of the state's Muslim electorate has rallied behind the parties seen as the main challengers to the BJP. Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi says Muslim voters in Uttar Pradesh tend to unite behind the candidate they believe has the strongest chance of defeating the BJP nominee. This varies from constituency to constituency, but the INDIA bloc is currently their preferred choice. He adds that in Muslim-majority constituencies, the presence of several Muslim candidates could lead to some division of votes, but the split is likely to be marginal and may not significantly affect the election result. Muslim votes can influence outcomes in SC-reserved constituencies Around 80% of Uttar Pradesh's Muslim population is Sunni. In several of the state's 84 Scheduled Caste (SC)-reserved Assembly constituencies, Muslim voters play a decisive role. In seats such as Nagina, Purqazi, Dhanaura and Nohjhil, candidates may belong to the Dalit community, but the outcome can depend on the 35–40% Muslim electorate. Like Mayawati, Chandrashekhar belongs to the Jatav community. Jatavs account for around 12% of Uttar Pradesh's Dalit population. There are five reserved constituencies where Jatav voters make up more than 25% of the electorate. Their share stands at around 33% in Agra Cantt, 31% in Rampur Maniharan, 28% in Chunar, 28% in Saharanpur Dehat and 25% in Rasoolabad, making them an important factor in these constituencies. Owaisi and Chandrashekhar face the challenge of bringing Dalit and Muslim voters together The biggest challenge for Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar will be to consolidate Dalit and Muslim voters behind their alliance. Chandrashekhar will need to strengthen his political base among Dalit youth, particularly within the Jatav community. Owaisi, meanwhile, will have to challenge the SP's strong hold over Muslim voters. If Chandrashekhar manages to attract a section of Jatav voters along with non-Jatav Dalits, the BSP's support base could weaken further. A split in Muslim votes, on the other hand, could affect the SP-Congress alliance. Owaisi and Chandrashekhar are planning to demonstrate their political strength through a joint rally at Lucknow's Ramabai Ambedkar Park on November 26. Their message is that Dalits, who account for 21% of the state's population, and Muslims, who make up 19%, can come together to choose their own government. Projecting Chandrashekhar as the alliance's chief ministerial face is also an attempt to attract Dalit voters. Sources indicate that AIMIM's Uttar Pradesh president, Shaukat Ali, could be projected as the alliance's deputy chief ministerial face at the rally. Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans believes the Owaisi-Chandrashekhar alliance could affect the INDIA bloc's electoral prospects. He points out that in the 2022 Assembly elections, 114 constituencies recorded victory margins of fewer than 10,000 votes. Of these, the BJP won 63 seats and the SP 41. In 10 constituencies, the winning margin was less than 500 votes. Congress's declining core vote base strengthened the SP and BSP The Congress last came to power in Uttar Pradesh with a full majority in 1985, winning 269 seats. Although the party remained part of coalition politics in the years that followed, it never regained the strength to form a government on its own. Until 1989, the Congress's core voter base comprised Dalits, Muslims and Brahmins. However, the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and the OBC reservation agitation in the 1990s led to a shift in these voting groups. Brahmin voters moved towards the BJP, Dalits gravitated towards the BSP, while OBC voters increasingly backed the Samajwadi Party. Muslim voters, meanwhile, began rallying behind whichever party they believed had the best chance of defeating the BJP, depending on the political circumstances.

stories.title: Azam Khan was helpless a year ago, now challenges govt:Out of jail, he takes on BJP; will 'Khan Sahab's' aggressive stance backfire?
stories.summary: This time, Azam Khan has come out of jail with a much more aggressive stance towards the BJP government. His recent remarks include statements such as, "Who is the son of a mother who can stop me from contesting elections?", "The rulers are extremely cruel and the entire country is scared" and "Bodies will start flying in the air." However, when he was released from jail on September 23, 2025, his statements reflected more disappointment and helplessness. The sharpness and bitterness that once defined his tone appeared to be missing. What changed over the past year? What happened over the past year that has brought Azam Khan back to his old, combative style? We examine the reasons in this UP Explainer. Legal setbacks and the 2027 Assembly elections have changed Azam Khan's tone The shift in Azam Khan's attitude over the past year is the result of a series of legal setbacks and the approaching 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The change becomes clearer when we compare his statements from September 2025 with his recent remarks. A) Azam Khan's position in September 2025 B) At the time, his family and future were his biggest concerns In October 2023, Azam Khan was sentenced in the fake birth certificate case and subsequently lodged in Sitapur jail. After spending nearly two years behind bars, he was physically and mentally exhausted. Dozens of cases were pending against him, and he constantly feared being sent back to prison. His wife, Tazeen Fatima, and son, Abdullah Azam, were also facing legal troubles and convictions. At the time, his priority was to protect himself and his family from further legal complications rather than take on the government. C) ED arrest outside jail fuelled his anger On November 17, 2025, Azam Khan and his son Abdullah were sentenced to seven years in the two PAN cards case. Both were sent to jail again. After securing bail, when they walked out of Rampur jail on October 31, 2026, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested Azam Khan at the gate itself. Repeated jail terms and the action against his dream project, Jauhar University, turned his frustration into deep political anger. By the time he walked out of Ghaziabad's Dasna jail on November 18, Azam had returned to his old, combative style. The bail granted by the High Court and observations made by the Supreme Court also helped restore his confidence. He began to feel that he had little left to lose, prompting him to speak more openly. D) Azam Khan's political influence in Rampur has weakened When Azam returned to Rampur on November 18 after his release from Dasna jail, he was accompanied by a convoy of more than 100 vehicles. A large crowd gathered outside his house and raised slogans of "The lion has arrived". The gathering pointed to two things: First, people continue to sympathise with Azam and his family over the legal action taken against them. Second, it showed that Azam remains the only leader in Rampur who can still bring thousands of people onto the streets in his name. Overall, Azam's political ground has weakened. He now faces the challenge of not only taking on the BJP but also proving to his own party and the people of Rampur that he remains the region's most powerful political force. E) Azam Khan's aggressive return could benefit both SP and BJP Azam Khan's combative approach is a double-edged sword for both the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the BJP, carrying potential gains as well as risks. For the SP, his return is a major relief. Leaders such as Chandrashekhar and Asaduddin Owaisi had accused Akhilesh Yadav of abandoning Azam and leaving him to fend for himself. His return could now boost morale among SP workers. More importantly, the party could gain a strong campaigner for dozens of seats in western Uttar Pradesh. Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says Azam Khan is the biggest Muslim political face in Uttar Pradesh. Although Asaduddin Owaisi is trying to attract Muslim voters, Kalhans believes Azam's active presence could prevent the Muslim vote from splitting. Azam's aggressive comeback also poses a direct challenge to the BJP. His open defiance of the BJP government has sent out a message that he has not bowed despite what he describes as the government's "oppression and excesses". His image as a leader who has stood firm in the face of adversity could create problems for the BJP. However, political analyst Ratanmani Lal believes the BJP could also use Azam's aggression to its advantage. His sharp remarks could lead to polarisation, dividing voters along religious lines. Political analyst Ravindra Rana says the BJP raises the issue of curbing "mafia rule and hooliganism" in Uttar Pradesh. The party could use Azam's aggressive statements to claim that the SP wants to bring back the "old days". This could strengthen the BJP's campaign around Hindutva and strict law and order. According to political experts, which party gains more from Azam's return will depend on the direction the election campaign takes. The SP stands to benefit if Azam uses his influence to unite Muslim voters and raise questions against the government. The BJP could gain if it turns Azam's anger and statements into a central election issue, shifting the campaign towards Hindu-Muslim polarisation or law and order. Overall, Azam Khan could prove to be a key factor in the 2027 Assembly elections. His return may make the SP's path to victory easier, but if his statements backfire, they could also strengthen the BJP's electoral campaign.

stories.title: Iqra Hasan tells Imran Masood to set aside his ego:Why should SP give a winning seat to Congress? Must give up stubbornness to defeat BJP
stories.summary: Congress MP Imran Masood has lashed out at the Samajwadi Party's first list of candidates for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. He said, "We are not beggars waiting to receive something from Akhilesh. You announced the candidates without any discussion, so why are we even talking?" After Imran's statement, SP MP Iqra Hasan advised him to exercise restraint. Iqra said that Imran Masood would have to set his ego aside. If the BJP is to be defeated, he would have to give up his stubbornness. The SP MP asked why the SP should give its winning seats to the Congress. Iqra said that the 26 seats given to the Congress include the constituencies of two of its sitting MLAs. There are four seats where the Congress finished second in 2022. In addition, we took 20 seats directly from their list. Meanwhile, Imran Masood heaped praise on Mayawati during a news channel programme. He said- If Behenji (Mayawati) steps out of the room, the state's entire picture will change. Asked whether the Congress would form an alliance with the BSP, Imran Masood said, "Rahul Gandhi and Kharge sahib have to decide that, not me. A mission and a movement died simply because Behenji remained confined to her room. Mayawati ji was a very senior leader of Uttar Pradesh." Meanwhile, the deadlock over seat-sharing between the Samajwadi Party and the Congress is becoming increasingly complicated. In response to the Congress's demand for 125 seats, the Samajwadi Party handed over a list of only 26 seats. Not only that, before the talks could progress, the Samajwadi Party released its first list of five candidates at 10 p.m. on Tuesday night. It includes the two seats in Saharanpur that the Congress had claimed. Earlier, Akhilesh wrote on 'X', "The process has begun with the first 26 winnable seats. The discussions will move forward through mutual understanding and cooperation." The two parties held meetings continuously for two days on Monday and Tuesday, but the seat-sharing arrangement could not be finalised. The two parties will now hold talks on 26 and 27 November.

stories.title: Posted video of dog bite with caption ‘Dog biryani’:Kanpur man says he staged it to increase views
stories.summary: A young man working for a security agency in Kanpur posted a video on Facebook showing himself cutting a puppy with a sickle. After the video went viral, an animal lovers' organisation lodged a complaint with the DCP South. Following this, Govind Nagar police registered an FIR against the accused at 2 p.m. on Wednesday. He was arrested within an hour. After being apprehended, the accused began apologising with folded hands. He said, "I will not make such a mistake in the future. The puppy was not harmed. I did this only to increase views." See two pictures... Posted a 21-second video A 21-second video was posted on Facebook showing a young man placing a puppy on the sharp edge of a sickle and cutting its throat. The post was tagged 'Dog Biryani'. After the video emerged, Mayank Tripathi, founder of the organisation 'Umeed Ki Ek Kiran', lodged a complaint with DCP South Deependra Nath Chaudhary. After an investigation, police arrested Bhupendra Singh, originally from Amrahat village in Banda. DCP South said the accused was currently living in rented accommodation in I-Block, Gujaini, and worked for a security agency. He had also posted an objectionable video of a child Accused Bhupendra Singh has around 4,000 followers on Facebook. He often posts similar reels. During questioning, Bhupendra Singh told the police that he had staged the act to gain likes, views and popularity on social media. The accused said he had posted an objectionable video of a child on social media some time ago, which received 18,000 views. The video in which he pretended to bite a puppy received 50,000 views after it was posted. The accused expressed remorse over his act and said he would delete the video. South DCP Deependra Nath Chaudhary said, A case was registered against the accused at Govind Nagar police station on the complaint of Mayank Tripathi, founder of an animal welfare organisation. Action has been taken against him under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.

stories.title: Minister Sandeep showers rose petals on fiancée:Dances to Punjabi song holding her hand
stories.summary: Education Minister Sandeep Singh's haldi ceremony was held at Delhi's Leela Hotel on Wednesday. Holding his fiancée Meghna Chaudhary's hand, he made an entrance to a Punjabi song. The couple danced enthusiastically. Sandeep also showered rose petals on Meghna. Sandeep Singh was seen wearing a pastel green Nehru jacket and a cream-coloured embroidered kurta. Meghna wore an off-white embroidered lehenga. The couple danced to Punjabi singer Sukhbir's song 'Munde Bhangra Paunde Te Kudiyan Gidda Pavan'. Sandeep's younger brother, Saurabh Singh, also made a grand entrance with his fiancée, Antara Tyagi, to the song 'Welcome'. The couple will get married on Thursday. See three pictures... Father showered flowers on his sons The Haldi ceremony began at 1:30 p.m. and continued until 5 p.m. During the ceremony, singer Ishika Shengar performed songs with an orchestra. A different side of Sandeep Singh's father, former MP Rajveer Singh, also known as Raju Bhaiya, was seen at the Haldi ceremony. He knelt down to give flowers to his wife and presented them to her. The couple appeared very happy at that moment. Rajveer Singh showered flower petals on his younger son, Saurabh Singh, and his fiancée. Other family members also took part in the ceremony. Those present celebrated enthusiastically. Both brothers mounted horses after the prayers Earlier, the ghurchadhi ceremony for the two brothers was held on Tuesday at Raj Palace on Marris Road in Aligarh. At around 4 p.m., Sandeep and Saurabh mounted horses at an auspicious time after the prayers. During the ceremony, their father, former MP Rajveer Singh, also known as Raju Bhaiya, danced enthusiastically with his sons. Raj Palace was filled with celebration amid the beating of drums. Sandeep Singh and Saurabh appeared in royal style Minister Sandeep Singh appeared in royal style during the ghurchadhi ceremony. He wore a dark maroon sherwani with heavy embroidery. The sherwani featured intricate floral and vine motifs embroidered in white thread. He paired it with a pink sash, a cream-coloured turban and embroidered mojari shoes. His brother, Saurabh Singh, appeared in a light cream-coloured embroidered sherwani. He paired it with a pink sash and a border decorated with golden gota-patti work. He wore a cream-coloured turban adorned with a kalgi. Wedding will be held tomorrow at The Leela Hotel in Delhi The two brothers will get married at The Leela Hotel in Delhi on Thursday (26 November). Sandeep Singh will marry his childhood friend Meghna Chaudhary, while Saurabh Singh will marry Antra Tyagi. Earlier, the two brothers got engaged on 14 November at Talanagari in Aligarh. A venue covering around 100 bighas was prepared for the event. Several prominent leaders, including Chief Minister Yogi, and other dignitaries attended it. See two pictures from the engagement Prime Minister may also attend the wedding Prime Minister Narendra Modi may also attend the wedding in Delhi. Several VIPs and political figures are likely to attend the ceremony. The reception will then be held on 27 November at The Zora, located near Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. Sandeep Singh is the MLA from Atrauli. He is currently the Uttar Pradesh government's Minister of State for Basic Education. He is the grandson of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh and the son of former MP Rajveer Singh.

stories.title: Akhilesh targets Congress’s weak spot by announcing candidate:Who needs the alliance more? Also responds to Owaisi and Chandrashekhar
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav has announced five candidates for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections even before finalising the seat-sharing arrangement with the Congress. This is being seen as a strategy to put pressure on the Congress. By doing so, Akhilesh has attempted to achieve two objectives at once. First, he has fielded Muslim candidates ahead of the Constitution Day rally by Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar, targeting their proposed alliance. Second, he has increased pressure on the Congress by signalling that it is not the only party that needs an alliance. Read what the announcement of five candidates means… Trying to send a message that Muslims are with the SP Senior journalist Harsh Vardhan Tripathi says that, over the past few years, Muslims have increasingly begun to see Rahul Gandhi as their leader at the national level. The Assembly elections in Karnataka and Telangana are two examples of this. However, in Uttar Pradesh, Muslims continue to stand firmly with the SP. In the Lok Sabha elections, when the two parties contested together, the alliance received a consolidated Muslim vote. Akhilesh now wants to break this perception. He wants to convey that Muslims in Uttar Pradesh stand with the SP rather than the Congress, and that the SP is the party capable of defeating the BJP. Another factor is Owaisi. By fielding four Muslim candidates in its first list of five, Akhilesh has tried to send the message that the SP is the community's true well-wisher. The electoral equations in the constituencies of all four Muslim candidates announced by Akhilesh are also shaped by Dalit and Muslim voters. The Owaisi-Chandrashekhar alliance has also been formed to tap into this combination. Behat seat – SP has the sitting MLA, but Congress led in the Lok Sabha election The SP has fielded sitting MLA Umar Ali Khan from the Behat constituency. The party had been staking a claim to this seat in Saharanpur district. When the SP and Congress contested the 2017 Assembly elections together, the seat was allotted to the Congress. Naresh Saini was elected MLA in 2017. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress had a lead of 5,000 votes over the BJP in this constituency. Imran Masood went on to win the Lok Sabha seat. On this basis, the Congress was staking its claim to Behat. 36% Muslim voters – The constituency has around 3.37 lakh voters. Muslims form the largest group, with approximately 1.21 lakh voters, or 36%. Jatav voters are the second-largest group, numbering around 52,000, or 15.42%. There are also 37,000 Thakur and around 38,000 Saini voters. Kamboj and Kashyap voters together number approximately 39,000. Saharanpur Dehat – Congress had a lead of 55,000 votes in the Lok Sabha election The SP has once again placed its trust in sitting MLA Ashu Malik from the Saharanpur Dehat seat. In 2017, the Congress's Masood Akhtar had won this constituency. At the time, the SP had allotted the seat to the Congress as part of their electoral arrangement. The Congress was staking its claim to the seat this time as well. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress had a lead of 55,000 votes in this Assembly constituency. In comparison, Ashu Malik had won the seat by a margin of just 31,000 votes in 2022. One-third Muslim population – The constituency has around 3.24 lakh voters, including 1.05 lakh Muslims, the largest voter group. There are more than 90,000 Jatav voters, along with 28,000 Saini, 17,000 Thakur, 16,000 Kashyap and 15,000 Pal voters. Here too, the Dalit-Muslim equation plays a decisive role in determining the outcome. Kairana – A strong SP stronghold The SP has fielded Nahid Hasan, who has won the seat twice on the party's symbol. He is the brother of MP Iqra Hasan. The SP had also held this seat in 2017. The Hasan family has considerable influence here. Its hold among Muslim voters has helped the SP remain strong in the constituency. Muslim and Gujjar voters decide the outcome – The constituency has more than three lakh voters, around 40% of whom are Muslims. The 1.20 lakh Muslim voters are the SP's strength here. There are also 35,000 Kashyap, 30,000 Gujjar, 20,000 Saini, 20,000 Jatav and around 15,000 Jat voters. Muslim and Gujjar voters play a decisive role in determining the winner. Amroha – Congress had a lead of 85,000 votes The SP has again announced Mahboob Ali as its candidate from Amroha for 2027. He has won the seat twice consecutively. Muslims account for 66% of the voters here. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress had a lead of 85,000 votes in this constituency. However, the SP had won the Assembly seat in 2022 by a margin of around 71,000 votes. Muslims decide the outcome here too – The constituency has around 2.86 lakh voters, including 1.89 lakh Muslims. Jatav voters are the second-largest group, with around 25,000 voters, or 9%. There are also 21,000 Saini and 11,000 Jat voters. Voters from other communities number between 1,400 and 7,000. Lalitpur – Akhilesh bets on an OBC woman The BJP's Ramratan Kushwaha has won the Lalitpur seat in the last two elections. The SP has fielded Jyoti Lodhi, who contested from the constituency in 2017. She is the only woman candidate in the party's first list of five. OBC voters decide the outcome – The constituency has 3.59 lakh voters. The Ahirwar community forms the largest group, with 70,000 voters. It is counted among the Dalit communities. The constituency also has 62,000 Kushwaha, 35,000 Brahmin, 30,000 Kurmi, 50,000 Lodhi, 40,000 Sahariya tribal, 41,000 Yadav and 12,000 Muslim voters. This means the OBC communities play a decisive role in determining who becomes the MLA here. The SP wants to consolidate the Lodhi, Yadav and Muslim vote combination. Together, these three voter groups account for more than one lakh voters in the constituency. Why does the SP not want to give the Congress more seats? Senior journalist Harsh Vardhan Tripathi explains the reason. He says Akhilesh Yadav wants to break the perception that the Congress was responsible for the alliance's improved performance in 2024. The SP chief also fears that giving the Congress more seats and allowing it to win more MLAs could create political difficulties for the SP in the future. The Congress is currently on the margins in Uttar Pradesh. If it becomes stronger, the SP could lose its own core vote bank. Will the Congress-SP alliance happen or not? Senior journalist Harsh Vardhan Tripathi says Akhilesh Yadav has identified the Congress's weak spot. At one point, it seemed that Akhilesh might even give the Congress more seats to save the alliance. But he now knows that if the Congress walks away from the alliance, it will send a message across the country that the party does not really want to defeat the BJP. By announcing the list of five candidates, Akhilesh has also tried to blunt the impact of the Owaisi factor. The Owaisi factor had hurt the RJD-Congress alliance in the Seemanchal region of Bihar. The SP-Congress alliance faces a similar risk in western Uttar Pradesh. SP would be in a better position if the contest is based on caste equations Senior journalist Ratan Mani Lal says four of the five constituencies in the SP's announced list have large Muslim populations. The Jatav community, which forms part of the Dalit population, is the second-largest group in these constituencies. Akhilesh wants to consolidate the Dalit-Muslim combination. If the elections in all four constituencies are fought along caste lines, the SP would be in a better position, he says. However, if the contest takes place on the basis of communal polarisation for some reason, the SP could lose some of these seats.

stories.title: High Court cancels APO Preliminary Exam results:Directs UPPSC to prepare fresh merit list; 50,000 candidates had appeared for the exam
stories.summary: Allahabad High Court has cancelled the results of the preliminary examination for the Assistant Prosecution Officer (APO) Recruitment Exam 2025. The court has directed the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) to prepare a fresh merit list. The court said the unreserved or open category is open to candidates from all categories. If a candidate from a reserved category scores more marks than the last selected candidate in the general category, they must be considered under the open category from the preliminary examination stage itself. The commission will have to restart the subsequent selection process accordingly. Around 50,000 candidates appeared for the examination for 182 posts. Vacancies were announced on 16 September 2025 UPPSC issued the recruitment notification for 182 APO posts on 16 September 2025. These included 27 posts for the general category, 67 for Scheduled Castes (SC), 9 for Scheduled Tribes (ST), 61 for Other Backward Classes (OBC) and 18 for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). The selection process was to be completed in three stages: the preliminary examination, the main examination and, finally, an interview. Candidates numbering 15 times the total vacancies were to be declared successful in the preliminary examination and shortlisted for the main examination. Preliminary examination was held on 22 March The preliminary examination for the recruitment was conducted on 22 March 2026, with around 50,000 candidates appearing for it. The commission declared the results on 30 April 2026, announcing 2,856 candidates as successful. Some OBC candidates objected after finding their names missing from the results. They said they had not availed themselves of any relaxation, including in the age limit, and had scored more marks than the last successful candidate in the general category. Despite this, they were not placed in the open category. 321 OBC and 43 SC candidates had scored higher marks During the hearing, the commission admitted in an affidavit that 321 OBC and 43 SC candidates had scored more marks than the last selected candidate in the general category. Despite this, they were retained in their respective reserved categories. The commission had issued an office order on 9 January 2020, which stated that reserved-category candidates who appeared for the examination without availing any relaxation would be included in the general category only at the final selection stage. The petitioners challenged this rule. Both sides presented their arguments in court Petitioners' counsel Anurag Tripathi argued that the general category is not a quota reserved for any one section. Candidates from all categories can secure a place in it on the basis of merit. He said reserved-category candidates who score higher marks should be included in the open category at every stage of the examination. On behalf of the commission, senior advocate Anoop Trivedi and advocate Avnish Tripathi appeared. Additional Advocate General Manish Goyal and standing counsel Gaurav Singh represented the state government. The commission and the government argued that reservation cannot be applied at the preliminary examination stage. They also defended the commission's authority to prepare category-wise lists. They further argued that the candidates had challenged the selection process only after appearing for the examination. Court cited Supreme Court judgments Justice Manish Kumar Nigam referred to the judgments in the Indra Sawhney, RK Sabharwal, Saurav Yadav and Rajat Yadav cases. The court said the open category is open to candidates from all sections. Their merit, rather than whether they belong to a reserved or unreserved category, should determine their eligibility for a place in it. The court held that restricting reserved-category candidates who score higher marks to their respective categories at the preliminary and main examination stages is arbitrary. It violates Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution. The court also observed that the commission's policy effectively reserved 50% of the places for the general category at the initial stages of selection. However, the law provides for minimum reservation, not maximum reservation. Stay imposed on 28 September; main examination to be held afresh Following the preliminary examination, the main examination was conducted from 28 to 30 June 2026. On 28 September 2026, during the interview stage, the High Court had stayed the declaration of the results in the case. The court has now cancelled the preliminary examination results declared on 30 April 2026, along with the commission's office order dated 9 January 2020. The commission must prepare a fresh merit list for the preliminary examination under No. A-8/E-1/2025. The main examination will be conducted afresh on the basis of the revised results. The remaining recruitment process will be completed only after that.

Inspector receives grand farewell with a 51-kg garland:Was posted in Pratapgarh for 5 yrs; locals showered him with flowers
stories.summary: An inspector in Pratapgarh was given a farewell with a 51-kilogram garland. Local residents saw him off with folded hands. They continued showering him with flowers until he got into his car. Satyendra Singh, SHO of Hathigwan police station, had been posted in Pratapgarh district for the past five years. A farewell ceremony was held for him at 1 p.m. on Wednesday (25 Nov) after he was transferred to Fatehpur. He had been posted at Hathigwan police station for 13 months. See two pictures... Locals joined police personnel in showering 50 kg of flowers Police personnel wanted to make Satyendra Singh's farewell ceremony memorable. With the help of local residents and public representatives, a 51-kilogram garland and around 50 kilograms of flowers were arranged. He was first presented with the garland. Everyone then showered him with flowers before accompanying him to his car. SHO Satyendra Singh served in Pratapgarh for five years and two months. He took charge as SHO of Kandhai in October 2021. He was subsequently posted in Patti, Nagar Kotwali, Kunda and Hathigwan. He also worked as the traffic in-charge.

stories.title: 2 Bangkok gold smugglers arrested with ₹1.30 crore haul:Gorakhpur Police exposes duo after they file false robbery complaint
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Cantonment police arrested two members of a gang involved in smuggling gold from Bangkok on Wednesday. Around 960 grams of gold, valued at approximately ₹1 crore 30 lakh, was recovered from the accused. Cash worth ₹2 lakh was also recovered. The accused had filed a false report with the police about a robbery on 22 November in an attempt to seize the smuggled jewellery. An investigation into the report exposed the entire operation. The arrested accused have been identified as Ashutosh Shukla of Jharkata in the Gola police station area and Sunil Mishra of Hata Bazaar in Gagaha. After strict questioning of the accused, Cantt police registered an FIR against 10 people under serious sections on Wednesday (25 Nov). The case names both accused, Sunil Mishra and Ashutosh Shukla, along with Ajay Yadav, Deepak Tiwari, Krishnakant, Chandan Tiwari, Ayush alias Nikhil and Priyanshu Tripathi, among others. Police are conducting raids to arrest the accused who are absconding. City SP exposes gang at press conference City SP Nimish Patil briefed the media about the gang at a press conference held at 2:30 p.m. at the White House in the police lines. He said police arrested two members of the gang near Mohaddipur crossing late on Monday night. Two gold chains, a gold bangle and ₹2 lakh in cash were recovered from them. The accused had misled the police by giving false information about a robbery so that the gold could be disposed of. Interrogation revealed the entire operation During interrogation, Ashutosh Mishra and Sunil Mishra said that several people like them work for Deepak Tiwari, a resident of Mukhlispur in Bansgaon. Deepak Tiwari lives in Lucknow with his brother, Mukesh Tiwari. The gold smuggling operation is carried out through Deepak Tiwari. Ashutosh said that on 22 November 2026, he came to Gorakhpur from Lucknow via Kolkata with his associate Ajay Yadav, carrying Deepak Tiwari's gold, two chains and a bangle. They planned to go via Gorakhpur Student Union Crossing to Ghantaghar to sell the gold, but after seeing a large police presence at the crossing, he falsely informed the police that he had been robbed. The police believed their account and began investigating, during which he handed all the gold to Ajay Yadav and left the scene. Both accused said they had gone to Ghantaghar on 24 November to sell the chains and bangle. When they arrived, they found that it was Tuesday and were unable to sell the gold because the market was closed. When asked about the ₹2 lakh recovered from them, both said they had gone to Prayag Bullion Traders in Ghantaghar to sell the gold. They already knew the owner. The shop was closed, but they met him outside. After examining the gold, he gave them ₹2 lakh, which they divided equally between themselves, taking ₹1 lakh each. They said they would receive the full payment after the market reopened.

stories.title: Boys beat dog to death in Lucknow:Impaled its eye with an iron rod after it attacked a goat; dog died two days after treatment
stories.summary: Six to eight boys surrounded and brutally beat a stray dog in Lucknow after becoming angry that it had bitten a goat. The accused drove an iron rod into its eye. The seriously injured dog was taken to hospital for treatment. After battling for life for two days, the dog died. It is alleged that the dog had bitten a goat. Angered by this, the boys attacked it. Police have registered a case in connection with the incident and are searching for the accused. Beaten for biting a goat According to Deepanshu Verma, a resident of Bhikhampur, the incident took place at 11:42 am on 22 November. Six to eight boys surrounded the dog and beat it brutally. They seriously injured it by driving a metal rod into its eye. The injured dog was admitted to the Jeev Ashray Centre, where it received treatment for two days. It died at 12:19 pm on Tuesday. Police identifying suspects from video People in the neighbourhood had recorded a video of the incident, which has now emerged. Police are using the video to identify the suspects. One of the suspects is reportedly named Narayan. The identities of the other suspects are being established. Police have registered a case following a complaint from local residents. Deepanshu has demanded a fair investigation and strict action against all the accused. Inspector Mahanagar said that after registering the case, the accused were being identified.

stories.title: Meerut man accused of holding Dalit girl hostage cries:‘I made a mistake’; had threatened to never let her be with anyone else
stories.summary: A man accused of holding a 24-year-old woman hostage at a hotel in Meerut was arrested after an encounter on Wednesday. After his arrest, Salman was seen crying and apologising to police personnel. He was heard saying, “Sir, I made a mistake. Please forgive me. I won’t do it again.” Salman is a resident of Shahpur Jainpur in the Rohta police station area of Meerut. A case has been registered against him following the woman’s complaint. Earlier on Wednesday, the SSP visited Hotel Square, inspected the premises and got the hotel vacated. It was subsequently sealed. How was Salman arrested? SSP BBGTS Murthy said a complaint had been received at Sadar Bazaar police station alleging that a man named Salman had held a Dalit woman hostage and sexually assaulted her. Based on the complaint, a case was registered under the relevant sections and legal proceedings were initiated. He said police received information on Wednesday that the accused was hiding near an under-construction underpass close to Nahar Narhera village in the Lohia Nagar police station area. Teams from Lohia Nagar and Sadar Bazaar police stations reached the spot and cordoned off the area. According to police, the accused opened fire at the police team after finding himself surrounded. When the police tried to catch him, he climbed onto a nearby bridge and attempted to flee. During the chase, he slipped and fell from the bridge. Both his hands were injured. He was taken to hospital for treatment. See three pictures related to the hotel incident Girl ran out of hotel screaming for help It was around 1.30 pm on Tuesday. A girl ran out of Hotel Square in the Abu Lane market in the Sadar Bazaar area, shouting for help. A young man came running after her, grabbed her by the hair, lifted her in his arms and tried to take her back inside the hotel. Hearing her screams, people nearby rushed to the spot. Seeing the crowd, the accused left her and ran inside the hotel. People tried to catch him, but hotel employees stopped them. A commotion continued for quite some time. Meanwhile, the accused managed to escape from the hotel's third-floor terrace. According to police, the man had held the girl hostage inside the hotel and threatened her with a knife. He would tell her, “If you cannot be mine, I won't let you be anyone else's either. I will kill you.” After receiving information, police reached the spot and took the woman to the police station. The accused, Salman, is married. Girl worked with Salman at a company According to police, the girl, a resident of Ghaziabad, met Salman, who belongs to the Kankarkhera police station area of Meerut, around a year ago. Both worked at a private company. They started talking and gradually began meeting each other. Recently, the girl's marriage was fixed. She then quit her job, and the two stopped meeting. Salman tried several times to meet her, but she refused. Around two days ago, the girl came to Meerut to visit a friend. Salman learnt about this. On the pretext of helping her find a job, he called her and took her to Hotel Square, where he locked her inside a room. Eyewitness says hotel employees helped the accused escape Eyewitness Aman said the girl came out of the hotel in a distressed condition. Her clothes were dishevelled, and she was screaming for help. A man named Salman was with her and was trying to forcibly take her away. When they rushed to the spot, the accused left her and ran inside the hotel. Hotel employees stopped people from entering Aman said they ran inside the hotel to catch the accused, but the employees stopped them. They said they would bring him downstairs themselves. Meanwhile, the accused jumped from the third-floor terrace onto a neighbouring house and escaped. Two people chased him, but could not catch him. The hotel employees then shut the rear door. Later, when they questioned the woman, she told them that Salman had kept her locked in a hotel room throughout the night and had not allowed her to leave. He had also threatened her with a knife. They then informed the police. Police seal hotel SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosale said a case had been registered based on the woman's complaint. On Wednesday morning, the SSP visited the hotel, inspected the premises and got it vacated. Hotel Square was then sealed. SSP BBGTS Murthy said the hotel was sealed primarily to preserve evidence at the crime scene. This would prevent anyone from tampering with the evidence until the investigation was completed. Hindutva leader demands encounter Sachin Sirohi, national president of the All India Hindu Suraksha Sangathan, demanded a ‘half encounter’ of the accused. He said the SSP himself had confirmed that Salman had opened fire at the police. Despite this, no ‘half encounter’ was carried out. He alleged that the police took pity on Salman after he sustained injuries to his hands and legs. He called the police action condemnable and said the police had failed to teach such an accused a lesson.

stories.title: Yogi says SP’s downfall is near:Takes a dig at ‘two boys’, says SP-Congress alliance has failed even before the elections
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took a dig on Wednesday at the tussle between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress over seat-sharing. He said, "The pairing of the two boys used to fail after the election results were announced, but this time it has already failed before the election." Yogi said that while meetings were being held between the two parties over seats, candidates were being announced on the other side. "What could be a greater insult than this?" he asked. A political contest to outwit one another is under way between the two parties. The condition of Congress, the country's oldest political party, is the result of its negative thinking. The people are repeatedly rejecting these parties. The Chief Minister was speaking at the ABP Conclave. He accused the SP of practising dynastic politics and not respecting the sentiments of Ram devotees. He said, "'Radhe-Radhe' is only the beginning; the time for 'Ram naam satya' is drawing near for the SP." Yogi says SP should apologise to Ram devotees On Akhilesh's visit to Ayodhya and questions related to Sanatan Dharma, Chief Minister Yogi said that riding two boats was always dangerous. He said visiting Ayodhya was a good thing, but the Samajwadi Party should also apologise to Ram devotees. He said that if this good sense had prevailed in the 1990s, there would have been no need to open fire on Ram devotees. Rejecting speculation about differences among the NDA's alliance partners, the Chief Minister made it clear that all the allies, including the Nishad Party and the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, were united and would contest the elections together. PDA described as 'Parivar Development Authority' The Chief Minister took a swipe at the Samajwadi Party's PDA slogan, describing it as the "Parivar Development Authority". He alleged that the party's politics is limited to its own family. 'Strict action against those challenging the law will continue' Responding to the Opposition's allegations concerning bulldozer action and encounters, the Chief Minister said that women's safety and respect for traders were the government's top priorities. Strict action against those challenging the law will continue. On the possibility of sitting legislators being denied tickets, he said that in the BJP, the parliamentary board takes the final decision after the election committee's recommendation, and that the party works to bring people together. He described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as the BJP's universally accepted leader and ideal, as well as a symbol of India's global stature. Responding to a question about the chief ministerial face, he said that the lotus symbol was supreme for the BJP. CM hits back at Akhilesh's 'Infiltrator' remark During the programme's rapid-fire round, the Chief Minister responded to various words. He described India as the 'World Spiritual Powerhouse', Uttar Pradesh as having 'Unlimited Potential', Lord Ram as the 'embodiment of dharma' and the BJP as 'Nation First'. The CM compared Rahul Gandhi to a rocket that is launched but fails to take off successfully. Asked about performing his mother's last rites on the day she died and receiving Prime Minister Modi, he said, "This is the duty of an ascetic." Hitting back at Akhilesh Yadav's 'infiltrator' remark, the Chief Minister said that he is a resident of undivided Uttar Pradesh and has been serving in Gorakhpur since 1992 under the Nath sect's tradition. Speaking in the context of Uttarakhand, he said that the waters of the Ganga, Yamuna and Saryu originate in Devbhoomi Uttarakhand. The state's soldiers protect the country's borders, and therefore there should be a sense of gratitude towards Uttarakhand. He said he did not need any certificate for his ascetic faith or identity. Claim that Uttar Pradesh's economy has grown threefold Yogi claimed that Uttar Pradesh had transformed from a 'BIMARU' state into an engine of development. Since 2017, the state's economy, per capita income and budget have grown more than threefold. He said that the state previously had factories manufacturing illegal country-made pistols and bombs, but now revolvers, rifles and BrahMos missiles are being manufactured. The state has received investment proposals worth ₹50 lakh crore, and 36 sector-based policies have been formulated to attract investment. According to the chief minister, Uttar Pradesh accounts for 55% of the country's mobile phone production and 60% of electronic component production. The MSME and ODOP schemes are providing employment to 3.25 crore people. He said that housing-related disputes involving 4 lakh homebuyers had been resolved through dialogue between builders and buyers. Target of 10.5 lakh appointments Yogi said that around 9.75 lakh appointment letters had already been issued to young people. The government's target is to raise this figure to 10.5 lakh by 26 January. Warning that the safety of women, traders and investors would be ensured, he said that those who cast an evil eye on daughters, traders and women walking on the streets had only two places to go-jail or hell. Speaking about the political leadership and the BJP's preparations for the election, the Chief Minister named Prime Minister Narendra Modi as his role model. He said he was an ordinary party worker and would fulfil whatever responsibility was assigned to him.

stories.title: Mock aircraft crash alert at Lucknow airport:250 personnel lead rescue operation as passengers are evacuated amid flames
stories.summary: A rescue and relief exercise simulating an aircraft accident was conducted at Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport in Lucknow on Wednesday. A crash scene was created after a simulated landing failure. As soon as the alert was sounded, fire engines, ambulances and rescue teams reached the site. The exercise covered everything from extinguishing the fire to evacuating passengers. Around 250 officers and employees took part. During the full-scale Aerodrome Emergency Exercise 'Sahas-2026' held at the airport, various agencies jointly assessed their preparedness to deal with an emergency. The exercise was conducted from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. See 4 pictures... Crash scene recreated after simulated landing failure A crash scenario was created during the exercise after the aircraft's landing failed. As soon as the information was received, air traffic control, the firefighting team, CISF and the medical team became active. Firefighters extinguished the blaze. The rescue team practised evacuating passengers from the aircraft. The process of taking the injured to hospital by ambulance was also tested. 250 personnel took charge Airport administration, CISF, NDRF, SDRF, Uttar Pradesh Police, the Fire Department, district administration and medical teams took part in the exercise. Personnel from the Sarojini Nagar Fire Station, Dial-112 and Air Force Station Bakshi Ka Talab also participated. Medical teams from Chandan Hospital and OP Chaudhary Hospital were present. Fire tenders, ambulances, rescue vehicles and modern firefighting equipment were used. Their deployment was used to assess the availability of resources during an emergency and coordination among the agencies. Preparedness assessed against international standards 'Sahas-2026' was conducted in accordance with ICAO and DGCA standards. The exercise reviewed the emergency response plan, communication systems, crisis management and rescue operations. It also assessed how quickly all agencies could respond together in the event of an accident. Exercise conducted after NOTAM issued, flights remain normal The airport administration had issued a NOTAM in advance for the exercise. A mock drill was conducted at the scheduled time. Regular air operations were not affected. Flights continued to operate normally during the exercise, and passengers faced no inconvenience.

stories.title: Mother daughter murdered in Ghazipur:Bodies found inside house with throats slit, gate locked from outside
stories.summary: The bodies of a 35-year-old woman and her eight-year-old daughter were found inside their house in Ghazipur at around 8 am on Wednesday. Both had been killed with a sharp weapon. The mother and daughter were alone at home at the time of the incident, and the main gate was locked from outside. The deceased were identified as Jaymoon Nisha (35) and her daughter, Aiman Nisha (8). After receiving information about the double murder, police reached the spot and began an investigation. The incident took place in Dharwan village, under the Nandganj police station area, about 25 km from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures... Read the full case... Mohammad Anirullah, the brother of Qasimabad resident Zaibun Nisha, said he had called his sister on Tuesday, but her mobile phone was switched off. When he contacted neighbours on Wednesday morning, he was informed that the house was locked. He then sent his sisters, Zubeida Khatun and Shabana Khatun, to the spot. They broke open the lock and found Zaibun Nisha's blood-soaked body lying on the floor inside. Her daughter's body was found lying on the bed. Both had marks on their necks caused by blows from a sharp weapon. Dispute over demand to rent land Anirullah has accused Parvez alias Sonu, a resident of the village, of the murders. He said the accused had threatened his sister in the past as well. He had been asking the family to rent out land to him, which had led to an ongoing dispute. According to the brother, a complaint had been lodged earlier over the threats, but a settlement was reached later. Despite this, the threats continued. The family suspects that the murders were committed due to this enmity. Her brother said that Jaibun Nisha's husband, Gulfaam, is a resident of Meerut and that the couple had separated eight years ago. Jaibun Nisha had built a house in Nandganj and lived there with her eight-year-old daughter. SP reaches the scene and conducts investigation Superintendent of Police Vinay Kumar Singh reached the scene after receiving information about the double murder. He inspected the site and spoke to the family members. The SP said the family members had accused an acquaintance of carrying out the crime. The police are investigating the case from all angles. Evidence is being collected from the scene, and steps are being taken to send both bodies for post-mortem examinations. The SP has said that the incident will be solved soon.

stories.title: SC quashes CBI, ED probe order in Rahul’s assets case:Sends matter back to Allahabad HC, directs it to make Gandhi a party
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside an Allahabad High Court order directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to probe allegations of disproportionate assets against Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, Bar and Bench reported. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana sent the matter back to the High Court for fresh consideration. It also directed the High Court to make Gandhi a party to the case and give him an opportunity to be heard before passing any orders. High Court had ordered CBI, ED to verify allegations In May, the Allahabad High Court directed the CBI and ED to verify claims made by BJP worker S Vignesh Shishir, who had sought an investigation against Gandhi and other members of his family. The High Court later asked the CBI to file a fresh affidavit detailing the progress of its inquiry. On July 20, a Bench of Justice Brij Raj Singh and Justice Rajesh Singh Chauhan expressed dissatisfaction with the agency's response, saying it did not adequately explain the investigation's progress. The Bench also observed that the ED had taken the required steps and could proceed further if the investigation revealed material warranting action. Gandhi challenged High Court directions in Supreme Court Gandhi challenged the High Court's directions before the Supreme Court. He argued that Shishir had no locus standi to file the petition and had not disclosed his credentials. Gandhi also questioned how confidential proceedings in the matter had been reported in newspapers. On August 17, the Supreme Court flagged that the High Court had passed orders without hearing Gandhi. It directed the High Court to defer the proceedings and questioned why the Congress leader had not been given an opportunity to present his side. The Supreme Court has now set aside the High Court orders and remanded the matter for a fresh hearing. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal appeared for Gandhi. Separate case alleges Gandhi holds British passport In a separate petition pending before the Allahabad High Court, Shishir has sought criminal action against Gandhi, alleging violations of citizenship laws. He has claimed that the Congress leader holds a British passport in addition to his Indian passport. The High Court had initially ordered the registration of an FIR against Gandhi in the case. However, the judge later withheld the order and recused himself after Shishir made certain social media posts related to the matter. The case remains pending before the High Court.

stories.title: UP transfers 10 IPS officers, including 6 women:Mavis Talk shifted to Lucknow; 18 additional SPs also transferred
stories.summary: Major police reshuffle in UP ahead of Assembly elections: 10 IPS, 18 Additional SPs transferred; several women officers among those moved A major reshuffle has taken place in the Uttar Pradesh Police ahead of the Assembly elections. The government has transferred 10 IPS officers and 18 Additional Superintendents of Police (ASP). Officers from several police commissionerates have also been moved. Of the 10 IPS officers, six are women, while five of the 18 Additional SPs are women. Puneet Dwivedi, who was awaiting posting, has been appointed ACP in the Lucknow Police Commissionerate. Neetu has been transferred from Varanasi to the Noida Police Commissionerate. Shiva Singh has been moved from Kanpur to Agra, Amit Kumawat from Lucknow to Ghaziabad, and Kiran Yadav has been shifted to the Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) headquarters in Lucknow. Pushkar Verma has been transferred from Prayagraj to Fatehgarh, Aditya from Agra to Badaun, Shaivya Goyal from Noida to Ghaziabad, Bhavre Diksha Arun from Shahjahanpur to Meerut, and Mavis Talk from Sonbhadra to Lucknow. The IPS officers transferred include Additional SP- and Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police-rank officers from the 2020, 2021 and 2022 batches. Mamta Kuril transferred from Aligarh to Muzaffarnagar The list of 18 Additional SP transfers includes Kumar Ranvijay Singh, Additional SP (City), Moradabad, who has been appointed Additional SP (Rural), Azamgarh. ASP Anoop Kumar has been transferred from Mau to Sonbhadra. Devendra Singh-1, who was serving as Deputy Commandant of the PAC in Mirzapur, has been appointed Additional SP (Rural), Shahjahanpur. Indu Prabha Singh has been appointed Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police in Lucknow. She had earlier been transferred to the Kanpur Nagar Police Commissionerate. Mamta Kuril has been transferred from the post of ASP (Crime), Aligarh, to ASP (Traffic), Muzaffarnagar.

stories.summary: Bageshwar Dham Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri visited the Chief Minister's residence today, where he met Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. According to sources, the meeting included detailed discussions on the religious discourses proposed in Lucknow and various other districts of Uttar Pradesh in the coming days, the recent Ramdev controversy and the political equations linked to the 2027 assembly election. Discussion held on bringing the Ramdev controversy to an end Reports of a war of words between yoga guru Swami Ramdev and Dhirendra Shastri had recently emerged over remarks related to Lord Ram and Lord Krishna. Swami Ramdev had expressed strong displeasure over comparisons involving the Sanatan tradition, superstition and deities. However, both saints have chosen not to escalate the dispute. Dhirendra Shastri made it clear that he does not hit back at saints and considers Swami Ramdev his senior and a guardian figure; according to him, criticism is also akin to a blessing. Swami Ramdev also clarified that he had used harsh words in the heat of the moment, but the matter was resolved after they spoke. stories.title: Yogi to inaugurate Kashi Tamil Sangamam on November 28:1,400 delegates will reach Namo Ghat in 7 groups
stories.summary: The fifth edition of the Kashi Tamil Sangamam, which connects the cultural heritage of North and South India, will begin in Kashi on 28 November. The event, which will continue until 12 December, will be inaugurated by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Organised by the Union Ministry of Education, the main ceremony will be held at Namo Ghat. This time, around 1,400 representatives from Tamil Nadu will arrive in Kashi in seven groups. This year's theme is 'Tirukkural Pailavom', meaning 'Let us practise Tirukkural'. Through the theme, the teachings related to ethics, morality and the values of life in Tirukkural, the famous classical work of Tamil literature, will be conveyed to students and young people across the country. 1,400 representatives to arrive in seven groups Representatives from Tamil Nadu have been divided into seven groups: students, teachers, writers and media professionals, people associated with the agricultural sector, professionals and artisans, women, and spiritual leaders. Each group will have around 200 participants. During the eight-day visit, the representatives will also travel to Prayagraj and Ayodhya, along with Kashi. They will visit religious, cultural and historical sites there. Students from 1,000 educational institutions will also join This time, students from 1,000 higher educational institutions across the country will also be included in the event. Students interested in the Tirukkural will be selected from each institution on the basis of merit. The selected students will receive online training in the 22 scheduled languages and English. This will be followed by a month of research and academic activities. Students will have to prepare a four- to 10-page article or research note on the Tirukkural. They will also have to give a one-hour presentation at their institution. Eligible students who fulfil the prescribed conditions will be awarded a scholarship of ₹10,000. They will experience Kashi's religious and Tamil heritage During their stay in Kashi, the representatives will visit major religious and historical sites, including the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Sarnath, BHU, Ramnagar Fort and Bharat Mata Temple. The programme will also include the Ganga Aarti, a dip in the Ganga, academic discussions and cultural events. Sites associated with Tamil heritage have also been given a special place in the itinerary. The delegates will visit the ancestral home of poet Subramania Bharati, Kedar Ghat and Kashi Math, known as 'Little Tamil Nadu'. An academic interaction will be held at the Tamil Department of Banaras Hindu University. The delegates will then visit the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj and the Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya.

stories.title: Imran Masood warns, 'We won't be trampled underfoot':Says, 'Rahul's 'magic' helped Akhilesh win 37 seats, otherwise parties got just 5 each'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Congress working president Imran Masood is extremely unhappy with Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. After the Samajwadi Party (SP) announced candidates for five seats, Masood openly criticised the party. In a warning tone, he said, We are ready to make every possible compromise for the alliance, but we won't be trampled underfoot. Masood also said it was Rahul Gandhi's “miracle” that Akhilesh won 37 seats in 2024. Otherwise, he said, the SP had won only five seats each when it contested elections in an alliance in 2019 and 2014. Without naming him directly, Masood also targeted Akhilesh Yadav. He said Rahul Gandhi was the only guarantee of defeating the BJP and that no one else in the country could defeat the party. Read the exclusive interview… Q: What do you have to say about the SP announcing five candidates while seat-sharing talks are still underway? Imran Masood: It is their decision. It is their party, and they are free to make decisions for it. They can release the list in whichever way they want. What can I say about that? But when it comes to an alliance, things cannot work like this. You say one thing during discussions and do something else. That is not right. Q: The SP has given a ticket to one of its sitting MLAs. What is wrong with that? Imran Masood: Why are they sitting MLAs? I joined you in 2022 with two MLAs, and both were sitting MLAs. I held discussions based on your promises and helped you win both seats. After that, what happened during my own election does not need to be explained. Despite everything, I won those two seats by margins of 40,000 and 47,000 votes. If we are talking about strengthening the alliance, then it should function like an alliance. You simply said that you would start with 26 seats. We did not even ask you for seats. Are we beggars? Will you now decide on your own where we should contest? We are not here to let you make all the decisions for us. Q: Will the talks remain stalled or reach a conclusion? Imran Masood: I don't know. Look, there should be seriousness in every matter. Talks on the alliance were underway in Delhi. What were those discussions about? We held marathon meetings for two days. Why did we do all that? If you want to announce candidates like this, you might as well announce them for all 403 seats. What difference does it make? Q: Akhilesh Yadav says this is the first list of 26 candidates. Imran Masood: We did not ask you for 26 seats. Why are you announcing them? We never asked you to give us these 26 seats. We did not give you any list. If you are announcing your own list, then select candidates from it. When did we give you these seats that you have announced them? Q: What will be your stand on the two Saharanpur seats where the SP has fielded candidates? Imran Masood: I will work according to whatever my party tells me. But we have to protect our identity and our party. We have repeatedly said that we are ready for every possible compromise. But that does not mean you can crush us. That is not acceptable. Q: It has been said that you will field candidates on all seven seats in Saharanpur. Imran Masood: I have not said anything like that so far. But let me ask you something. In 2022, there was a lot of talk about forming the government. People kept saying the government was being formed. We were also drawn into the alliance. The SBSP joined, along with several other parties. The Rashtriya Lok Dal was also there. Yet, you could not go beyond 111 seats. It was Rahul Gandhi's miracle that you reached 43 seats. That alliance was Rahul Gandhi's. Otherwise, there was an alliance in 2019 as well. The SP and BSP had contested together. Where did you stand then? You could win only five seats. You won only five in 2014 as well. If we assess all these things, you cannot claim that we do not have people capable of working on the ground. In this country, Rahul Gandhi is the only guarantee of defeating the BJP. There is no other guarantee in the country from anyone who can claim to defeat the BJP. Q: What do you think is the future of the alliance? Imran Masood: I don't know what its future will be. I am not an astrologer who can predict the future. I simply don't know what will happen. Q: Will your next scheduled meeting take place after this decision by the SP? Imran Masood: What is the point of holding those meetings? The meeting will take place in Delhi, while the list will be announced from Lucknow. We did not even discuss the matter in the meeting, and you will simply announce a list and say that you have given us 26 seats. What does that mean? You were giving 35 seats to the RLD. This kind of behaviour is deeply insulting. Q: Is this your personal anger or the Congress's anger? Imran Masood: What am I? I am the Congress. This is an insult to the party and its workers. What do you mean by 26 seats? We are not asking you for seats. You want to give us all the seats you have lost and then tell us that our strike rate is not good. Well, we are not going to function according to your wishes.

stories.title: Men clash after car collision in Lucknow:Youth beaten with kicks, punches and slippers; bleeds from face
stories.summary: A minor collision between two cars on Khurram Nagar Road in Lucknow led to a physical fight on Tuesday afternoon. Near the Indira Nagar Sector-17 market, the people travelling in both cars got out onto the road and clashed with each other. During the fight, a young man was surrounded and beaten with slippers, kicks and punches. A video of the incident has surfaced. According to an eyewitness, the young man was bleeding after the assault. According to information, two young men were travelling in the Ciaz car, while a young man and an elderly person were in the Swift Dzire. An argument began after the two cars collided. The dispute soon turned into a physical fight. In the video, some people can be seen surrounding and beating the Dzire passenger wearing a Nehru jacket. Passer-by recorded the video A crowd gathered on the road during the assault. Meanwhile, a passer-by recorded the incident. The video shows several people hitting the young man with slippers, kicks and punches. "Uttar Pradesh Government" was written on the Ciaz car.

stories.title: Suresh Gautam appointed new BSP district president:Party changes 6 district presidents in 11 months in Gorakhpur, some lasted just 7 days, others 100
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) has repeatedly changed its district president. In the past 11 months, the party has entrusted six leaders with this responsibility. It has now changed the district president once again and handed the reins to a new face. Jaikaar Prasad, who was appointed district president on 17 August, has been removed from the post and given responsibility as divisional co-ordinator. Suresh Kumar Gautam has been appointed the new district president in his place. The appointment order was issued on the night of 24 November. Suresh Kumar Gautam has previously served as district president. He has also been responsible for four districts as the chief divisional co-ordinator. He is considered a senior leader in the party. The repeated changes have also left workers confused. Some removed after seven days, others after 100 days Gorakhpur has been a strong political base for the BSP in eastern Uttar Pradesh. However, for some time now, the party has been unable to settle on stable leadership for its organisation here. The repeated changes of district president are creating a situation of instability within the organisation. On 20 January, Ghanshyam Rahi, who had previously served as district president twice, was given the responsibility for a third time. But just seven days later, he was removed and Hari Prakash Nishad was appointed district president. On 12 June, Santosh Kumar Jigyasu was given the responsibility in place of Hari Prakash Nishad. Within two months, Santosh Kumar Jigyasu was appointed chief mandal coordinator. On 4 August, Rishi Kapoor was made district president for the second time, but he was removed on 17 August and Jaikar Prasad was handed the reins. Now, around 100 days later, Jaikar Prasad has also been removed. First, know when and to whom the responsibility of district president was given Jigyasu became district president immediately after returning from expulsion Santosh Kumar Jigyasu was the Bahujan Samaj Party's district president during the 2022 Assembly elections. He was also holding the same responsibility during the 2023 municipal elections. He was expelled from the party for allegedly campaigning against the party's candidate in Ghaghasra Nagar Panchayat. He returned to the party on 12 June 2026. He was appointed district president on the same day. However, around two months later, he was given the responsibility of chief divisional coordinator. Experts say: Repeated changes are affecting the organisation Senior journalist DBB Mishra said district presidents are not changed so frequently in any political party. In the Bahujan Samaj Party, the same old faces are repeatedly being given a chance. The district president is the organisation's highest-ranking post in a district. Appointments to the post should be made after careful consideration. According to him, changing district presidents six times in 11 months points to immature decision-making. Such changes close to elections could affect the organisation. Traditionally, the BSP has appointed district presidents from the Dalit community. A district president should be given a tenure of at least two years to strengthen the organisation. Who is Suresh Kumar Gautam, the BSP's new district president? Suresh Kumar Gautam is a long-time BSP worker. He had also served as district president before 2007. In addition, he has been responsible for four districts as the chief divisional coordinator. He is a resident of Sisai village in the Pali block of the Sahjanwa Assembly constituency. His village lies on the border of the Sahjanwa and Campierganj Assembly constituencies. Suresh Gautam says he will work with party workers to bring the BSP to power. Learn about the leaders appointed as district presidents... Ghanshyam Rahi Ghanshyam Rahi, who belongs to the Scheduled Caste category, has been associated with the Bahujan Samaj Party for a long time. He has served as a councillor of the Pipraich Nagar Panchayat and has also held the responsibility of zonal coordinator. He was appointed district president three times. His third term lasted only seven days. He is currently overseeing the party's work in Gorakhpur district as divisional in-charge. Hari Prakash Nishad Hari Prakash Nishad, a resident of the Pipraich Assembly constituency, has been involved in student politics. He has also served as a district panchayat member. In the Bahujan Samaj Party, he has held the responsibilities of zonal coordinator, chief zonal coordinator and chief divisional in-charge. He is currently overseeing the work of the Backward Classes Bhaichara Committee. Santosh Kumar Jigyasu He is a resident of Ghaghsara Nagar Panchayat in the Sahjanwa area. He was expelled for campaigning against the party candidate in the 2023 municipal elections. He was appointed district president upon his return to the party on 12 June. Rishi Kapoor Rishi Kapoor is originally from Gorakhpur. He began his political career in student politics, after which he joined the BSP. He has remained with the BSP ever since and was appointed district president in 2023. The 2024 Lok Sabha election was held under his supervision. He was given the responsibility of district president for a second term on 4 August, but his responsibility was changed 13 days later. Jaikar Prasad Thirty-nine-year-old Jaikar Prasad is originally from Madaई Tola in Bansgaon block. He has been active in the BSP since 2007. He began his political journey as a booth president. After this, he took charge as the sector in-charge, assembly constituency in-charge, assembly general secretary and district in-charge. He was appointed district president on 17 August. He was removed around 100 days later. Suresh Kumar Gautam Suresh Kumar Gautam has been appointed the new district president. He is a long-time BSP worker. He had served as district president before 2007. As the chief divisional coordinator, he has been responsible for four districts. He is a resident of Pali block in the Sahjanwa Assembly constituency. His village, Sisai, lies on the border of the Sahjanwa and Campierganj Assembly constituencies. He said he would work with party workers to bring the BSP to power.

stories.title: Pratapnagar-Barauni special train to run from today:Train to pass through Gorakhpur with 19 coaches as railways respond to post-Chhath rush
stories.summary: The Railways has decided to run an additional festival special train between Pratapnagar and Barauni to manage the rush of passengers after the Chhath festival in Gorakhpur. Train number 09159, the Pratapnagar-Barauni Festival Special, will operate as a one-way service on November 25. It will pass through Gorakhpur. The train is expected to provide relief to passengers travelling across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. According to the Railways, the train will depart from Pratapnagar at 11:50 pm. The next day, Thursday, it will reach Vadodara at 12:10 am, Godhra at 2:47 am, Ratlam at 7 am, Nagda at 7:50 am, Kota at 10:45 am, Sawai Madhopur at 12:12 pm and Gangapur City at 1 pm. It will then reach Idgah Agra at 4:25 pm, Tundla at 5:35 pm and Kanpur Central at 11 pm. Continuing its journey, the train will reach Aishbagh at 12:58 am on Friday, Barabanki at 2:25 am, Gonda at 3:40 am and Basti at 4:55 am. Train to reach Gorakhpur at 6:55 am The train will arrive in Gorakhpur at 6:55 am on Friday. From there, it will reach Narkatiaganj at 11:35 am, Muzaffarpur at 4:35 pm and Samastipur at 5:45 pm. It will finally reach Barauni at 8 pm. The journey from Pratapnagar to Barauni will take more than two days. Train to have 19 coaches The special train will have a total of 19 coaches, including 10 sleeper coaches, one general second-class sitting coach, six general coaches and two SLRD coaches. This will provide more travel options for passengers travelling with sleeper and general tickets. The Railways said the special train was being introduced in view of the additional rush of passengers after the Chhath festival. It will make travel easier for passengers at major stations along the route.

stories.title: Imran Masood praises Mayawati, says she can turn things around:‘She just needs to step out’; responds to possibility of an alliance with BSP
stories.summary: Congress MP Imran Masood has expressed anger over the Samajwadi Party's first list of candidates for the UP Assembly elections. He said, "We are not beggars waiting to get something from Akhilesh. You announced candidates without discussing it with us, so why are we even holding talks?" Speaking at a TV channel's programme, he also praised Mayawati. Imran Masood said: "If Behenji (Mayawati) steps out of her room, the political picture of the state will change completely." When asked whether Congress would form an alliance with the BSP, he said the decision rested with Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, not him. He added that a mission and movement had lost momentum simply because Behenji remained confined to her room. There was no doubt that she was a major political leader in Uttar Pradesh, but he did not know what had happened to her after 2012. She had shut herself inside her room to such an extent that she no longer stepped outside. The seat-sharing deadlock between the two parties has been intensifying. Against Congress's demand for 125 seats, the SP submitted a list of just 26 constituencies. Moreover, before further discussions could take place, the SP released its first list of five candidates at 10 pm on Tuesday. It included two seats in Saharanpur that Congress had also claimed. Earlier, Akhilesh had written on X: "We have started with the first 26 winnable seats. Talks will move forward through mutual understanding and cooperation." The two parties held consecutive meetings on Monday and Tuesday, but failed to finalise the seat-sharing arrangement. The next round of talks is scheduled for November 26-27.
