stories.title: Pollution rises as Kashi turns colder, mercury at 19°C:AQI crosses 100 at all four stations after Dev Deepawali, with Maldahiya recording highest pollution
stories.summary: The weather has started changing in Varanasi, with falling temperatures bringing colder conditions. At the same time, rising air pollution has become a concern. The city's minimum temperature was recorded at 19°C on Wednesday morning. Winds blew at 5 kmph, while humidity stood at 60%. The city's Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 264, falling in the poor category. According to meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh, temperatures are likely to continue falling over the coming days. Haze may increase during mornings and nights over the next week, making the cold more intense. However, sunshine during the day may provide some relief. AQI crosses 100 at all four monitoring stations after Dev Deepawali Air quality in Kashi was affected by the lamps and fireworks during Dev Deepawali celebrations. AQI readings crossed 100 at all four air quality monitoring stations in the city. Maldahiya recorded the highest AQI at 153, followed by Bhelupur at 149, BHU at 139 and Ardali Bazar at 119. Air quality was satisfactory on November 22, pollution rose the next day According to data from the Sameer app, Varanasi recorded an AQI of 54 on November 22. For the first time in November, air quality had reached the satisfactory category. However, pollution levels rose again the very next day. Data from previous years also shows a recurring rise in pollution around Dev Deepawali. The AQI was recorded at 97 in 2023, 155 in 2024 and 128 in 2025. This year's post-festival rise in pollution has once again raised concerns over air quality in the city.

On this auspicious occasion, the Ganga Seva Nidhi organised a special Maha Aarti at the world-famous Dashashwamedh Ghat. As evening set in, 21 priests performed the grand aarti of the River Ganga together amid Vedic chants and the sound of conch shells. Lakhs of devotees and domestic and international tourists gathered at the ghat and were mesmerised by the spectacle. The entire ghat was decorated like a bride with thousands of earthen lamps and colourful lights. Chants of 'Har Har Mahadev' filled the city with a devotional atmosphere. stories.title: 2,000 guests to attend Rinku Singh-Priya Saroj wedding in Lucknow:PM Modi invited; Akhilesh, Rahul among VVIPs; functions at Ramada hotel
stories.summary: Cricketer Rinku Singh and Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj will get married on December 4 at Hotel Ramada in Lucknow. Around 2,000 guests from across the country have been invited. The list of VVIP guests includes Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, former Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and MP Priyanka Gandhi. Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan has also been invited. Members of both families will arrive at the hotel on December 3. All wedding functions, including the mehendi ceremony and other rituals and pujas, will be held at the venue. Priya Saroj will wear jewellery sourced from her local market in Pindra for the jaimala ceremony. She will also wear artificial jewellery to complement her lehenga. See three pictures... SP chief Akhilesh Yadav likely to attend with family SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has been invited by Priya Saroj and is expected to attend with his family, including his wife Dimple Yadav, daughters and son. Priya Saroj also invited Rahul Gandhi through Priyanka Gandhi. Rinku Singh personally handed invitation cards to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Invitations sent to 90 MPs and MLAs Apart from them, around 8–10 Union ministers and nearly 90 MPs and MLAs have been invited by Priya Saroj and her father, Tufani Saroj. Those invited include Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari, Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Kamlesh Paswan. Congress Rajya Sabha MP Rajeev Shukla is also expected to attend. UP leaders and young cricketers to attend Rinku's fellow cricketers will also start arriving from December 3. They include Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Tilak Varma, Suresh Raina, Praveen Kumar, RP Singh, Piyush Chawla and Kuldeep Yadav, among others. Bhojpuri artists, including Samar Singh, are also expected to attend. Arrangements have been made for around 2,000 guests in total. Famous Banarasi sarees purchased for Priya The wedding menu will be entirely vegetarian, with arrangements ranging from soups to desserts. Priya Saroj is getting her clothing collection from New Delhi, while some shopping has also been done in Lucknow. Famous Banarasi sarees have been purchased from Varanasi. The jewellery has been sourced from Pindra's local market, PC Jewellers in Delhi and Mohammed Zubair in Varanasi.

stories.title: Mercury dips to 9.5°C in UP, Hardoi coldest:Muzaffarnagar also shivers as nights and mornings set to get colder
stories.summary: Cold conditions have intensified in Uttar Pradesh due to snowfall in the hills. The mercury has dropped below 10°C. Over the past 24 hours, Hardoi recorded the lowest temperature at 9.5°C, followed by Muzaffarnagar at 9.8°C. On Tuesday morning, dense fog covered 15 cities, including Lakhimpur, Sitapur, Ballia, Sambhal, Bijnor and Muzaffarnagar. Visibility in Lakhimpur dropped so much that objects beyond 25 metres could not be seen on the roads. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said that wind patterns have changed after the impact of the cyclone originating in the Bay of Bengal subsided. Westerly winds are now gaining strength. As a result, minimum temperatures may drop by 3–5°C over the next week. This will make nights and early mornings colder. According to Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, Temperatures are falling due to cold and dry winds. Fog has also increased. However, clear skies are allowing good sunshine during the day. But the mercury drops rapidly after sunset. Light rainfall is possible at isolated places tomorrow. Farmers advised to take precautions while sowing and irrigating Rabi crops With the possibility of rainfall in November, farmers have been advised to remain cautious while managing Rabi crops. In particular, those sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard in eastern UP should ensure proper drainage in their fields. Waterlogging in low-lying fields can damage crops. Farmers should avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields where rainfall has already provided sufficient moisture. Sowing and irrigation decisions should be based on weather conditions and soil moisture. stories.title: Foreign birds hunted and served at UP hotels:Poacher tells Bhaskar on camera, 'We supply meat to politicians and officials'; hotels offer on-demand delivery
stories.summary: Foreign migratory birds travelling nearly 6,000 km to India to escape deadly temperatures of -40°C are falling into a death trap in Uttar Pradesh. Protected migratory birds are being hunted in more than 10 districts of the state. Their meat is reportedly sold at hotels for up to ₹3,000 per kg. Customers are told that eating this meat increases physical strength and virility and keeps the body warm during winter. A shocking revelation emerged from a sting operation by Dainik Bhaskar, which found that hunters allegedly enjoy the protection of local politicians, police personnel and forest department officials. In return, they supply them with bird meat. To expose the network of hunters and the alleged nexus between politicians and officials in UP, an investigation was conducted in Sant Kabir Nagar, Siddharthnagar, Maharajganj and Bahraich districts. We received information that large-scale hunting was taking place in UP districts bordering Nepal. With the help of a source, a Bhaskar reporter reached a hunter named Azim alias Battery. We were told that hunters operated in the forests of Badhara Ghat and Chetia in the Bansi area. Posing as a buyer, we reached Badhara Ghat, where the hunter negotiated a deal with us. Reporter: I need foreign bird meat, every week or even every month… Azim: We can arrange it. Just place your order, whatever quantity you need. We will deliver it. Reporter: How much will it cost if we buy a larger quantity? Azim: The rate is the same, ₹1,700. We will also roast or clean and cut the meat properly. If we supply it as it is, we could get caught. Reporter: How much can you provide at a time? Azim: We can give you up to 5 kg at a time. We will prepare it so that nobody finds out. Reporter: Hunting these birds is prohibited and the rules are strict. How do you manage to hunt them in forests with guns? Azim: Forest department officials trouble us a lot, so we keep them on our side too. We have to give them some meat as well. Many people are in contact with us. Reporter: How do you catch foreign birds? Azim: We set traps and catch several at once. Come along and we will show you how they are caught. Reporter: I need more birds. Arrange things by managing the department officials. Azim: Just inform us in advance. We can arrange as many as you want. ‘We supply meat to Raja Sahab; he gets us out of trouble’ After confirming that hunting was taking place openly, the question was how hunters managed to escape the police, local residents and politicians. Azim also had an answer. He said they supplied foreign birds to 'Raja Sahab' of Bansi. Whenever they got into trouble, they would ask him to call senior police officers. Reporter: The forest is an open area. Surely everyone must know what is happening? Azim: We know 'Raja Sahab'. Reporter: So, he also helps you? Azim: Yes. Sometimes, when we get caught, he calls the police station or police outpost. Reporter: Don't the police demand money? How would they let someone go just like that? Azim: No. Once Raja Sahab says that we are his men, that's enough. We also make arrangements for food and drinks. Reporter: How do you know Raja Sahab? Azim: We have known him for a long time and keep visiting him. We work in his orchard and even catch monkeys for him free of cost. Ten days later, the reporter returned to Badhara Ghat village in the Bansi area. We wanted to find out where the hunters kept so many birds after catching them. After a lengthy conversation, the hunter became convinced that we would place a large order and took us to a dilapidated-looking house. Feathers were scattered all around the outside of the house. There were bloodstains on the walls. Besides Azim, four other associates were present inside. At the reporter's request, a minor boy showed us 12 to 15 birds kept in five large separate sacks. They were alive and tied with ropes. Among them were Chaha, Surkhab and Patera birds. Reporter: I need more birds. Do you also supply them alive? Azim: Yes, we can. How many do you need? We keep the birds alive by tying them up. If their wings are left free, they will fly away. Reporter: These are foreign migratory birds, right? Azim: This is a Surkhab. It sells for a very high price. We will give it to you. Cook it separately; it is an excellent bird. Its meat is tender. Hold it and check; you won't find any bones. It is not sold openly. Some hotels serve it only to regular customers. The price can go up to ₹3,000 per kg. Reporter: What species is this other bird? Azim: This is Patera, and the other one is Chaha. Reporter: Why are they called that? Azim: Today, you can eat Chaha. I also have foreign Tikiya species of birds. Reporter: What is special about this one? Azim: It lives among water hyacinths and is a large bird. We caught it from a pond. Reporter: The police won't catch you, will they? Azim: We have no fear of the police. We supply them with meat. The hunter had prepared a price list for the birds: Surkhab meat: ₹3,000 per kg Lalsar meat: ₹2,500 per kg Tikiya meat: ₹650 per kg Chaha meat: ₹500 per kg Patera meat: ₹550 per kg Hunter says prices are non-negotiable; claims hunting requires hard work When the reporter asked for a lower price in exchange for a bulk order, the hunter refused. He said these birds arrive only once a year and that Lalsar and Surkhab are particularly difficult to find. They sell for ₹2,500 to ₹3,000 per kg. Hotels also have to place orders in advance because the meat is very expensive. He added that if we bought a larger quantity for hotels, he could offer a slightly lower rate, and we could sell it for up to ₹3,000 per kg. He also claimed that catching these birds required considerable effort. Hunters do not use guns to catch foreign birds During the sting operation, we also learnt about other hunters operating like Azim. Such hunting is reportedly taking place in several districts, including Pilibhit, Sant Kabir Nagar, Bahraich, Maharajganj, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Unnao, Hapur and Varanasi. These birds are found along the Ganga and in wetlands, lakes and ponds. Hunters reportedly use three methods: - Method 1: Hunters carry guns but do not use them. Instead, they lay spring-loaded traps to catch the birds. They sew the beaks and eyes of two or three Siberian birds with thread and tie them up. A rope is attached to the trap, which the hunter holds while hiding nearby. When a flock of Siberian birds lands on the trap, the hunter pulls the rope, trapping the birds by their long legs and claws. - Method 2: Hunters tie the legs of one or two Siberian birds with ropes and place them in water. This attracts other birds to the pond. Once the birds arrive, hunters catch them. They generally choose the morning hours for this. - Method 3: Some hunters put chemicals into ponds to kill fish, causing them to float to the surface. Foreign migratory birds then gather around these ponds, making them easier to hunt. When asked why they did not simply shoot the birds, the hunter said catching them alive helped preserve more meat, whereas shooting them resulted in greater wastage. Hunting peaks between November and February In Siberia, Russia, Mongolia and Central Asia, temperatures drop to between -20°C and -40°C from November to February. Thick layers of ice form over rivers and lakes, making it difficult for these birds to find food. These birds travel 4,000 to 6,000 km to reach India. After spending the winter here, they return to their countries in March and April. Hunting of these birds increases significantly during this period. Poaching can lead to up to seven years in prison - Non-bailable offence: Hunting, killing, selling the meat of or keeping protected migratory birds at home is a non-bailable offence. Rare and endangered migratory birds listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act receive the highest level of protection, on a par with tigers and elephants. - Strict punishment: Under Section 51 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, a first-time offender can face imprisonment ranging from three to seven years and a fine of ₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh. The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) is active in preventing illegal hunting and trade. During winter, special teams monitor lakes and wetlands through patrols and motorboats. In November 2018, the ministry launched a special action plan for the conservation of migratory birds under the Central Asian Flyway initiative. Protected lakes are also being developed as Ramsar sites. Number of migratory birds is declining Dr Yogesh Pratap Singh says birds from extremely cold regions migrate to the Terai wetlands of eastern UP. He says large-scale hunting due to administrative negligence is rapidly reducing their numbers. These birds play an important role in maintaining the balance of our ecosystem. Continuous hunting is making the birds feel unsafe. If the situation continues, they may stop visiting these areas permanently.

stories.title: NDA allies seek 4 times more seats:Claim ministerial constituencies too; BJP could face challenges if it contests fewer seats
stories.summary: The tussle over seat-sharing has begun within the NDA ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP had allotted 32 seats to two of its allies, Apna Dal (S) and the Nishad Party. They won 23 of these seats. The RLD and SBSP, which were part of the Samajwadi Party alliance at the time, have now also joined the NDA. The four allies are now collectively demanding around 123 seats, nearly four times their combined allocation in the previous election. They argue that their support base and organisational strength have grown over the past four years. BJP National General Secretary and UP in-charge Vinod Tawde and state party president Pankaj Chaudhary are set to begin discussions with the allies to finalise a seat-sharing formula. The picture is expected to become clear by December. Here is a detailed breakdown of the allies' demands… RLD: Jayant eyes seats held by BJP ministers The RLD contested the previous election in alliance with the Samajwadi Party on 33 seats and won nine. After joining the NDA, the party has demanded 35 seats, spread from western to eastern UP. These include seats in Awadh and Purvanchal currently held by BJP MLAs. The Chhata seat in Mathura is particularly significant. Yogi government Cabinet Minister Chaudhary Laxmi Narayan represents this constituency. Giving up such seats could trigger resentment and rebellion within the BJP at the local level. This makes the RLD's demand one of the most complicated issues for the BJP. SBSP: Rajbhar insists on 17 seats allotted by SP The SBSP contested the previous election in alliance with the SP. It was allotted 17 seats and won six. Now aligned with the BJP, the party is demanding 25 to 30 seats. Its main condition is that it should get all 17 seats allotted to it by the SP in the previous election. It also wants a share of seats in other Purvanchal districts. Om Prakash Rajbhar claims that his party's presence will directly benefit the NDA in Purvanchal. Apna Dal (S): Demands more seats based on strike rate Anupriya Patel's party was the most successful NDA ally in the 2022 elections. It won 12 of the 17 seats it contested, emerging as the third-largest political party in the state. On this basis, Anupriya is demanding 30 seats this time, including the 17 it received previously. The additional seats include constituencies in Purvanchal and Bundelkhand where the BJP had lost. Nishad Party: Sanjay bets on seats lost by BJP Sanjay Nishad's party currently has five MLAs. For 2027, it is demanding 22 to 25 seats. Its proposed formula is that the BJP should allot it seats in addition to the constituencies it currently holds, particularly those where the BJP lost in 2022. Sanjay Nishad believes his party can perform better than the BJP in constituencies along riverbanks and those with a significant Nishad population. In the previous election, the party was allotted 16 seats. It contested 10 of them on its own symbol, a plate filled with food, and won six. On the remaining six seats, Nishad Party candidates contested on the BJP symbol and won five. How has the situation changed since 2022, and what could be the impact? In 2022, the BJP contested 376 of the 403 Assembly seats, leaving 27 for its allies. The BJP alone won 255 seats, comfortably above the majority mark of 202. However, the political picture for 2027 looks very different… BJP does not want smaller allies to grow stronger

stories.summary: For the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party has sounded the election bugle first by releasing its first list of five candidates. Issued late on Tuesday night with the signature of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, the list seeks to work out the political equations in western Uttar Pradesh and Bundelkhand with the slogan, "This time, voting will be united in the name of the PDA." The SP announced two candidates in Saharanpur. On both seats, Imran Masood had been asserting the Congress's claim. Congress had also placed these seats in the non-negotiable category. Imran Masood had sought a total of five seats in Saharanpur, including Behat and Saharanpur, as well as Gangoh, Nakur and Rampur Maniharan. In 2022, the SP won two seats here-Behat and Saharanpur Rural. The SP has declared tickets for both its MLAs. Besides this, the SP has also announced the ticket of Naheed Hasan, brother of Iqra Hasan, who is currently an SP MLA. View the list...

stories.title: Minister Sandeep dances with father:Rides a mare with brother in Aligarh; wedding in Delhi on November 26, reception on 27th
stories.summary: Wedding celebrations have begun in the family of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh. Ceremonies for the weddings of his grandsons, Uttar Pradesh minister Sandeep Singh and his brother Saurabh Singh, were held on Tuesday. At around 4 pm, the two brothers took part in a traditional wedding procession ceremony at Raj Palace on Marris Road in Aligarh. Their father, former MP Rajveer Singh, also known as Raju Bhaiya, danced with his sons. A video of the three dancing is going viral on social media. Both brothers mount horses after prayers The wedding ceremonies began with prayers and religious rituals. Sandeep and Saurabh mounted horses at the auspicious time. Raj Palace was filled with celebrations as drums played and music filled the air. Their father, Raju Bhaiya, was also seen dancing with his sons. See 3 pictures below : Mother Premlata, grandmother Ramwati Devi, both sisters, brothers-in-law, relatives and friends also took part in the ceremony. After the ghurchadhi ceremony, the entire family and close relatives left for Delhi. Sandeep Singh and Saurabh appeared in royal attire During the ghurchadhi ceremony, Minister Sandeep Singh was seen wearing a dark maroon sherwani with heavy embroidery. It featured intricate floral and vine motifs embroidered in white thread. He wore a pink sash around his waist, a cream-coloured safa on his head and embroidered juttis on his feet. His brother Saurabh Singh wore a light cream-coloured embroidered sherwani. It was paired with a pink sash and a border featuring golden gota-patti work. He wore a cream-coloured safa on his head, adorned with a kalgi-like embellishment. The wedding will take place at The Leela Hotel in Delhi on 26 November The two brothers will get married at The Leela Hotel in Delhi on 26 November. Sandeep Singh will take the seven rounds with his childhood friend Meghna Chaudhary, while Saurabh Singh will marry Antara Tyagi. Earlier, on 14 November, the two brothers got engaged in Talanagari, Aligarh. A grand venue had been prepared for the ceremony across around 100 bighas. Several prominent figures from politics and social life, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended the ceremony. The Prime Minister may also attend the ceremony A grand reception will be held on 27 November at The Jora, near Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi may also attend the wedding ceremony, while several VVIPs and political figures are expected to be present. Political heavyweights, ministers, MPs and MLAs from the country and the state are also likely to attend the reception. Sandeep Singh is the MLA from Atrauli and the Minister of State for Basic Education in the state government. He is the grandson of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh and the son of former MP Rajveer Singh. As a result, the weddings of the two brothers have become a topic of discussion not only as a family event but also in political circles.

stories.title: Why are seat-sharing tensions rising between Akhilesh and Rahul?:SP cites 2022, Congress 2024 polls; 3 formulas under discussion
stories.summary: Tensions over seat-sharing between the Samajwadi Party and Congress have started to rise ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. There are two main reasons for this. Congress is demanding 125 seats, while the Samajwadi Party has offered only 26. This has created a wide gap between the two parties. Both parties have different views on how to judge their electoral strength. The Samajwadi Party is looking at Congress's performance in the 2022 Assembly elections. Congress, however, says its position has changed after the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and it should not be judged by its earlier performance. Congress MP Imran Masood said, "We are not begging anyone. Congress is no longer the party it was in 2022." Leaders of both parties held a meeting for around three hours on Tuesday. After the meeting, Samajwadi Party general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav said that discussions were held on all 403 Assembly seats. He added that the talks would continue. The seat-sharing dispute is not just about the number of seats. It also reflects the struggle for a bigger role and leadership within the alliance. The Samajwadi Party wants to remain the alliance's largest partner, while Congress wants a bigger share based on its improved performance. Three formulas that could lead to an agreement... First: Congress gets 90 seats, with the SP fielding candidates in 35 According to SP sources, the party is prepared to offer the Congress 55 to 60 seats. In addition, it may offer the option of fielding its own candidates in 30 to 35 seats on the Congress symbol. This would allow the SP to field its strong candidates while increasing the number of seats allocated to the Congress. Second: Congress wants 100-125 seats, with its own candidates contesting 60-70 According to a leader associated with the Congress, the party wants 100 to 125 seats. It wants to field its own candidates in 60 to 70 of these seats. Samajwadi Party candidates could contest the remaining seats on the Congress symbol. Under this arrangement, the Congress would get an opportunity to strengthen its organisation and expand politically, while strong SP candidates could also find a place in the alliance. Third: Seat-sharing modelled on the Lok Sabha election In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP gave the Congress 17 of the 80 seats. This was a share of around 21.25 per cent. If the same ratio is applied to the Assembly election, the Congress would get around 86 seats. Under this formula, the Congress could stake a claim to at least 85 seats. The Congress wants at least one seat in every district, in addition to the Assembly constituencies falling under the Lok Sabha seats it holds. One thing is common to all three formulas: both parties want to field their respective strong candidates in the electoral fray. The dispute is over which party's candidate would be more useful to the alliance on which seat. SP's arithmetic: Congress gets 26 seats, party relies on its vote in 20 The list of 26 seats that the SP has given to the Congress includes two where the Congress won in 2022. Aradhana Mishra Mona won from Rampur Khas, while Virendra Chaudhary won from Pharenda. The Congress finished second in four seats-Mathura, Kheragarh, Jagdishpur and Kidwai Nagar. The SP's argument is that it has a strong vote base in the remaining 20 seats. According to Ram Gopal Yadav, the SP received between 60,000 and 70,000 votes in these seats in 2022, while the Congress received around 2,000 votes. The SP says the alliance could benefit if its strong candidates are fielded from these seats on the Congress symbol. The other aspect of this list is that Congress candidates forfeited their deposits on 16 of these 26 seats in 2022. In such a situation, the SP is presenting its proposal as offering the Congress more seats than its current strength in the Legislative Assembly. Of the 26 seats on the list, 10 were contested in 2022 by alliance partners that were with the SP. Of these, nine seats were held by the RLD, while the Pindra seat in Varanasi was held by Apna Dal (Kamerawadi). Congress believes it has a strong claim to the Assembly constituencies under its six Lok Sabha seats-Rae Bareli, Amethi, Saharanpur, Barabanki, Sitapur and Prayagraj. In addition, it wants at least one seat in every district. In other words, Congress is seeking not only a certain number of seats but also space to strengthen its political presence and expand its organisation across the state. Surprisingly, however, the list of 26 seats does not include Amethi and Rae Bareli. Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says: Because of Rahul and Priyanka's active involvement, the Congress considers Rae Bareli and Amethi its political strongholds. The proposal did not include any Assembly seat from the area influenced by Saharanpur MP Imran Masood. No seat was left for the Congress in Lucknow either. The political implication could be that the Samajwadi Party does not want to give the Congress an opportunity to expand in areas where it seeks to build strength on the back of its senior leaders and organisation.

stories.title: Girl flees hotel in Meerut screaming ‘Help, help’:Man grabs her by the hair and pulls her back inside; escapes by jumping off the roof
stories.summary: Young woman ran out of a hotel in Meerut screaming for help. She was running away when a man caught her by the hair and tried to drag her back inside. Hearing her screams, people from the neighbourhood gathered at the spot. When they tried to enter the hotel, the staff stopped them. Meanwhile, the accused jumped off the hotel roof and fled. The incident took place in the Sadar Bazaar police station area. Man grabs woman by hair and tries to drag her back inside According to eyewitnesses, chaos broke out outside a hotel in the Sadar Bazaar area on Tuesday. A young woman ran out of the hotel, shouting for help. A man following her grabbed her by the hair and tried to pull her back inside. Seeing the woman being dragged, nearby shopkeepers and passers-by gathered at the spot. Some people tried to enter the hotel to rescue her, but the staff stopped them. Accused escapes by jumping off the roof As the crowd outside the hotel grew, the accused went to the rooftop and jumped down to escape. People then asked the woman what had happened. She said she had been held captive inside the hotel since Monday. She alleged that the man had kept her under his control at knifepoint. On Tuesday, she found an opportunity to get out and seek help from the public. Accused identified as a resident of Kankarkhera The woman identified the accused as Salman, a resident of Kankarkhera. After learning about the incident, Sachin Sirohi, national president of the Akhil Bharatiya Hindu Suraksha Sangathan, also reached the spot. He informed the police. Police arrived, questioned the woman and took her to the police station. Woman is from Ghaziabad At the police station, the woman told police that she was from Ghaziabad. She accused Salman of holding her captive in the hotel at knifepoint and forcibly keeping her under his control. Police are investigating the case based on her statement. They are also examining the circumstances under which she was kept at the hotel and the possible role of the hotel management. The search for the accused is underway, while the hotel's CCTV footage could also prove important to the investigation. The report is being updated…

"Perhaps he did not like something this time, so he said it. He does not feel uncomfortable about it," Shastri said. He added, "We will not respond to his words. He is our elder, senior and guardian. He has always shown us affection, and we have always respected him as our guardian. We accept both his criticism and his praise." Shastri said he could not disrespect saints. He added that his aim was to unite Hindu society, not divide it. He made these remarks while speaking to the media on Tuesday, the final day of the three-day Shri Hanumant Katha at Lamini Stadium in Pathankot. This is a developing story. More details will follow.

stories.title: Man stages his own death to avoid arrest:Blind youth killed, his Aadhaar card found near body
stories.summary: A man allegedly planned a murder to avoid arrest in criminal cases and frame his rivals in Shahjahanpur. He killed Rajpal, a visually impaired man, and cut off his head with a machete. He then threw the head in Badaun and left his own Aadhaar card near the body before fleeing. The accused had reportedly told Rajpal that he could cure his eyesight through rituals. He also involved a relative and the relative's friend in the plan by promising to turn brass coins into gold. Police said he carried out the murder to avoid the criminal cases registered against him and blame his rivals. Police arrested all three accused on the night of 23 November. On Tuesday, at around 1 pm, SP (Rural) Diksha Bhaware shared details of the case. The incident took place in the Kalan police station area, around 70 km from the district headquarters. Roamed around disguised as a holy man after being released from jail Five cases, including rape, have been registered against 50-year-old Vinod, a resident of Siuri village. He was released from jail on bail a year ago. He had been absconding ever since. Meanwhile, Vinod's wife and children had moved to Delhi. After his release from jail, Vinod roamed around disguised as a holy man and used occult rituals to lure people. Was looking for someone who lived alone Vinod's in-laws live in Chaudhera village, under the jurisdiction of Nigohi police station. Rajpal, 30, lived there. Rajpal's wife had put chilli in his eye around 10 years ago, causing him to lose his eyesight. After this, his wife left with their son. Vinod was thinking of a way to avoid a police case. He was looking for someone who had no family. This was why Vinod chose Rajpal as his target. He involved a relative and his friend in the conspiracy Vinod then began luring Rajpal. He told him that his eyesight could be restored through occult rituals. Convinced by Vinod's words, Rajpal agreed to undergo the rituals. However, Vinod feared that he would not be able to carry out the task alone. So he also involved his relative Vikas, who lived in Badaun, and Vikas's associate, Ompal. Promise to turn 15 brass coins into gold Vinod told his relative that he had 15 brass coins. He said the coins would turn into gold after a sacrifice. He would give all the coins to Vikas and Ompal. In addition, Vikas's aunt, who had left home, would also return. Greed prompted the two men to agree to sacrifice Rajpal. Head severed near the well, Aadhaar card placed beside the torso On the night of 14 November, the three reached a dry well in Siyuri. They called Rajpal there for a पूजा ceremony. Vinod then beheaded Rajpal with a billhook and crushed his face with a brick. Vinod placed his Aadhaar card near the torso. He then took the head to Badaun, around 50 kilometres away, and threw it into a river. Family falsely identified the body and had an FIR registered against nine people The torso was found in the well on 17 November. The villagers refused to accept that it was Vinod's body. On 18 November, Vinod's wife, Pooja, and son, Aditya, reached the village. They identified the body as Vinod's after seeing the thread tied around its leg. An FIR was registered against nine people, including the village head. Called his son to reveal that he was alive Meanwhile, Vinod bought a new SIM card and inserted it into Rajpal's mobile phone. Vinod then called his son and told him that he was alive. He revealed the entire plan to his family. Vinod told his family to go to the Chief Minister's public hearing to have their opponents sent to jail. This would put pressure on the police. Vinod's wife Pooja, mother Sumirta, brothers Nand Kishore and Kunwarpal, sons Alok and Aditya, and nephew Manoj then supported him. Surveillance and the deceased's mobile phone exposed the truth Meanwhile, when police showed the clothes from the body to Rajpal's villagers after receiving information that he was missing, his true identity was revealed. The police then placed Vinod and his family members' mobile phones under surveillance. As soon as Rajpal's mobile phone was switched on, the police traced its location and arrested Vinod and his two associates. The three accused were planning to flee from Budaun to Nepal. Seven family members involved in the conspiracy were also taken into custody. A billhook and a brick used in the murder were recovered from the accused. SP (Rural) Diksha Bhawre said: As the deceased was 30 and Vinod was 50, the police already suspected him. However, Vinod's wife and son blocked the road to put pressure on the police. The police have also added the names of seven family members to the FIR for their involvement in the conspiracy. All three accused have been sent to jail. Rajpal's head has not yet been found.

stories.title: Azam says he cannot be stopped from contesting polls:Rulers are cruel, and the entire country is living in fear
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party senior leader Azam Khan said on Tuesday in Rampur, "Who can stop me from contesting elections? My election symbol is the bicycle. The bicycle will contest, and the bicycle will win." Azam said he could not think of anything beyond the bicycle. "I do not want to think about cars, helicopters or planes," he said. Azam was released from Ghaziabad's Dasna Jail on interim bail on 18 November. Earlier, after being released from Rampur Jail on 31 October 2026, he was arrested in a case filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). Read details below : Question: Will you contest the 2027 Assembly elections? Azam Khan: "Who can stop me from contesting elections? My election symbol is the bicycle. The bicycle will contest, and the bicycle will win." He said he could not think of anything beyond the bicycle. "People with small hearts and narrow thinking do not think about cars, helicopters or planes. They are doing their work, and we are doing ours. We are grateful to the High Court and Supreme Court judges," he said. Question: Are you afraid or worried about anything? Azam Khan: "People do feel afraid when the rulers are cruel. That is why people are silent and cannot speak their minds. They will express themselves on election day. It is not just me; the entire country is afraid." Question: But is there also fear of vote theft? Azam Khan: “There is fear. You were also worried about whether I would speak or not. Fear is something that exists in every heart.” Azam Khan says, 'One day, we will visit Nagina' Azam Khan was asked about the possible impact of a political alliance between Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad on Uttar Pradesh politics. In a joking tone, he said, "What are you talking about? One day, we will go to Nagina and tell the people there, as well as the people across the country." After his release from jail, several people have been visiting Rampur to meet the Samajwadi Party leader. These meetings are being linked to preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections and his future role in politics. Will Azam Khan be able to contest elections? According to legal experts, Azam Khan has been sentenced to jail terms ranging from 2 to 10 years in eight cases. Because of these convictions, he is currently not eligible to contest elections. Abdullla Azam has received relief in the fake birth certificate case, but he is also disqualified due to convictions in two other cases. Tanzeen Fatima can contest elections. However, considering her age and health, the names of Azam Khan's elder son, Adeeb, and daughter-in-law, Sidra, are also being discussed. According to senior Supreme Court lawyer Shariq Abbasi, getting bail alone does not make a person eligible to contest elections. The person must get a stay on the conviction from the court.

stories.title: Baba Ramdev softens criticism of Dhirendra Shastri:Describes him as a child and friend, a day after calling him fraud and hypocrite
stories.summary: Ramdev clarified his remarks about Dhirendra Shastri at a press conference in Haridwar on Tuesday. He said that Bageshwar Baba was like a child in front of him. He was also like his younger brother and disciple. Therefore, he had scolded him in his capacity as an elder over the things he found inappropriate and which had hurt him. Shastri had accepted his reprimand as an expression of affection. This also reflected his greatness. Ramdev said that a massive uproar had been going on for two days. He had also spoken to Dhirendra Shastri the previous day. He said he had been deeply hurt by the comments being made about their gods and goddesses. This was not part of the Sanatan tradition. There was no distinction among the gods. Discrimination being practised in the name of gods, castes and religions was dividing society. He said he was deeply saddened. Secondly, he had a serious question in his mind: Sanatan Dharma should not be associated with superstition or hypocrisy. This was because Sanatan Dharma was divine. Sanatan Dharma was scientific. The values of Sanatan Dharma were very lofty. The matter was trolled in a very wrong manner. My words should not have been taken this way. Now know what Ramdev had said earlier... 1. They do not know the Vedas, Upanishads or Constitution, yet claim to be Sanatanis Some people have neither read the Vedas, nor studied philosophy and the Upanishads, nor read the Puranas, the Ramayana or the Mahabharata. They do not know the Constitution or democracy either. They keep standing up and talking utter nonsense. They say, "We are Sanatanis; we will save Hinduism." Such people incite crowds with misguided ideas. He described such storytellers as frauds and hypocrites. 2. They exploit people by creating religious hysteria Some storytellers frighten people in the name of religion and possession by ghosts and spirits. They let their hair down, chant strange mantras and pretend to drive away ghosts. They then sprinkle water and claim that the problem has been resolved. This is a way of creating religious hysteria and exploiting people. He said women are the biggest victims of this hypocrisy. 3. Ram is great, Krishna is crooked... Repeated the same statement even after apologising Ramdev said, "Ram is great, while Krishna is crooked..." and then apologised. After apologising, he went there and bowed before Banke Bihari. Even after that, he is saying, "Krishna is indeed crooked!" You hypocrite, you have lost your senses! We are saying this deliberately: do not make such statements. No one has the right to make frivolous remarks in society. Everything has its own limits, discipline and protocol. 4. It is necessary to call out those who engage in hypocrisy, so I criticised them from the stage Do not compare deities. Even in jest or banter, do not disrespect or insult our divine incarnations. Who are we to compare deities, insult them or show them disrespect? How can we joke or banter about them? It is wrong. Even when someone says something like this personally, we try to explain it to them. If they still do not understand, we have to speak out from the stage. Otherwise, no one should say tomorrow that someone was engaging in hypocrisy while Swami Ramdev was present, and that Swami Ramdev did not stop him. That is why we have called it out from the stage here today. 5. We cannot engage in pretence and hypocrisy in the name of Sanatan Ramdev said that people should understand that deceit, ostentation and hypocrisy cannot be practised in the name of Sanatan. Such things are wrong and cause pain and distress within us. We are ascetics, so we will never make deranged remarks. Now, know which statement by Dhirendra Shastri sparked the controversy Shastri had said, "Your Thakurji is bent at 3 places" Dhirendra Krishna's remarks about Lord Krishna sparked a controversy. Comparing Lord Shri Ram with Lord Krishna, he said- 'Just look at even one picture of your Thakurji. Even when he stands, he is bent at three places. One foot over the other, he bends his waist and plays the flute with his neck tilted. Our Thakurji stands completely straight. Even his name is straight. Our Thakurji walks straight and looks straight too. Your Thakurji's name is crooked, he walks crooked and even stands crooked. Lifting a mountain is no great feat. A disciple of our God flew away with an entire mountain. Our God's abode is straight too-Ayodhya, while yours is Vrindavan!' Shastri said-Many people misunderstood what I said However, as the controversy grew, Dhirendra Shastri released a video clarifying his remarks. He said, "Many people misunderstood what I said. We ourselves are devotees of Thakurji and Braj. Whenever we pray to Thakurji, we ask that we be allowed to live in Braj." He said, "We also narrate the Shrimad Bhagwat Katha and sing the praises of Thakurji. We had no intention of differentiating between Lord Ram and Lord Krishna." In fact, Dhirendra Shastri had commented on Lord Krishna during the Shriram Katha being held in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh. After a video of the remarks emerged on 10 October (Sunday), the saints of Mathura expressed their displeasure. They had asked Dhirendra Shastri to apologise. Dhirendra Shastri reached Vrindavan on 21 November and offered prayers at the Banke Bihari temple. He said, "I bow by rubbing my nose at the feet of the people of Braj." He also led chants of, "Victory to the Crooked Thakur Ji... Victory to Hanuman Ji with the crooked leg..."

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav offers prayers at gurdwara in Lucknow:Says Election Commission is adding 3 crore voters under pressure from CM
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged that the Election Commission was planning to add 3 crore voters under pressure from the Chief Minister. He said, "The account numbers of the people whose votes are being added are also being collected. It is worth considering who these account numbers will be given to." Earlier on Tuesday, Akhilesh Yadav visited a gurdwara in Sadar, Lucknow, where he paid obeisance and sought the blessings of Guru Nanak Dev. He spent more than half an hour at the gurdwara, attended the satsang and listened to kirtan. Akhilesh said the Sikh community had made many sacrifices for the country, which would always be remembered. He added that the community had made India proud across the world. Check out pictures below : The committee presented Akhilesh with a sword and prasad On reaching the gurdwara, Akhilesh Yadav tied a yellow scarf around his head and bowed in prayer. During the visit, the gurdwara committee honoured him by presenting him with a sword and prasad. Akhilesh Yadav said that the Sikh community had brought glory to India across the world. The Sikh community had made a significant contribution to strengthening the country's unity and integrity. Guru Nanak Dev had always conveyed the message of peace, unity and brotherhood. 'BJP putting pressure on Election Commission' Akhilesh Yadav said that the public wanted elections to be held on time. It was the responsibility of the constitutional body to conduct free and fair elections, but questions were now being raised about the body itself. The BJP's preparation was focused on how to add 3 crore voters. On the one hand, EVM machines were being repaired. On the other, continuous pressure was being exerted on the Election Commission. Alliances are formed to secure victory Akhilesh Yadav said that the party's senior leaders are holding discussions. They are discussing each other's seats and considering how many seats the other party could win. It is difficult to say anything at this stage about seat-sharing. Alliances are formed so that we can win. We will work together on an arrangement that enables us to defeat our opponents. 'Government unable to bring investment to the state' Akhilesh Yadav said, "They know they are going to lose the village-head elections, which is why they are not holding them on time. They have no answer on inflation and are unable to provide employment. They are unable to bring investment. They cannot answer the people, and the Bharatiya Janata Party will lose on the very day the election date is announced. We are the ones who are going to defeat them." Akhilesh Yadav said that the other party has to keep several allies happy. You must all have heard about a boat that does not know whether it will end up moored on this bank or the other. He claimed that Samajwadi Party candidate Sangram would win the Atroliya seat by a historic margin of votes.

stories.title: Stories of Kashi’s ghats to be available in 15 languages:Tourism Minister to launch service today, with broadcasts in French, German, Spanish and Japanese
stories.summary: Tourists and pilgrims visiting Varanasi will soon be able to explore the history of Kashi's 84 ghats without relying on guides. The Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department has linked all 84 ghats to a digital platform and developed the 'Varanasi 84 Ghats Audiobook-Audio Tour'. The GPS-based facility will allow visitors to listen to audio guides and read about the history, religious beliefs and cultural significance of each ghat in their preferred language. Tourism Minister Jaiveer Singh will launch the facility at Namo Ghat on Dev Deepawali. The department has completed preparations for the launch. The service will be accessible through the official UP Tourism mobile app and website. Separate options for walking tours and boat rides Individual audio chapters have been prepared for all 84 ghats, covering their historical, cultural, religious and mythological significance. Visitors will be able to choose between two modes: a walking tour and a boat tour. Those exploring the ghats on foot can select the 'walking tour' option, while visitors taking a boat ride on the Ganga can choose the 'boat tour' to listen to stories associated with the ghats. GPS to automatically play audio at each ghat The facility's main feature is its GPS-enabled smart system. As soon as visitors reach a ghat, the mobile app will detect their location and automatically play the corresponding audio guide. The audio will pause when they move away from the designated location and resume from the same point when they return. Visitors will also have the option to manually select any ghat and listen to its history and significance. Audio tour available in 15 languages To cater to domestic and international tourists, the audio tour has been developed in 15 languages. These include Hindi, English, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Kannada, Odia, Malayalam and Urdu. International visitors can also access it in French, German, Spanish, Japanese and Korean. Visitors will be able to download the complete audio tour before starting their trip. This will allow them to explore the ghats without requiring a continuous internet connection. People can explore Kashi's ghats from home The facility will also be accessible to people living outside Varanasi. Through the 'Enable Offline/Remote Tour' option, users from anywhere in India or abroad will be able to experience the ghats virtually. They can listen to stories and learn about the history and cultural heritage of Kashi's ghats from their homes. How to use the audio tour without logging in Visitors can access the facility by opening the official UP Tourism app on their Android or iOS smartphones. They will then need to select the 'Varanasi 84 Ghats Audiobook-Audio Tour' option, choose their preferred language and select either the walking or boat tour mode. After reaching a ghat, they can tap on 'Start Tour at Location' to begin the GPS-based audio guide. The service will also be available on the UP Tourism website. No account creation or login will be required.

stories.title: VIDEO | Leopard attacks man in Kanpur:Pounces as he enters field; 9 injured, people flee to save their lives
stories.summary: A leopard attacked villagers working in fields in Kanpur around noon on Tuesday, injuring nine people. Around 12 people initially entered the fields in an attempt to surround the leopard. Later, nearly 50 villagers gathered at the spot carrying sticks and clubs. During the operation, the leopard attacked them, leaving nine people injured. The injured were taken to hospital for treatment. Police and Forest Department teams reached the spot after receiving information about the incident. A search operation is under way to track down the leopard. The incident took place in Karan Kheda village, under the jurisdiction of Maharajpur police station. See 2 pictures.... Leopard attacks villagers attempting to surround it Villager Kishanlal said a leopard was spotted in the fields between 11 am and noon on Tuesday (24 Nov). After an alert was raised, villagers gathered at Ramsajeevan's marigold field. Around 12 people surrounded the animal from all sides, but it suddenly attacked them. After receiving information about the incident, nearly 50 villagers reached the field carrying sticks and began trying to corner the leopard. During this, the animal first attacked Ramkesh and then injured several others. Panic spread across the area as people ran for safety. Mohit Sharma, a resident of Madarpur, said he was harvesting cauliflower in a field when the leopard attacked him. Leopard also attacked villager who came to save his friend Injured Ravi Nishad said that he had gone to the field to pick marigold flowers. During this, the leopard attacked one of his friends. When he heard his friend scream and went to save him, the leopard attacked him as well. He somehow managed to escape from the spot with his life. Ravi said the leopard had also bitten and injured five or six other people besides him. 9 people injured, admitted to hospital The injured include Hariram Nishad (40), Ramkesh Nishad (18), Buddhi Nishad (50), Mohit Vishwakarma (18) and Sahil. Four other people were also injured. Sahil is a resident of Sikhtiya and had come to Karnakheda to stay at his maternal aunt's house. He suffered serious injuries. The injured were taken to hospital by their family members. On receiving the information, Sheikhpur outpost in-charge Anuj Patel and the Dial 112 team reached the spot. The police and Forest Department teams are conducting a search for the leopard with the villagers. Villagers urged to stay indoors The administration has appealed to villagers to stay in safe homes with their families and children. They have been advised not to go towards the fields alone and to work in the fields only in groups. Bhupendra Singh of the Forest Department said that Karnkheda village is situated along the river and is surrounded by forest. In such circumstances, a wild animal can emerge from the forest and enter the village. The Forest Department's rescue team has reached the spot and is conducting an operation to capture the animal.

stories.title: Fake oxytocin factory busted, 2 arrested in Dubagga:Accused mix phenyl, salt and powder; goods worth ₹2 crore seized
stories.summary: A joint team of the Special Task Force (STF) and Dubagga Police has busted an illegal factory manufacturing counterfeit oxytocin in Lucknow. Two men were arrested during a raid in Mohari Jehta village on Monday (23 Nov) night. Police seized fake oxytocin worth more than ₹2 crore, along with equipment and raw materials used in its manufacture. A vehicle allegedly used to transport and supply the counterfeit drug was also recovered from the premises. Two brothers arrested, fake oxytocin worth ₹2 crore seized According to police, the accused were preparing to fill the counterfeit oxytocin into bottles and ampoules before supplying it. The arrested men have been identified as Dildar and Irfan. The two brothers are residents of the Cattle Colony in Thakurganj. See 3 pictures... 3,700 bottles and 1.77 lakh ampoules seized During the raid, police recovered 3,700 bottles of 200 ml each and 1,77,800 plastic-packed ampoules of 2 ml each. The seizure also included 35 litres of liquid oxytocin, suspected powder, empty bottles, caps, rubber stoppers, packaging material and other equipment. A pickup vehicle was also seized from the premises. Police said materials used to manufacture and package counterfeit oxytocin were found at the site. Phenyl, salt and suspected powder found at factory Police recovered five-litre cans of phenyl, 36 packets of Tata Salt and suspected oxytocin powder from the premises. Investigators suspect that the accused were using these materials to manufacture counterfeit oxytocin. The STF and police are questioning the accused to establish where the counterfeit drug was being supplied and identify others involved in the operation. Case registered against two brothers A case has been registered against both accused at Dubagga police station under Case No. 360/2026. What is oxytocin, and why is it given to patients? Oxytocin is a hormone that is naturally produced in the body. It is also administered as an injection. In hospitals, it is mainly used during labour to induce uterine contractions and to stop excessive bleeding after childbirth. Using counterfeit medicine can pose a serious risk to patients.

stories.title: SP releases first list of 5 candidates for UP polls:3-hour seat-sharing talks with Congress end without deal; Congress seeks 125 seats, SP offers 26
stories.summary: The seat-sharing arrangement between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress in Uttar Pradesh appears to be heading for a deadlock. Akhilesh Yadav wants to offer Congress only 26 of the state's 403 Assembly seats, while Congress is sticking to its demand for 125 seats. On Tuesday, leaders of the two parties held a meeting lasting around 3 hours and 15 minutes at the residence of Congress MP Pramod Tiwari in Delhi. Discussions continued from 12.15 pm to 3.30 pm. SP announces five candidates for Assembly polls The Samajwadi Party released its first list of five candidates as seat-sharing talks cantinue with Congress. The SP announced two candidates in Saharanpur. On both seats, Imran Masood had been asserting the Congress's claim. Congress had also placed these seats in the non-negotiable category. Imran Masood had sought a total of five seats in Saharanpur, including Behat and Saharanpur, as well as Gangoh, Nakur and Rampur Maniharan. In 2022, the SP won two seats here-Behat and Saharanpur Rural. The SP has declared tickets for both its MLAs. Besides this, the SP has also announced the ticket of Naheed Hasan, brother of Iqra Hasan, who is currently an SP MLA. View the list... Before the meeting, SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav took a firm stance, saying, "I have given Congress a list of 26 seats from which it can field its candidates." SP MP Rajeev Rai also reiterated the same position. Congress MP Imran Masood objected to the SP's offer, saying, "We are not begging anyone. This is not appropriate for an alliance. Congress is much stronger today. It is no longer the same party it was in 2022." However, Akhilesh appeared to adopt a somewhat softer stance. In Lucknow, he said the objective of the alliance was to win the elections. The SP was ready to accommodate its allies by giving up seats and making adjustments, as this was a major political battle and the shared goal was victory. The second round of talks between the two parties has now concluded.After the meeting, leaders from both Congress and the SP appeared positive about the negotiations. Ram Gopal Yadav and Rajendra Pal Gautam said the alliance would be finalised within the next two days.

stories.title: 4 killed, including father and son, in Lakhimpur crash:Truck rams van, car crushed from 11 feet to 8 feet; 6 injured
stories.summary: A truck collided head-on with a van in Lakhimpur Kheri. Four people, including a father and son travelling in the van, were killed in the accident. Six people were injured. There were 11 people in the van. They were returning home after working all day. The collision was so severe that the van was completely mangled. The 11-foot van was reduced to 7-8 feet. The driver's cabin was crushed, and even the seat was torn out. The people remained trapped inside. The truck driver abandoned the vehicle and fled. Police reached the spot after receiving the information and sent the bodies for post-mortem examinations. They cut open the gate to pull the injured people out and took them to hospital by ambulance. The truck has been impounded and efforts are under way to locate the driver. The accident took place at 12.30 a.m. late on Monday night in the Sadar Kotwali area, around 12 km from the district headquarters. The deceased have been identified as Jagannath, 59, his son Pappu, 30, Ajay and Bahadur. Pictures of the accident- Now, let us understand the full case step by step- Mehwaganj outpost in-charge Bharat Singh said- The van was carrying more people than its capacity. Police are examining CCTV footage from the surrounding area. At present, the accident appears to have been caused by the van driver dozing off. However, the actual cause will be known only after the investigation.

stories.title: Suspected terrorist Ujaid arrested in Meerut:Was planning an attack on JK military airbase; probe reveals links to Pakistani handler
stories.summary: Security agencies arrested a suspected terrorist, Ujaid, in Meerut on Monday night over his alleged links with Pakistani handlers. He is accused of plotting an attack on a military airbase in Jammu and Kashmir and having connections with the Shahzad Bhatti gang. Investigators reportedly recovered several suspicious WhatsApp chats from his mobile phone. Ujaid was also in online contact with suspected terrorist Mohammad Sajid, who was arrested in Jammu and Kashmir on November 27, 2025. Suspect questioned by IB, ATS and other agencies During questioning, Sajid reportedly named Ujaid. Following his arrest, the Intelligence Bureau (IB), Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and other intelligence agencies questioned him. The investigation is under way. Ujaid is a resident of Baniyapara, under the Kotwali police station area. Suspect had been in contact with arrested terrorist for six months According to investigating agencies, Ujaid had been in online contact with suspected terrorist Mohammad Sajid for the past six months. Sajid was arrested in Jammu and Kashmir on November 27, 2025, while allegedly preparing to carry out a fidayeen attack on the Army. During questioning, Sajid reportedly disclosed Ujaid's name, following which police began searching for him. On January 18, 2026, Jammu and Kashmir Police raided Ujaid's house, but he managed to escape. Fearing further police action, his family locked the house and left. He was eventually arrested on Monday night. Suspect allegedly expressed willingness to carry out suicide attack According to sources, Ujaid discussed fidayeen attacks on social media and told Sajid that he was y to carry out a suicide attack. Police have recovered several chats related to these conversations from his mobile phone. Investigating agencies are examining the chats and other digital evidence. The investigation has also revealed that Ujaid was allegedly in contact with Pakistani handler Shahzad Bhatti. He is also accused of being part of a conspiracy to attack a military airbase in Jammu and Kashmir. After his arrest, the Intelligence Bureau (IB), Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and other intelligence agencies questioned him for several hours. Ujaid escaped during police raid on his house in January On January 18, the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Jammu and Kashmir Police raided the house of Ujaid Qureshi, a resident of Baniyapara in the Kotwali police station area, while searching for him. However, he was not at home at the time. The team pasted a notice outside the house before leaving. Some time later, Ujaid returned on a scooter but fled after seeing the notice. A video of the incident also surfaced. ATS suspects he was recruiting youths for terror activities According to the Uttar Pradesh ATS, Ujaid was active in a WhatsApp group where a conspiracy was allegedly being hatched to carry out a fidayeen attack on the Indian Army. The agency suspected that he was radicalising young people and recruiting them for terrorist activities. He was also suspected of being associated with an Al-Qaeda-linked sleeper cell. During the raid, the team detained his two brothers for questioning, but later released them. Case registered under Section 113 of the BNS A case was registered against Ujaid under Section 113 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). This section relates to terrorist activities. Investigating agencies were probing his alleged terrorist network, contacts and activities.

stories.title: Scorpio crashes into BJP MLA Sushil Singh’s convoy:Two Fortuners hit in Chandauli as MLA returns from Anant Singh’s daughter’s event
stories.summary: A speeding Scorpio rammed into two Fortuner SUVs in the convoy of BJP MLA Sushil Singh in Uttar Pradesh's Chandauli district. One of the Fortuners overturned, while both vehicles sustained damage. Three people travelling in the Scorpio were injured and taken to hospital. Four people, including the drivers, were travelling in the two Fortuners. Their occupants narrowly escaped injury. Four people were in the Scorpio, of whom three sustained injuries. MLA suspects conspiracy behind convoy accident The incident took place late on Monday night near Futiya and Jagdisarai villages in the Sadar Kotwali area. Sushil Singh, the BJP MLA from Saiyadraja, was returning from Mokama in Bihar with a convoy of 10 vehicles. He had gone there to congratulate MLA Anant Singh ahead of his daughter's wedding. The MLA was also travelling in the convoy when the accident occurred. He has raised the possibility of a conspiracy behind the incident. Two pictures related to the accident... Convoy vehicles hit at two locations The MLA's convoy was travelling from Chandauli to Varanasi. According to information, a speeding Scorpio collided with one of the convoy's Fortuners near Futiya village. After this, the driver tried to flee the scene. During this, the Scorpio collided with another Fortuner near Jagdisarai. One of the vehicles overturned in the accident. Some people also sustained minor injuries. Scorpio occupant admitted to hospital The injured youth has been identified as Pankaj Yadav, a resident of Manrajpur village in the Saiyadraja area. He was admitted to hospital in critical condition. Both Fortuners were also damaged in the accident. After receiving the information, police reached the scene and seized the Scorpio. Police are investigating the case. MLA Sushil Singh said, “He was present in the convoy at the time of the accident. His vehicle was not damaged. There is suspicion of a conspiracy behind the incident.”

stories.title: Former MP accused of rape in Gorakhpur:Woman alleges he had sex with her on promise of marriage, then blocked her number
stories.summary: A former MP from Purvanchal has been accused of rape and sexual exploitation in Gorakhpur. The woman approached the police station and created a scene, demanding action against him. Following this, Gorakhpur SSP assigned the investigation to Ramgarhtal police under the supervision of the Cantonment Circle Officer (CO). The complainant, a manager at a finance company in the Taramandal area, has alleged that the former MP established a physical relationship with her on the promise of marriage. Woman alleges former MP promised to marry her On Saturday, the woman created a scene at Ramgarhtal police station and insisted that a case be registered. In her written complaint, she alleged that the former public representative had taken her on a trip while he was in office. They stayed at a hotel, where he allegedly had a physical relationship with her after promising to marry her. She also claimed that he staged a marriage ceremony at a temple. However, she alleged that he has now been avoiding her requests to get married. When she pressed him on the issue, he allegedly threatened to kill her. Claims former MP blocked her number The woman further alleged that the former MP had blocked her mobile number. She claimed that people who live with him were also refusing to help her contact him. She reiterated that he had threatened to kill her and demanded police action. Police verifying photographs on her phone The woman showed police several photographs on her mobile phone, allegedly featuring her with the former public representative. She also showed a photograph of what she claimed was their wedding. Police are verifying the photographs found on her phone. Reports suggest that officers have also contacted the former MP, who reportedly said he was away on party-related work. stories.title: 5 lakh devotees take holy dip in Ganga in Kashi:Crowds gather at 80 Ghats from 4 am; offer lamps and perform charity on Kartik Purnima
stories.summary: Varanasi witnessed a massive turnout of devotees on Tuesday on the occasion of Kartik Purnima. Large crowds gathered at around 80 ghats along the Ganga, including Dashashwamedh Ghat. Devotees began arriving as early as 4 am to take a holy dip. Despite the biting cold and dense fog, their enthusiasm remained undiminished. More than 5 lakh devotees had taken a holy dip in the Ganga by morning. After bathing, devotees offered water to the Sun God. They also performed charitable activities, chanted prayers, meditated and sang devotional hymns. Chants of 'Har Har Gange' and 'Har Har Mahadev' echoed across the ghats during the lamp-offering ceremonies. See the picture... Crowds gather from Dashashwamedh to Assi Ghat Dashashwamedh Ghat witnessed a steady stream of devotees from early morning. Heavy crowds were also reported at other prominent ghats, including Assi, Tulsi, Janki, Shivala, Dandi, Kedar, Darbhanga, Sheetla, Rajendra Prasad and Bhainsasur. After taking a holy dip in the Ganga, devotees offered lamps and worshipped the river. Religious rituals and prayers continued at various ghats throughout the morning. Holy dip and charity believed to bring eternal blessings According to religious beliefs, taking a dip in a sacred river before sunrise, offering lamps and performing charitable activities on Kartik Purnima hold special significance. It is believed that bathing in the Ganga on this day washes away sins and brings happiness and prosperity. The month of Kartik is considered sacred to Lord Vishnu. Devotees also worship Lord Vishnu and Goddess Tulsi on this occasion. Dev Deepawali is traditionally celebrated on Kartik Purnima. According to Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva killed the demon Tripurasura on this day, freeing the gods from his terror. To celebrate the victory, the gods lit lamps in Kashi and marked the occasion with a festival of lights. Police and river patrol teams remain on alert The administration and police made extensive security arrangements in view of the large crowds. As a security measure, people were prohibited from carrying belongings along the route from Godowlia Crossing towards Dashashwamedh Ghat. NDRF personnel continuously monitored the Ganga from boats. Police personnel, river police and women officers remained deployed under the supervision of Dashashwamedh ACP Vivek Kumar Tiwari and Station House Officer Santosh Kumar Singh. Special attention was given to crowd management at the ghats and the safety of devotees taking a dip in the river.

stories.summary: Four children were killed and 25 others injured after a speeding truck rammed into a school bus from behind on the Lucknow-Agra Expressway in Uttar Pradesh’s Kannauj district. The bus was carrying 60 people, including 50 students. They were returning to Kaushambi after a picnic in Agra. Kannauj SP Vinod Kumar said the bus belonged to Oriental Public School in Kaushambi. It had left Agra at midnight on Tuesday. At around 6 am on Wednesday, the driver had stopped the bus on the expressway in the Tirwa police station area to allow the children to use the toilet. The accident happened during the stop. The impact was so severe that the rear section of the bus was badly damaged and several seats were dislodged. Several children were trapped between the seats. stories.title: Cold intensifies in UP as snowfall hits hills:Dense fog covers 15 cities; temperatures set to drop further next week
stories.summary: Snowfall in the hills has begun affecting the plains, with temperatures dropping across Uttar Pradesh. The cold is intensifying, accompanied by dense fog during the morning hours. On Tuesday morning, fog covered around 15 cities, including Prayagraj, Ballia, Deoria, Lakhimpur, Sambhal, Bijnor, Chandauli and Mau. On Monday, fog was particularly dense in Deoria and Sambhal, reducing visibility to just a few metres. Motorists faced difficulties due to poor visibility during the morning. According to Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, the impact of the cyclone over the Bay of Bengal has now ended. As a result, northerly and north-westerly winds have replaced easterly winds. These winds will gradually lower night temperatures, while dense fog is expected during the morning. The cold is likely to intensify further from next week. Night temperatures may fall by 3–5 degrees According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), winds are likely to turn westerly following the withdrawal of the cyclone's influence. This could lead to a fall of 3–5 degrees Celsius in minimum temperatures across the state over the next few days. This will increase the chill during the night and early morning hours. Moderate to dense fog is likely across most parts of the state, including the Terai districts. People are advised to take precautions against the cold, particularly during early mornings and late nights. Farmers advised to protect crops from cold and fog Wheat: Maintain adequate moisture in the soil during the early growth stage. Avoid waterlogging in fields. Mustard: Prolonged fog and moisture can increase the risk of white rust and other fungal diseases. Monitor crops regularly. Potato: Check leaves for signs of late blight. Consult agricultural experts if symptoms appear. Peas and gram: Excess moisture and waterlogging can damage roots. Ensure proper drainage in fields.

Soon after, all the ghats along the river lit up with rows of diyas. Visitors from 40 countries have reached Kashi to witness the festival. Around 15 lakh tourists have arrived in the city. Large crowds have gathered at the ghats to watch the Ganga Aarti, laser show, drone show and fireworks. The areas from Kashi Vishwanath Temple to Namo Ghat and Harishchandra Ghat have been beautifully decorated. The temples are glowing with colourful lights. The decoration at the Masan Ghat has also caught the attention of visitors. Foreign tourists praised the grand celebrations. Jessica, who came from Cambodia, said, "I did not expect such a huge festival." Alexia from Greece said, “India is a beautiful and spiritual country. Everyone should visit Kashi at least once in their life.”
