stories.title: Why law and order dominates Akhilesh’s SP manifesto:Yogi repeatedly invokes pre-2017 UP, but how different was the situation in 2022?
stories.summary: "Irrespective of which caste, religion or political party a criminal belongs to, his place will be in jail and he will not be spared at any cost." - Akhilesh Yadav While releasing the Samajwadi Party's manifesto (pledge document) ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Akhilesh Yadav placed the greatest emphasis on law and order. He even said that a criminal would be identified by his crime, not his party, and that no criminal would be spared. Akhilesh appeared to be trying to break the image that the BJP has repeatedly imposed on him. This is why Akhilesh said that a zero-tolerance policy would be implemented by adopting a tough stance towards crime and criminals. He made three promises to improve law and order... Akhilesh also promised in the manifesto to set up a special unit of the STF. These units will resolve land disputes and prevent mafias or influential individuals from encroaching on the land of poor, backward and helpless people. He also said that vehicles of a different colour would be prepared on the lines of Dial 100/112 to patrol and take action. The accountability of the concerned district officials would then be fixed. Akhilesh's masterstroke: 10 grams of gold on the birth of a daughter Akhilesh made a major announcement to give up to 10 grams of gold on the birth of a daughter. The announcement is being seen in political circles as a 'masterstroke'. It is being compared with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister 'Thalapathy' Vijay's gold scheme for newborn babies. The Tamil Nadu government promised to launch the 'Thaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam' scheme, under which eligible newborn babies born in government hospitals would receive a one-gram gold ring and a baby welcome kit. Later, Thalapathy Vijay's government was also formed. An attempt to win over four sections Women - 33% reservation in police recruitment Women's role has become significant over the past few elections. This is why the Samajwadi Party has courted women voters. Akhilesh promised that if the party came to power, it would provide 33% reservation in police recruitment. He also announced an annual pension of ₹40,000 for women living below the poverty line. A 'Bicycle' and 'Solar Table Lamp Distribution Scheme' will be launched for girls in Class 9 and above. The announcement to provide laptops to students who pass Class 12 is also expected to attract women voters. Girls currently account for the highest number of successful candidates in board examinations. While releasing the manifesto, Akhilesh also made it clear that the party would issue a separate manifesto for women. It will provide assistance of ₹2 lakh and a house to those who marry widows, women with disabilities and orphan girls. Farmers - Loans will be waived within 100 days if the party comes to power The Samajwadi Party's biggest announcement is a farm loan waiver. Farmers in the state currently have debt of ₹1.40 lakh crore. The SP has announced that it will waive 100% of the loans of all farmers in the state within 100 days of forming the government. A 'Farmers' Income and Welfare Commission' will be established to survey and suggest ways to increase farmers' incomes every year. The SP will provide two bags of DAP and five bags of urea free of cost to all small and marginal farmers. They will also receive free electricity, irrigation, interest-free loans, insurance and a pension of ₹40,000. A 'Kisan Kosh' will be established to provide emergency assistance during natural disasters. The party has said it will increase the compensation provided under farmers' insurance to ₹10 lakh. Subsidies will be provided on electricity rates for cold storages and cold chains located in rural areas. Profitable Minimum Support Price All farmers in Uttar Pradesh will be given a legal guarantee of MSP (Minimum Support Price) for all crops, including milk. The MSP will be determined on the basis of the Swaminathan formula (C2 + 50%). In the case of certain notified crops such as tomatoes, onions, potatoes and sugar, a 'price compensation mechanism' will also be established with the state government's support. A ₹10,000 crore fund will be created to ensure that sugarcane farmers are paid within 24 hours. Youth: Promises a law akin to sedition for exam paper leaks Students will be given free travel passes for roadways buses. To win over young people, the Samajwadi Party (SP) has announced that it will provide 25 lakh government jobs in five years. The SP has said it will decide at its first Cabinet meeting to immediately fill 10 lakh government posts. The BJP, meanwhile, has continued to take credit for providing 10.5 lakh jobs during its 10-year government. All graduates will be guaranteed employment through skill development. It has also promised a monthly unemployment allowance of ₹5,000 until a person finds a job. The SP had tried this strategy earlier, in 2012. At the time, a ₹1,000 unemployment allowance played a key role in bringing the SP to power. It has said that a stringent law, on the lines of the law against sedition, will be enacted to deal with paper leaks, and that an annual calendar will be prepared for state-level examinations. One-stage recruitment processes will be completed within three months, while recruitment processes involving two or three stages will be completed within six months. A waiting-list provision will be introduced for Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services examinations. There will be no contractual appointments from now on. Teachers - Old Pension Scheme to be implemented Teachers at private schools will be given an additional monthly honorarium of ₹5,000. Shiksha Mitras will receive ₹5,000 every month and will be regularised within three years. It has been announced that the Old Pension Scheme, or OPS, will be implemented for government employees. The state currently has the highest number of teachers in employment. In addition, he announced that teachers would be kept free from any work other than teaching. The Samajwadi Party had also released its manifesto before the 2022 Assembly elections. Before the 2027 elections, Akhilesh Yadav has made new moves... Expert says: Manifesto poses a challenge for the BJP Senior journalist Manmohan Agrawal says of the Samajwadi Party's manifesto, "Akhilesh has come up with the best and most popular manifesto so far. It focuses on everyone from Gen Z to women, rural residents and farmers. Through unemployment allowance, laptops and jobs, an effort has been made to connect with Gen Z." For women, the major announcements include 10 grams of gold on the birth of a girl, a ₹40,000 pension, Kanya Vidya Dhan, 300 units of free electricity for rural residents, loan waivers for farmers and payment for sugarcane within 24 hours. These directly affect a family. Several of these announcements have been made before, and the governments of Akhilesh Yadav and Mulayam Singh Yadav also fulfilled them.

stories.title: Man shot dead with four bullets at Prayagraj salon:He was getting shave before his wedding; witness in a murder case
stories.summary: A young man sitting in a salon was shot dead in Prayagraj on Thursday evening. Three attackers fired several rounds at him, and he was hit by four bullets. The young man was due to attend a wedding at his maternal aunt's house. Before that, he had come to get a shave. His family told the police that he was a witness in a murder case and had been repeatedly threatened. The incident took place at 6:30 near UCO Bank in Allahpur. See 2 pictures... Now read the full account Arvind Pasi, 32, son of Kishun Lal, was a resident of Pura Dalel in Allapur. It was his maternal aunt's wedding that day. He had gone to a salon to get a shave before attending it. At around 6.30 pm, he went to Sheru the barber's shop near UCO Bank for a shave. He was sitting at the shop when three men arrived. One of them put a country-made pistol to the barber's head. The other two began firing indiscriminately at the young man. Arvind was hit by four bullets-one in the head, one in the back, and the third and fourth near his abdomen. He fell to the ground after being injured, and the attackers fled. His family arrived first after receiving the information, followed by the police. He was taken to hospital, but doctors declared him dead on arrival. The family members said several other associates of the shooters were also present outside the salon. After hearing the sound of gunfire, people from the surrounding area gathered at the spot. The police were immediately informed about the incident. A police team reached the spot, inspected the scene and began an investigation. Arvind was the fourth of five brothers. He has a nine-year-old son. Attackers and motive behind murder remain unclear The identity of the person who killed Arvind Pasi and the reason for the murder are not yet known. The police are questioning people in the area. CCTV footage from cameras installed at and around the scene may also be examined to gather information about the route taken by the attackers and their identities. Fear of murder over old enmity On 26 September 2025, Sajan Mehtar was brutally beaten to death with bricks in Allahpur itself. The deceased, Arvind, was a witness in the case and was also pursuing the matter. It is suspected that the murder was carried out because of this old enmity. The family members said Arvind was repeatedly being stopped from testifying in Sajan Mehtar's murder case. He was being threatened to reach a compromise. Complaints were made several times to the local police station and the ACP's office, but no action was taken. DCP City Sagar Jain said that CCTV footage was being examined. A city-wide cordon has been put in place. Three police teams have been deployed to search for the killers. Regarding the allegations made by the family, he said that an FIR would be registered and further action taken on the basis of the complaint they submit.

stories.title: Minister Sandeep gets married, exchanges garlands with bride:President Droupadi Murmu attends wedding in Delhi to bless the couple
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Education Minister Sandeep Singh and his brother Saurabh got married at Delhi's Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium (JLN) on Thursday. The jaimala ceremony was held at around 7 p.m. Sandeep and Saurabh exchanged garlands with their brides. Earlier, the sehra-bandi ceremony was held at The Leela Palace. The wedding procession then set out from Gate No. 1 of JLN Stadium at around 6 p.m. Both grooms wore light cream embroidered sherwanis, paired with matching churidars and embroidered shawls. They wore peach-and-gold turbans on their heads. The brides wore heavily embroidered red and orange lehengas with turquoise borders along the lower sections. Their heads were covered with veils made of bright red dupattas. President Droupadi Murmu, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Maurya and several other leaders attended the wedding and blessed the two brothers. The reception will be held at JLN Stadium on Friday. See four pictures... Sandeep and Saurabh dance enthusiastically at mehndi and haldi ceremonies The haldi ceremony was held at the same hotel on Wednesday. Sandeep made an entrance holding his fiancée Meghna Chaudhary's hand to a Punjabi song. The two danced enthusiastically. Sandeep also showered rose petals on Meghna. Sandeep's younger brother, Saurabh Singh, also made a grand entrance with his fiancée, Antara Tyagi, to the song 'Welcome'. Father showered flowers on his sons The haldi ceremony began at 1:30 pm and continued until 5 pm. During the ceremony, singer Ishika Shengar performed songs with an orchestra. Sandeep Singh's father and former MP Rajveer Singh, also known as Raju Bhaiya, was seen in a different avatar at the haldi ceremony. He got down on one knee to give his wife flowers. The couple looked very happy at the moment. Rajveer Singh showered flower petals on his younger son Saurabh Singh and his fiancée. Other family members also took part in the ceremony. Those present celebrated enthusiastically. Both brothers mounted horses after the worship The horse-mounting ceremony for the two brothers was held on Tuesday at Raj Palace on Marris Road in Aligarh. At around 4 p.m., after prayers, Sandeep and Saurabh mounted the horses at an auspicious time. During the ceremony, their father and former MP Rajveer Singh, also known as Raju Bhaiya, danced enthusiastically with his sons. The engagement was held on 14 November Earlier, the two brothers got engaged on 14 November in Talanagari, Aligarh. A venue spread across around 100 bighas was built for the event. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, along with several senior leaders and other dignitaries, attended it. Sandeep Singh is the MLA from Atrauli. He is currently the Minister of State for Basic Education in the Uttar Pradesh government. He is the grandson of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh and the son of former MP Rajveer Singh. See 2 pictures from the engagement

stories.title: Soldier dies after falling from moving train in Sultanpur:Body severed into three parts; told wife, ‘I’m coming, I’ll take care
stories.summary: An army soldier died after falling from the Begampura Express train in Sultanpur on Thursday. The accident was so severe that his body was torn into three pieces. The soldier was returning to his home in Sonbhadra on leave to attend his sister's wedding. He had spoken to his wife for the last time two hours before the accident. He had said, "I will reach home by evening. I will take care of all the wedding arrangements." According to information, the soldier had gone to wash his face at the basin near the train door. He was pushed because of the crowd, lost his balance and fell from the train. Police who reached the spot after being informed of the accident identified the soldier on the basis of documents found in his pocket. The accident occurred at around 11 a.m. near Lambhua station. His wife, who reached the GRP police station, was distraught. She was inconsolable and kept crying. Family members comforted her. See three pictures related to the incident... Anup joined the Army in 2009 Mahesh Yadav's family lives in the Anpara-Obra area of Duddhi tehsil in Sonbhadra district. He has three sons-Anup Kumar Yadav (34), Mrityunjay and Sanjay. His eldest son, Anup, joined the Army in 2009. He married Aradhana in 2012. They have two children. Their elder son, nine-year-old Manas Yadav, and their younger son, Vayun, is 23 months old. Anup was posted with the 17th Battalion of the Rajput Regiment in the Tibri-Mukerian area of Gurdaspur, Punjab. Anup's cousin, Anshu Yadav, is getting married on 30 November. To attend the wedding, Anup had taken leave from 25 November to 15 January. His head and one arm were severed and fell some distance away Anoop boarded the Begumpura Express from Lucknow to Varanasi on Thursday. According to information, during the journey he went to wash his face at the basin near the train door. At that moment, he lost his footing after being jolted and fell from the train. In the accident, Anoop's head was severed and fell away from the tracks, while one of his hands was also severed. Passers-by spotted the body and informed railway employees After the train had passed, passers-by walking along the track saw the body and informed railway staff. The RPF and GRP then reached the spot. Anoop was identified on the basis of the driving licence and Aadhaar card found in his pocket. The GRP sent the body for post-mortem. He spoke to his wife 2 hours before his death His maternal cousin Anand Kumar Yadav said Anoop was like an elder brother to him. He was posted with the Rajput Battalion. He fell from the train while going to wash his face during the journey. Anoop last spoke to his wife at around 9 a.m.

stories.title: Father and two children die in Etah pickup truck collision:Family was on a bike to collect clothes
stories.summary: A father and his two innocent children died after writhing in agony on the road in Etah. The three were travelling on a motorcycle when a pickup truck hit them from behind. The impact was so forceful that the pickup broke through a tree before plunging into a ditch. A police investigation found that the father was taking both children to buy clothes. The accident occurred near Ulayatpur village in the Kotwali Dehat police station area. Daughter was 5 years old, and the son was 3 According to police, Tejveer (30) lives with his family in Kathauli village. On Thursday, he was going to buy jackets for his children. His daughter Geeta (five) and son Yuvraj (three) were also riding his Splendor motorcycle. Children writhed by the roadside before losing consciousness Eyewitnesses said that Tejveer was travelling towards Vahanpur when a speeding pickup hit the motorcycle from behind. The impact threw Tejveer face-first onto the road. He did not get up after losing consciousness. The two children, meanwhile, lost consciousness after writhing in pain for some time. Passers-by took Tejveer and both children to Veerangana Avanti Bai Medical College for treatment. Doctors declared all three dead. Police also reached the hospital after receiving the information. They then informed the family and sent all three bodies for post-mortem examinations. Police said the pickup driver fled the scene. The vehicle has been taken into custody and efforts are being made to trace him.

stories.title: Two burnt alive after truck-trailer collision sparks fire:Sonbhadra police recovers bodies from wreckage; smoke visible from 3 km away
stories.summary: Two people were burnt to death after a truck and a trailer collided in Sonbhadra. Police recovered their charred bodies from the wreckage. The dead were the truck driver and a motorcyclist. The truck driver's body was so badly burnt that only the skeleton above the waist remained. According to eyewitnesses, there was a loud explosion after the collision. Both vehicles then caught fire. The truck driver was trapped inside. A motorcyclist was caught between the truck and the trailer and was also burnt to death. Two other people were injured in the accident. The accident took place at around 2:30 p.m. on Thursday near the Sukrit outpost of Robertsganj Kotwali. See two pictures of the accident Now, here are the full details CO Randhir Mishra said, "One truck was travelling from the Robertsganj side, while the other was coming from the Varanasi side. Both trucks were travelling in their respective lanes." Meanwhile, the tyre of a truck travelling towards Banaras suddenly burst. The truck veered out of control into the other lane and collided with a truck coming from the opposite direction. Both vehicles caught fire in the collision. Truck driver and motorcyclist burnt alive According to the police, trailer driver Abhay (35), a resident of Lalpur Naudiha in Mirzapur, died in the accident. An unidentified motorcyclist was also burnt alive. Two people, including helper Golu (18), a resident of Lalpur, were seriously injured in the accident. Eyewitness Amit Kumar Sonkar said, "There was a powerful explosion in both vehicles after the collision. They then caught fire. Both vehicles began burning fiercely. The plume of smoke rising from the fire was visible from around 3 kilometres away." People rescued by breaking the glass Eyewitness Amit said that after the accident, people nearby tried to rescue those trapped in the vehicles. One person was pulled out after the truck's glass was broken, while some others were also dragged out. A motorcyclist was also caught in the fire during the accident. He was crying out in pain. Around four people are feared to have died in the accident. Circle Officer Randhir Mishra said- After the accident, the police immediately called the Fire Service and Traffic Police teams to the spot. The two people injured in the accident were sent to hospital for treatment.

stories.title: BJP MLA’s election cancelled in UP:Hid income in affidavit; High Court delivers verdict four months before polls
stories.summary: Allahabad High Court has cancelled the election of BJP MLA Om Kumar in Uttar Pradesh. He had provided incorrect information about his income in the affidavit submitted while filing his nomination papers. Om Kumar won the 2022 Assembly election from the Nahatour seat in Bijnor, securing his third consecutive victory. He defeated Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) candidate Munshi Ram by 258 votes. Munshi Ram, who finished second, filed a petition in the High Court alleging that the MLA had concealed his income. After hearing the case, a bench led by Justice Salil Kumar Rai on Thursday ordered the cancellation of Om Kumar’s election. The bench has given him 15 days to appeal against the verdict in the Supreme Court. Even if the MLA does not get relief from the Supreme Court, no by-election will be held in the Nahatour constituency. This is because by-elections are not conducted when less than six months remain before the next general Assembly election. He had also sought a recount of votes; decision still awaited Petitioner Munshi Ram said Om Kumar had not disclosed the details of his sources of income in the nomination form and had concealed his earnings. Several columns in the nomination form were also left incomplete. The court declared his nomination invalid and cancelled his election. The court's order runs to around 400 pages. Munshi Ram had also sought a recount of votes, but no decision on that plea has been announced yet. Defeated RLD candidate by 258 votes The 2022 Assembly election in the Nahatour constituency saw a close contest between the BJP and the RLD. BJP candidate Om Kumar secured 77,935 votes, while RLD candidate Munshi Ram received 77,677 votes. Om Kumar won by a narrow margin of 258 votes, securing his third consecutive victory. BSP candidate Priya Singh finished third with 38,020 votes. After his defeat, RLD candidate Munshi Ram, who finished second, filed a petition in the High Court, alleging that Om Kumar had won through corrupt practices. Won three consecutive elections since 2012; first victory was on BSP ticket Om Kumar, who has now lost his Assembly membership, first won the election in 2012 on a BSP ticket. He defeated BJP candidate Rajkumar by 19,398 votes. However, before the 2017 Assembly elections, he joined the BJP, which fielded him as its candidate. He defeated Congress candidate Munna Lal Premi by 23,151 votes. The BJP fielded him again in 2022. This time, he defeated RLD candidate Munshi Lal by 258 votes to secure his third consecutive victory. BJP fielded him from Nagina in 2024 In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP fielded Om Kumar from the Nagina reserved constituency. However, he lost to Chandrashekhar, national president of the Azad Samaj Party.

stories.title: Man dies en route to brother's funeral, wife also killed:Bike hits flyover railing in Mainpuri, three family deaths
stories.summary: A husband and wife died in a road accident in Mainpuri. They were travelling to Hardoi for the funeral of the husband's younger brother. Nimesh (22), had died on Wednesday (25 Nov) night after a prolonged illness. As soon as his elder brother Amit Kumar, 32, who lived in Haryana, received the news, he set off for home on a motorcycle with his wife Pinky, 28. Near the Fatehjangpur flyover, the speeding motorcycle went out of control and collided with the railing. The impact was so severe that both of them were thrown onto the road. Amit suffered a fatal head injury and died at the spot, while Pinky died in hospital. Police have placed the bodies in the mortuary for post-mortem examinations. The accident took place at 6 a.m. on Thursday (26 Nov) on National Highway 34 in the Kurawali police station area. The younger son's funeral bier had been prepared at home. Meanwhile, news arrived that the elder son and daughter-in-law had died. The family was overcome with grief. The couple's two children, daughter Ayesha, 14, and son Asmit, seven, were inconsolable. Relatives kept comforting them. No bus was available, so they set off on a motorcycle Two children lose both parents Amit and Pinky had married around 15 years ago. They had two children. The house where preparations were under way for the last rites of Amit's younger brother Nimesh is now steeped in mourning over three deaths. The cause of the accident has not yet been established. Police are examining CCTV footage.

stories.title: Akhilesh promises 10gm gold for every newborn girl:SP manifesto offers ₹5,000 monthly unemployment allowance to youth, 300 units of free electricity in villages
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav released the party's manifesto on Thursday. It promises to give up to 10 grams of gold on the birth of a girl child. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay had also promised to give gold to newborns and brides during the election campaign. His party later formed the government. The SP has also announced a monthly unemployment allowance of ₹5,000 for youth, an annual pension of ₹40,000 for elderly women and salaries equal to those of regular teachers for 1.5 lakh Shiksha Mitras (contractual teachers). The party has also promised health insurance cover of up to ₹10 lakh for poor families, reopening of closed schools and efforts to restore the old pension scheme. Akhilesh said ASHA workers, Anganwadi workers and contractual employees would be given better salaries. He also promised to work towards making their jobs permanent. Akhilesh brings back 2022 promises with new packages for 2027 Akhilesh has included several promises made in 2022 in the 2027 manifesto as well. These include farm loan waivers, MSP for crops, employment, and pensions. However, the financial assistance promised under some schemes has been increased this time. For instance, in 2022, the party had promised an annual pension of ₹18,000 for women in need. In 2027, it has promised an annual pension of ₹40,000 for elderly women, labourers and artisans. BJP says Akhilesh should answer for his past record In Maharajganj, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary said, "Writing good governance on the pages of a manifesto does not change history. Akhilesh Yadav must also answer for his party's past actions and record."

stories.title: Raja Bhaiya's party fields three candidates:Raja Bhaiya from Kunda, Kuldeep Patel from Vishwanathganj, and Vinod Saroj from Babaganj
stories.summary: Jansatta Dal Loktantrik has released its first list of candidates for three seats in the 2027 Assembly elections in Pratapgarh. The party has fielded its national president, Raghuraj Pratap Singh, alias Raja Bhaiya, from Kunda. According to the list released in Pratapgarh, Raghuraj Pratap Singh, alias Raja Bhaiya, will contest from the 246 Kunda seat, Vinod Saroj from the 245 Babaganj seat and Kuldeep Patel from the 247 Vishwanathganj seat. Following Kuldeep Patel's candidature, discussion has begun in the district over the Vishwanathganj seat. The party has given the ticket to a candidate from the Patel community for this seat. Political discussions see this as part of the party's strategy to balance social equations. Kuldeep Patel is the husband of Pratapgarh Zila Panchayat chairperson Madhuri Patel. His candidature is being discussed in the district's political circles. Following the release of the first list, attention will now also focus on the potential candidates for the other Assembly seats and the party's strategy. So far, the party has announced the names of candidates for three seats.

stories.title: Alok Singh appointed chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service:All 4 recruitment boards now headed by IPS officers
stories.summary: The Yogi government has appointed IPS officer Alok Singh as the new chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC). The government issued an order in this regard on Thursday afternoon. The commission's outgoing chairman, Sanjay Sreenet, retired on November 21. Alok Singh, a 1995-batch IPS officer, is currently the Director General of the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC). He also holds the charge of Director General of the Uttar Pradesh Special Police. Singh is due to retire in January 2027. Dainik Bhaskar reported four days ago that Alok Singh would be appointed chairman. However, he will continue as the commission's chairman for two years even after his retirement. With Singh's appointment, all four recruitment boards in the state are now headed by IPS officers. The Subordinate Services Selection Commission is already headed by former DGP Satya Narayan Sabat, the Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission by former DGP Prashant Kumar, and the Police Recruitment and Promotion Board by DGP SB Shiradkar. Alok Singh was Noida's first Police Commissioner Alok Singh was the first Police Commissioner of Noida (Gautam Buddh Nagar). He was appointed to the post in January 2020. He has also served as ADG of the Kanpur Zone, IG of the Meerut Range, and SSP and IG of Kanpur. He has received several medals during his police service. Alok Singh has been awarded the Police Medal for Gallantry (PMG) in 2003, Police Medal for Meritorious Service (PM) in 2012, President's Police Medal for Distinguished Service (PPM) in 2021, Medal for Excellence in Service in 2020, and Ati Uttam Seva Medal in 2026. UPPSC conducts 15,000-20,000 recruitments every year The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) conducts around 15,000 to 20,000 recruitments every year. It is also responsible for conducting prestigious examinations such as the Provincial Civil Services (PCS) and PCS-Judicial examinations. Apart from these, the commission also conducts recruitment examinations for posts such as Review Officer (RO), Assistant Review Officer (ARO), Tehsildar, electricity department and health department positions, Naib Tehsildar and Assistant Regional Transport Officer (ARTO). Why is the government placing its trust in IPS officers? Experts believe that appointing IPS officers as chairpersons of recruitment commissions and boards has proved successful. Their appointment keeps police chiefs and district magistrates alert and reduces the chances of irregularities in examinations. Earlier, IAS officers were appointed to these commissions, but their tenure was relatively less effective. During the tenure of former chairman Praveer Kumar at the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission, the pace of work had slowed down considerably.

stories.title: Ghaziabad woman poisons husband, son and nephew for ₹6 crore:Mixes lead in food; named nominee in ₹2 crore insurance policy
stories.summary: Police have arrested 42-year-old Renu Bhatnagar in connection with the alleged attempt to kill her husband, son, and nephew by slowly poisoning them in Indirapuram, Ghaziabad. For nearly a year, she had been mixing small quantities of lead powder into the food of the three family members. During police questioning, Renu admitted to poisoning her husband. Police said Renu wanted to take control of her husband Sushil Kumar Bhatnagar's travel business. The business has an annual turnover of around ₹5 crore to ₹6 crore. In addition, there is a ₹2 crore life insurance policy in Sushil's name, with Renu as the nominee. Police said she targeted her husband, son and nephew out of greed for the business and insurance money. Sushil is a resident of Vasundhara. He filed a complaint alleging a conspiracy to murder against his wife Renu, mother-in-law Lata Saxena, brother-in-law Ravi Saxena, co-brother Sushil Girdhar and acquaintance Bablu. Police are also investigating the role of the other people named in the case. Blood test reveals high lead levels; stays in hospital for two months Travel businessman Sushil said, "My health suddenly deteriorated severely on 21 August 2025. I had a blood test at a private diagnostic centre, which found that the lead level in my body was much higher than normal. I was then admitted to Max Hospital in Vaishali. I remained in hospital for around two months. As my condition became critical, I also had to be kept in the ICU." After treatment, the doctors told me that I had developed chronic lead poisoning because of the presence of lead in my body. Prolonged exposure to lead had caused the poison to start spreading through my body. After I was discharged from the hospital, my health deteriorated again that same year, and I had to be admitted once more. Over the next few months, my son Vansh (16) and my nephew Dev Bhatnagar (21) also fell ill. It took all three of us several weeks to recover. After medical reports confirmed lead poisoning in all three cases, Sushil began suspecting his wife, Renu. Mum kept my food and hers separately According to Trans Hindon DCP Rijul, Sushil initially had no concrete evidence against Renu. In the first week of September 2026, their 12-year-old daughter told me that her mother, Renu, would set aside portions of food for herself and me before serving it. She would then sprinkle something on the food served to the other family members. When Sushil asked Renu about this, she did not respond. She then went to her sister's house in Delhi. On 24 September, Sushil filed a complaint at the Indirapuram police station. Based on the complaint, police registered an FIR against Renu under Sections 109 (attempt to murder), 123 (causing harm by administering poison or an intoxicating substance) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The complaint also named Renu's mother, Lata Saxena, brother Ravi Saxena, brother-in-law Sushil Girdhar and acquaintance Bablu. The DCP said police recorded the statements of the girl and the doctors. The medical reports of all three victims were also examined. During the preliminary investigation, police found evidence indicating that Renu had been poisoning her husband, son, and nephew's food between 2024 and 2025. She wanted to kill her husband and nephew and take control of the business During police questioning, Renu said she wanted complete control of her husband's travel business. To achieve this, she had planned to kill Sushil and her nephew Dev. Dev oversaw the business. Renu also targeted her son Vansh because he always supported his father. Police said Renu regularly mixed small quantities of lead into the food of her husband, son and nephew. Renu was also the nominee on Sushil's life insurance policy worth ₹2 crore. ACP Abhay Daga said Renu admitted to slowly poisoning her husband out of greed for his property and insurance. Lead is used at her father's jewellery shop The police investigation has revealed that Renu's father runs a jewellery shop. Lead is used there for work related to metal casting. The police are also investigating whether the accused obtained the lead from this shop or arranged it from elsewhere. According to the police, Renu threw the poison into a dustbin somewhere before leaving her husband's home in September. The police registered a case and launched an investigation based on a complaint received on 24 September. The accused, Renu Bhatnagar, was arrested on 24 November from Jhilmil Colony in Vivek Vihar, Delhi. She was at her sister's house. The police took her into custody after launching an investigation based on the complaint. Prolonged exposure to lead can damage organs Doctors said lead is a toxic metal. Even prolonged exposure to small amounts can cause serious harm. The early symptoms of chronic lead poisoning are often not clear. During this time, lead continues to accumulate in the body and gradually affects several organs. Its symptoms may appear after several weeks, months, or even years. It mainly damages the digestive system, nervous system, heart, and reproductive system. Its effects may vary depending on a person's age. Dr Sanjay Tyotia, former CMS of Sanjay Nagar Hospital in Ghaziabad, said that excessive lead in the body can also cause death. If its level in the body is very high or treatment is delayed, the patient may suffer seizures. The patient may slip into a coma and suffer permanent brain damage. A case similar to Kerala's Koodathayi cyanide murder case This case in Ghaziabad is similar to Kerala's Koodathayi cyanide murder case. In that case, Jolly Joseph was accused of murdering six members of her family between 2002 and 2016. The victims included her mother-in-law, Annamma Thomas; father-in-law, Tom Thomas; first husband, Roy Thomas; Annamma's brother, Matthew Manjadiyil; Sily; and her two-year-old daughter, Alphine. Investigators alleged that Jolly poisoned five people by mixing cyanide into food or drinks. For Annamma's murder, she allegedly used a veterinary poison sold under the name "Dog Kill". Police suspected that property disputes and her desire to marry Sili's husband could have been behind the killings. Jolly was arrested in October 2019. Six murder cases have been registered against her. She is currently in jail as an undertrial prisoner, and the trial is ongoing.

stories.title: Azam says 'We will fight till death':Akhilesh should spend 6 months in jail to understand our pain
stories.summary: “Me, my son and my wife… under normal circumstances, we should have died. But we proved to be tough survivors. Now I feel that when we die, we will die only after doing something.” “Today, I wish Akhilesh could also spend six months in jail so that he would know the truth about how the days pass and nights are spent there. What more can I say…” SP leader Azam Khan made these remarks ahead of the Samajwadi Party's manifesto launch. After being released from jail, Azam arrived in Lucknow for his first public event. He shared his pain from the stage in the presence of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. He told Akhilesh that the people who were troubling him today had been given prominence by Akhilesh himself. Key points from Azam's speech 1. Seeing his son in jail was the biggest punishment Recalling his time in prison, Azam said staying in solitary confinement was not as difficult as seeing his son behind bars. He said the hours before he learnt that his son was alive and lodged in Hardoi jail were extremely difficult. 2. Used to pray for death every night Azam said he would pray to Allah every night that if a morning filled with sorrow was approaching, he should not live to see it. He would go to sleep praying for death. “Death was very cheap… but the life we spent in jail was very expensive,” he said. 3. Sentenced for stealing a hen, but never even got the hen Referring to the hen theft case, Azam spoke about his 21-year prison sentence and a fine of ₹36 lakh. He said strict legal provisions were invoked against him in the theft case, resulting in a harsh punishment. “If I had stolen a hen, I would at least have got the hen. Here, I did not even get the hen,” he said. 4. Targeted Owaisi and Chandrashekhar without naming them Azam indirectly targeted Chandrashekhar and Asaduddin Owaisi, saying their objectives were very limited. He alleged that their aim was to disrupt someone else's growing political prospects. “This is a very small target. They have been assigned this very task,” he said. He also described himself as someone who helps bring votes together, rather than someone who cuts into another party's vote share. 5. BJP is neither for this world nor the next Targeting the BJP government, Azam said those who had harmed Indian politics, democracy and weaker sections of society could never succeed. He said such people belonged neither to this world nor the next. 6. A manifesto is not a book from heaven Speaking about the Samajwadi Party's manifesto, Azam said, “This is not just a manifesto. It is not some book from heaven that only what has been written will happen. When the time comes, even things that have not been written will happen.” Referred to Mulayam, sent a message to the SP Chandrashekhar stabbed us in the back; making two or four candidates lose is all he is capable of Earlier, speaking about the alliance between Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad, Azam said, “I have tried not to make them worthy of much discussion. Their objective is very small — they just want to make two or four candidates lose, which is all they are capable of.” He added that people could identify and understand those who were harming the country. Azam said some people joined them because of their silver and gold coins. He added that the MP from Bijnor had suffered a major loss by associating with them. “He is our younger brother, and we love him. But he has ended his political career because the very people who gave him strength have used that strength to stab us in the back,” he said. The SP leader said nobody should assume that they could harm him or weaker sections of society to achieve their limited objectives. “We were helpless because we were in jail, and that was when the foxes started crossing the Ganga. The river was dry then. Now the Ganga is flowing. People are very troubled. They are tired of Hindu-Muslim conflicts. No matter how big your claims are, the truth has reached people's hearts,” he said. Azam was released from Ghaziabad's Dasna jail on November 18. He had been released from Rampur jail on October 31, 2026, but was subsequently arrested in connection with an Enforcement Directorate (ED) case. Azam had said, ‘One day, we will visit Nagina’ Earlier, on Wednesday, Azam was asked in Rampur about the impact of the Owaisi-Chandrashekhar combination on Uttar Pradesh politics. In a light-hearted response, he said, “What are you talking about? One day, we will go to Nagina and tell the people there, as well as the people across the country.” On seat-sharing with Congress, says ‘Leave it to the seniors’ On seat-sharing with the Congress, Azam said deciding the matter was not his responsibility. “It would be better to leave it to our seniors,” he said. When asked whether he would contest the elections, Azam said, “Who can stop me from contesting elections? My election is my bicycle. The bicycle will contest and the bicycle will win. We cannot see anything other than the bicycle.”

stories.title: Owaisi says people will not fall prey to Akhilesh’s betrayal:Holds first show of strength with Chandrashekhar; rally draws 1 lakh people
stories.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad held a major rally in Lucknow on Thursday, drawing a crowd of more than one lakh people. AIMIM chief Owaisi said, “Akhilesh Yadav has taken everything away from Muslims and reduced them to a mere vote bank. Your presence in such large numbers sends a message to the Samajwadi leader that people will no longer fall prey to his betrayal.” He said, “Abdul will no longer just lay carpets. He will make Chandrashekhar the Chief Minister.” Challenging Samajwadi Party and Congress leaders, Owaisi said, “Compete with me in a speech. I will leave you speechless and send you back within five minutes.” He added, “If speaking the truth and raising one's voice for the rights of the poor is considered incitement, then I will continue to do so.” Nagina MP Chandrashekhar said his party would provide women with a monthly assistance of ₹25,000 if it came to power. He said justice would be delivered through the Constitution, not bulldozers. “If Chandrashekhar becomes Chief Minister, Abdul will become Deputy Chief Minister. We will also appoint a leader from the backward community as Deputy Chief Minister,” he stated. First joint appearance on a major stage after alliance Key points from Owaisi's speech 1. “I would rather die than remain silent in the face of oppression” Addressing the 'Bahujan Swaraj Sankalp Maha Rally', Owaisi said, “You attackers fired bullets at me. You also fired at Chandrashekhar. We would rather die than remain silent in the face of such oppression. We have come forward to bring change. I also want to say that two people are responsible for spreading hatred in this country and Uttar Pradesh: Modi and Yogi.” 2. Owaisi accuses Akhilesh of pushing Muslims to the margins Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi launched a sharp attack on Akhilesh Yadav, alleging that he wanted Muslim votes without giving the community adequate political representation. He accused the Samajwadi Party leader of promoting dynastic politics and pushing Muslims to the margins. 3. “Akhilesh will talk about socialism but promote nepotism” Owaisi said, “You must have heard 'Bhaiya' say these things, in Yogi's words: 'love', hatred and nepotism. These people will talk about socialism but promote nepotism. They will invoke Ram Manohar Lohia's name but work for the benefit of their own families. I appeal to you to use every single vote wisely.”

stories.title: ‘Some people are spreading misinformation with red booklets in hands’:Yogi says these are very people who strangled the Constitution; warns people to remain cautious
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday launched beautification works under the Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme at Lok Bhavan in Lucknow on Constitution Pride Day. Addressing the event, he said 4,029 sites had been identified across the state, of which work would begin at 3,955 on Wednesday. Criticises those carrying 'red booklet' Without naming the Opposition, Yogi said, "Some people are carrying a 'red booklet' in their hands and trying to spread confusion and weaken constitutional institutions and democracy. There is a need to remain vigilant against them." He added, "If such people had read a copy of the Constitution, they would not have claimed to be protectors of India's sovereignty." Questions past amendments to Constitution The Chief Minister said that when these people had an opportunity, they would not have attempted to "strangle" the Constitution. "After Independence, we would not have made the first amendment to the Constitution by holding press freedom hostage, nor would we have had the audacity to amend the Constitution from time to time for our own interests," he said. Yogi further alleged that these people had repeatedly attempted to put both the Constitution and constitutional institutions in the dock. He further said, "They attempted to put India's democracy in the dock, repeatedly levelled allegations against India and carried out every conspiracy to endanger democracy-actions they continue to pursue even today." On this occasion, I want to say to everyone that whether it is an individual, society, caste or country, if it cannot take pride in its great figures and heritage and cannot make its present glorious, its future too will be bleak. Modi Decided to Mark November 26 as Constitution Day Yogi said the Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949, and every adult Indian was granted the right to vote from the very beginning, without discrimination based on caste, region, language or gender. "In 2015, on Baba Saheb's 125th birth anniversary, Prime Minister Narendra Modi decided to observe November 26 as Constitution Day. The words 'We, the people of India' in the Preamble make it clear that sovereignty rests not with any individual, family or particular caste, but with ordinary citizens," he said. Referring to the illustrations in the original copy of the Constitution, created by Acharya Nandalal Bose and Ram Manohar Sinha, Yogi said they depicted figures such as Lord Ram, Lord Krishna, Gautama Buddha and Emperor Ashoka, reflecting how the Constitution honoured India's heritage. Yogi said - Uttar Pradesh had the highest number of members in the Constituent Assembly... Yogi Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh had the highest number of members in the Constituent Assembly, with 55, while six of the 15 women members were from the state. They included Sucheta Kriplani, Govind Ballabh Pant, Purushottam Das Tandon and Acharya Narendra Dev. He said the double-engine government had struck a balance between development and heritage. As part of this, a statue of Ahilyabai Holkar has been installed at the Kashi Vishwanath Dham, Ayodhya airport has been named after Maharishi Valmiki, and connectivity works have been carried out at ChÄ«r Govardhan, the birthplace of Sant Ravidas.

Without naming Yogi Adityanath, Kharge said: "Another leader has emerged in Lucknow, and he is now eyeing the Prime Minister's chair. Shah is also eyeing the Prime Minister's chair, but Modi does not want to give it up. We would advise him to step down now." Praising Imran Masood's enthusiasm, Kharge also advised him to follow coalition discipline. He said, "Our Imran Masood speaks with great enthusiasm. I watch him on TV every day. But we have to do more than just talk. The more we work together, the further we will progress. Imran is in Parliament and always fights for the party. He puts up a fight and tries to get his point across." Kharge has arrived in Lucknow to participate in the Congress's 'Save the Constitution March'. However, the administration has not granted permission for the march. UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said that Congress workers would take out the march after Kharge leaves. He added that they would not clash with the police but would sit down wherever they were stopped.

stories.title: Congress unhappy with Samajwadi Party's separate manifesto:Rajendra Pal says, 'Joint manifesto will be released if alliance is formed'
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress have started facing differences over their proposed alliance ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Congress has expressed displeasure over the SP preparing to release a separate manifesto. Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said that since talks between the two parties were underway, there was no need to rush into making separate announcements or declaring seats. He said both parties should take decisions through mutual agreement. Says joint manifesto will be released if alliance is formed Rajendra Pal Gautam said Congress was also preparing its manifesto. The party has held discussions with different sections of society, including farmers, youth, labourers, students and women, to understand their concerns and include their issues. He said the manifesto draft was ready, but the party was waiting for the INDIA alliance talks to conclude. He clarified that if an alliance is finalised in Uttar Pradesh, both parties will jointly release a manifesto. If no agreement is reached, Congress will finalise its existing draft and present it to the public. Questions urgency behind SP's seat announcements The Congress in-charge also questioned the SP's announcement of seats. He said there was no need to rush into declaring seats when discussions between the two parties were still underway. He added that it would have been better for both parties to take decisions through mutual agreement. Urges leaders of both parties to respect alliance commitments Rajendra Pal Gautam appealed to leaders of both SP and Congress to exercise restraint. He said they should avoid making remarks against each other that could affect alliance talks and their mutual relations. He also stressed that leaders should respect public sentiments while dealing with each other. He said any decision on the alliance would be taken keeping in mind the interests of the public, the country and Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: 'Try forming your govt in Hyderabad':Hoardings target Owaisi in Lucknow, urging him to 'Leave us to our fate'
stories.summary: With the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections scheduled for 2027, political activity is beginning to gather pace. Hoardings opposing AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi have appeared at several locations in Lucknow on Constitution Day. The messages urge him to return to Hyderabad and stop contesting elections in other states. They also appeal to him to leave Muslims to manage their own affairs. The hoardings have come up ahead of a joint rally by the AIMIM and the Azad Samaj Party. Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party chief Chandrashekhar Azad are scheduled to attend the rally. The messages have triggered discussions in political circles. 'Do not contest elections in other states' One hoarding reads: Owaisi sahib, if you genuinely want us to be happy and progress, you should not contest elections in any other state. Allah has blessed you abundantly over the years. Now, please stop. Another appeals to him to leave Muslims alone, saying: Owaisi sahib, for Allah's sake, please leave us to our own affairs. We were happy when you were in Hyderabad. Our religious places were safe. 'Try to form your own government in Hyderabad' A third hoarding urges Owaisi to remain silent in the interest of Muslims and focus on forming a government in Hyderabad. It reads: “Owaisi sahib, please have mercy on Muslims. If you want Muslims across the country to be happy and progress, then remain silent. Try to form your own government in Hyderabad.” No organisation named on the hoardings None of the hoardings carries the name of an individual or political party responsible for putting them up. They only mention “Ummat-e-Muslima (the entire Muslim community)” at the bottom. The identity of those behind the messages remains unknown. Their appearance ahead of the joint rally has triggered political discussion in Lucknow.

stories.title: Bahubali Udaybhan Karwariya daughter to become daughter-in-law of ‘Tiwari Hata’:Set to marry Vinay Shankar Tiwari’s son after the elections
stories.summary: The daughter of Prayagraj Bahubali Udaybhan Karwariya is set to become the daughter-in-law of Gorakhpur's prominent 'Tiwari Hata'. Kadarp Shankar Tiwari, son of former MLA Vinay Shankar Tiwari, got engaged to Sakshi on Wednesday. The engagement ceremony was held in Dehradun in the presence of close family members. Photographs from the event surfaced on Thursday (26 Nov). 'Tiwari Hata' is the name popularly given to the residence of former MLA Vinay Shankar Tiwari's father, the late Bahubali Harishankar Tiwari, in Gorakhpur. Couple exchanges rings, elders bless them Kadarp and Sakshi walked onto the stage holding hands. Kadarp wore a safari suit, while Sakshi was dressed in a sari. The couple exchanged rings and received blessings from their elders. Before the engagement, Sakshi's god-bharai ceremony was also held. Women from Kadarp's family draped a chunari over her, applied a tilak and presented her with gifts. Vinay Shankar Tiwari and Udaybhan Karwariya were also seen together at the ceremony. Wedding planned after 2027 Assembly elections Kadarp is the son of former Chillupar MLA Vinay Shankar Tiwari and runs a construction business. Sakshi is Udaybhan Karwariya's younger daughter. The two families have planned the wedding after the 2027 Assembly elections. See the engagement pictures- Talk of the relationship had been going on for a long time Speculation about a possible alliance between the Tiwari Hata and Karwariya families had been doing the rounds for some time, but neither side had confirmed the reports. There were also claims that the match had fallen through. However, discussions between the two families continued. On Wednesday, Kandarp and Sakshi exchanged rings at a private family function in Dehradun. stories.title: Prisoner dies by suicide at Lucknow's Adarsh Jail:Body found hanging in bathroom; serving life sentence for wife's murder, 2 jail staff suspended
stories.summary: A prisoner serving a life sentence for murdering his wife died by suicide at Lucknow's Adarsh Jail. His body was found hanging in a bathroom behind his barrack on Wednesday morning. He had allegedly made a noose by tearing a bedsheet. The incident came to light when jail staff found one prisoner missing during the morning headcount and began searching for him. The jail administration informed the police and the prisoner's family. Police took custody of the body and sent it for a post-mortem examination. Following allegations of negligence in the incident, the jail administration suspended two staff members. Disciplinary proceedings have also been initiated against another jail warder. Shifted to Adarsh jail on October 29 Raju, also known as Abbas and Aslam (32), was originally from Bankati in Lalganj, Basti district, and lived in Harola, Sector 20, Noida. Gautam Buddh Nagar Police had arrested him in connection with his wife's murder and filed a chargesheet against him in court. Following the trial, the court convicted him and sentenced him to life imprisonment. He was subsequently transferred to Adarsh Jail in Lucknow on October 29. Found missing during second headcount 15 minutes later Jailer Rajesh Singh said the regular headcount was conducted at around 6 am on Wednesday, when all prisoners were present. However, during another headcount around 15 minutes later, Raju was found missing. Jail staff then began searching for him. During the search, he was found hanging from a noose made of a bedsheet tied to a pipe in the bathroom behind the barrack. He had torn the bedsheet and used a portion of it to make the noose. Jail staff immediately brought him down and called a doctor. After examining him, the doctor declared him dead. Deputy jailer and warder suspended The jail administration has taken action following the prisoner's death. Deputy Jailer Madan Gopal, who was in charge of unlocking the barracks, and Jail Warder Rajesh Kumar, who was responsible for the barrack, have been suspended. Disciplinary proceedings have also been initiated against Jail Warder Atiq Ahmed. Action against all three is part of the process to fix responsibility for the incident.

stories.title: BTech graduate preparing for UPSC dies by suicide in Shahjahanpur:25-year-old used father's licensed revolver; both parents are govt teachers
stories.summary: A 25-year-old BTech graduate died by suicide after shooting himself in Shahjahanpur. On Wednesday night, he allegedly used his father's licensed revolver to shoot himself in the temple. The bullet passed through his head. Hearing the gunshot, his parents rushed into the room and found Shashwat lying in a pool of blood. The family immediately took him to the medical college, where doctors declared him dead. The deceased was identified as Shashwat Sharma. His father, Pradeep Sharma (45), and mother, Mridula Sharma (38), are government teachers at a Sanskrit school. His elder brother, Shivansh Sharma, works at the State Bank of India (SBI) and is married. He also has a younger sister who is still studying. The incident took place in Shastri Nagar, under the Sadar Bazar police station area. 2 pictures... Was preparing for UPSC after completing BTech His father, Pradeep Sharma, said Shashwat completed his BTech from ABS College in Ghaziabad last year. He was living in Noida and preparing for the UPSC examination. He had come home during Diwali and had been staying there since then. Went to his room after birthday party and shot himself A birthday party was organised at the house on Wednesday for his brother Shivansh's daughter, Pinky. Relatives and guests had also attended the celebration. After the party ended, Shashwat suddenly went into his room. He took his father's licensed revolver from the cupboard and shot himself in the temple. Was depressed; family had planned to take him to a doctor The family said Shashwat was under stress over his studies and future employment. His mental health was not good. On the morning of November 24, Shashwat had called the family from Noida and informed them that he was coming to Shahjahanpur. He set off by bus. However, when the bus broke down on the way, he continued his journey on foot. His mobile phone was switched off during the journey. When the family could not trace his location, they lodged a missing person complaint with the police. After searching for him, the family brought him back to Shahjahanpur. The family had decided to take him to a doctor on Wednesday. However, as his niece's birthday party was being held at home, they planned to visit the doctor on Thursday. SP City Devendra Singh said, The young man died by suicide after shooting himself with a licensed revolver. The body has been sent for post-mortem. The family has said that he was under mental stress. The matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Saryu-Kamala Express to start running on November 28:Train to pass through Gorakhpur, making travel between Nepal and Ayodhya easier
stories.summary: The Saryu-Kamala Express, aimed at strengthening rail connectivity between India and Nepal, will begin regular operations from November 28. The train will run between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya Cantt in Uttar Pradesh. The weekly train, numbered 15595/15596, will pass through Gorakhpur, Basti and Mankapur. It will depart from Janakpur Dham every Saturday and from Ayodhya Cantt every Monday. The service will provide direct rail connectivity between Janakpur Dham and Ayodhya, making travel easier for pilgrims visiting the two religious destinations as well as other passengers. The North Eastern Railway released the train timetable on Wednesday. Train to leave Janakpur on Saturday afternoon and reach Ayodhya on Sunday morning Train No. 15595, the Janakpur Dham-Ayodhya Cantt Saryu-Kamala Express, will depart from Janakpur Dham at 1:10 pm every Saturday from November 28. It will reach Jainagar at 3:10 pm Indian time. The train will then pass through Madhubani at 3:50 pm, Shisho at 5:15 pm, Sitamarhi at 7:05 pm, Raxaul at 9:40 pm and Narkatiaganj at 11:20 pm. The train will reach Gorakhpur at 4:05 am on Sunday. It will depart from Basti at 5:22 am and reach Mankapur at 6:30 am. After leaving Ayodhya Dham Junction at 7:30 am, it will arrive at Ayodhya Cantt at 8:10 am. Return journey to begin on Monday evening, reaching Janakpur on Tuesday In the return direction, Train No. 15596, the Ayodhya Cantt-Janakpur Dham Express, will depart from Ayodhya Cantt at 5:50 pm every Monday from November 30. It will reach Ayodhya Dham Junction at 6:25 pm and Mankapur at 7:32 pm. The train will then arrive at Basti at 8:40 pm and Gorakhpur at 10:23 pm. On Tuesday, it will reach Narkatiaganj at 2:20 am, Raxaul at 3:15 am and Sitamarhi at 4:47 am. It will then pass through Shisho at 6:10 am and Madhubani at 7:02 am before departing from Jainagar at 10:30 am Indian time. According to Nepal time, the train will leave Jainagar at 10:45 am and reach Janakpur Dham at 12:40 pm. Train to have 17 coaches, including AC and sleeper classes The Saryu-Kamala Express will have a total of 17 coaches, including seven sleeper-class coaches, three third AC coaches, three third AC economy coaches and two second AC coaches. It will also have one generator-cum-luggage van and one coach equipped with facilities for specially abled passengers. The regular service will strengthen rail connectivity between India and Nepal via Gorakhpur. Pilgrims travelling between Janakpur Dham and Ayodhya will no longer need to change trains multiple times. The service is also expected to support religious tourism and passenger movement between the two countries.

stories.title: Air purifier demand rises in Varanasi as winter sets in:Up to 50-fold increase from last year; doctor says people with respiratory problems need them more
stories.summary: Concerns over air pollution are rising in Varanasi with the onset of winter. The impact is now visible in the market, with more people buying air purifiers to ensure cleaner air in their homes and offices. According to shopkeepers, demand for air purifiers has increased significantly compared with last year. Owners of RD Kothari and Yati TV showrooms said that earlier, doctors were the primary buyers, purchasing the machines for their clinics. Now, however, ordinary consumers are also enquiring about and buying them. Experts say cases of respiratory illnesses generally increase between September and December. However, they caution that not everyone needs to buy an air purifier. Doctors were the main buyers last year; now more people are enquiring Sankalp Singh, owner of Yati TV showroom, said sales of air purifiers were very low until last year. Most buyers were doctors purchasing them for their clinics. In some cases, patients also gifted the machines to doctors. However, concerns over pollution and firecracker smoke have increased since Diwali. Following reports of severe pollution in Delhi, people in Varanasi have also started enquiring about air purifiers. Greater awareness and information available online have contributed to the rise in demand. Singh said customers are currently showing interest in air purifiers from brands such as Eureka Forbes and Philips. However, availability and after-sales service remain challenges in the local market. Filters and spare parts are not easily available, making shopkeepers cautious about stocking new brands. Sales rise from 15 units to 30-35 in a year Mukund Kapoor, owner of RD Kothari, said demand for air purifiers has increased considerably compared with last year. While around 15 units were sold last year, sales have already reached 30-35 units this year. Earlier, doctors were the main buyers, but more people are now purchasing air purifiers for their homes. Respiratory illness cases rise between September and December Respiratory disease specialist and Indian Medical Association (IMA) president-elect Prof. Dr Manoj Kumar Srivastava said cases of respiratory illnesses increase between September and December. During this period, dust, pollen and other allergens in the air, along with smoke from Diwali firecrackers, can worsen respiratory problems. This can lead to an increase in conditions such as allergic rhinitis, allergic bronchitis and asthma. People already suffering from asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or bronchitis need to be particularly careful during this season. Air purifiers are not necessary for everyone Dr Srivastava said air purifiers can help improve indoor air quality. They may be particularly beneficial for people who already have respiratory conditions. However, their benefits are largely limited to the room in which the machine is operating. Once a person steps outside, they are exposed to polluted air again. Varanasi's air was more polluted this Diwali than last year Air pollution levels in Varanasi were higher this Diwali than during the festival last year. According to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data, the city's Air Quality Index (AQI) on Diwali day was 118 in 2025. This year, it rose to 224 on November 8. The AQI on the day after Diwali also increased from 156 in 2025 to 274 this year. The AQI was recorded at 160 on November 10 and 134 on November 11. A comparison of the four days shows that pollution levels around Diwali were approximately 58% higher this year than last year. Meanwhile, private platform AQI.in reported that the AQI reached 921 around midnight between November 8 and 9. However, this reading comes from a different platform and time period and should not be directly compared with the CPCB's average AQI figures.

stories.title: ECI team to review election preparations in 11 districts today:Team reaches Gorakhpur; 3 commissioners, 11 DMs and police chiefs to attend
stories.summary: A team from the Election Commission of India (ECI) has reached Gorakhpur on a two-day visit to review preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. On November 26 and 27, the team will assess election arrangements in 17 districts across five divisions of the state. On Thursday, the first day of the visit, preparations in 11 districts across the Gorakhpur, Varanasi and Basti divisions will be reviewed. The review meeting will be held at the Courtyard by Marriott hotel on the banks of Ramgarh Tal. It will be led by senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg. Divisional commissioners, district magistrates (DMs), police officials and district police chiefs from the concerned areas will attend the meeting. On Friday, the team will review preparations in six districts across the Azamgarh and Vindhyachal divisions. Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa will also be present on both days. Officials will use PowerPoint presentations to brief the team on election preparations and proposed action plans. Preparations in 11 districts to be reviewed on first day On November 26, the review in Gorakhpur will cover Gorakhpur, Deoria, Kushinagar, Maharajganj, Varanasi, Jaunpur, Chandauli, Ghazipur, Basti, Sant Kabir Nagar and Siddharthnagar districts. The meeting will be attended by the commissioners of the three divisions, one police commissioner, three Deputy Inspectors General (DIGs), and the DMs and district police chiefs concerned. Officials will present details of election-related arrangements and the preparations completed so far. On November 27, preparations in six districts across the Azamgarh and Vindhyachal divisions will be reviewed. These include Azamgarh, Mau, Ballia, Mirzapur, Bhadohi and Sonbhadra. Preparations aimed at ensuring free and fair elections The Commission is reviewing preparations to ensure that the 2027 Assembly elections are conducted in a free, fair, transparent and peaceful manner. The progress of election arrangements will be assessed on the basis of presentations made by officials. The ECI team will then issue necessary directions to ensure that all arrangements are completed on time before the elections.

stories.title: 5 companies to invest ₹17,650 crore in GIDA:MoUs to be signed in Yogi's presence on November 29; ₹16,000 crore earmarked for green ammonia plant
stories.summary: Investment proposals worth ₹17,650 crore will be formalised on the 37th Foundation Day of the Gorakhpur Industrial Development Authority (GIDA). Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) will be signed with companies on November 29 in the presence of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The proposed investments will be used to establish units for green ammonia, pharmaceutical manufacturing, metal processing, distillery operations and fish feed production. According to GIDA, seven major companies will invest in these projects. The biggest proposal is from ACME, which plans to invest ₹16,000 crore in the green ammonia sector. Other proposals include investments of ₹500 crore each in pharmaceutical manufacturing and metal processing, ₹500 crore in a distillery and ₹150 crore in a fish feed unit. GIDA CEO Vishal Kumar said new investment MoUs would be signed during the foundation day celebrations. These projects are expected to boost industrial activity in eastern Uttar Pradesh and create employment opportunities locally. Green ammonia plant to receive the biggest investment ACME's proposed green ammonia plant will be the largest project among the investments, with an estimated investment of ₹16,000 crore. Pharmaceutical manufacturing and metal processing units are also expected to receive investments of ₹500 crore each. These facilities are expected to boost industrial production. The proposals also include a distillery worth ₹500 crore and a fish feed unit worth ₹150 crore. The distillery is expected to provide a market for farmers growing sugarcane and other grains. Meanwhile, the fish feed unit will make fish feed locally available to fish farmers. Dhooriyapar Industrial Corridor expands land availability GIDA is expanding its land bank to make more land available for industries. The development of the Dhooriyapar Industrial Corridor has increased land availability for large industrial projects. Efforts have also been made to improve infrastructure, including roads, electricity and drainage facilities. The authority is also working to simplify land allotment and No Objection Certificate (NOC) procedures through the Nivesh Mitra portal. Several companies have already started production Companies such as PepsiCo, Kayan Distilleries, Gyan Dairy and Tatva Plastics have established units in the GIDA area and started production. A Coca-Cola unit is also being set up. Projects such as a plastic park and a flatted factory complex are also under development. Improved road connectivity in Gorakhpur has further supported industrial activity. The network of four-lane and six-lane roads, along with connectivity to the Purvanchal Expressway and Gorakhpur Link Expressway, has made it easier to transport goods and deliver finished products to markets.

stories.title: 'I am a gangster, I will marry only you':Man attempts to abduct young woman from Etawah home, threatens to throw acid if she refuses
stories.summary: "Nikhil has been harassing me for one year. He says he is a gangster and that he will marry only me. He says that if I do not marry him, he will shoot me, run a truck over me and disfigure my face by throwing acid on me. I am afraid to leave the house." This is what the young woman said after an attempt was made to abduct her in front of her family. On Tuesday (25 November), the accused youth arrived at the girl's home in Etawah with his accomplices in two cars. In front of her family, he began dragging the young woman away to marry her. He assaulted her brother and father. Villagers gathered and rescued the girl. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the victim. Read the report... The girl is due to get married in January The family of the 19-year-old survivor lives in a village in the Jaswantnagar police station area, 5 km from the district headquarters. She has her father and 4 brothers in the family. Her mother died in a road accident 3 years ago. Three of her brothers live outside the village for work. The girl lives in the village with her father and younger brother. Her family has finalised her marriage alliance. The accused's family lives one neighbourhood away Satish Diwakar's house is one neighbourhood away from ours. Satish oversees farming work. His only son, Nikhil, lives at home. Nikhil occasionally drives a truck, but spends most of his time roaming around the village. Villagers said Nikhil's family is well-off. There are police cases against him. He was also jailed some time ago, but was released on bail. Now read what the victim told us... The victim said, "Nikhil has been harassing me for a long time. I studied up to high school, but had to give up my studies because of him. I do not go outside the house much either. Whenever I occasionally go to the market or elsewhere, he harasses me. I remained silent out of fear of being defamed. I had complained to my family once." Attempt to defame her by posting her photograph on social media My family went to Nikhil's house. His father pleaded with them and assured them that his son would never do anything like this again. However, his behaviour did not stop. He also tried to defame me by posting my photograph on social media. Yesterday morning, I was sweeping outside the house. Nikhil suddenly arrived in two cars with several boys. He said, "Come, I have come to take you. I will marry you today." He dragged me by my hair to the car. When I raised an alarm, my brother and father came there. These people assaulted them as well. They fled when people from the neighbourhood arrived. The police have not taken any action either. I have now complained to the SP. Brother said: "I was discussing my sister's marriage" The young woman's brother said, "My sister is 19 years old. Her marriage has been arranged. I was on the roof today, discussing the wedding-related transactions with my father. My sister was sweeping downstairs. Suddenly, at least 10-12 young men arrived in two vehicles. When they said something to my sister, she began screaming. Hearing the noise, people from the neighbourhood gathered. The accused began molesting my sister in front of everyone. They repeatedly grabbed her hand and said, 'Marry us, otherwise we will pick you up, put you in the vehicle and take you away.'" They assaulted people and then tried to drag her into the vehicle We also ran downstairs. One of them was trying to put my sister into the vehicle. He was carrying a country-made pistol and a weapon. He was dragging my sister by her hair towards the vehicle. When I and some people from the neighbourhood tried to rescue her, they beat everyone. My hands and legs were scraped and my clothes were torn in the assault. When more people from the surrounding area gathered and began protesting, the men got into the vehicle and fled. Police released him after making him sign a blank sheet of paper He had done something similar once before, 10-15 days ago. Whenever my sister goes outside, he tells her, "You look very beautiful and attractive. Marry me, or we will kill you. We drive trucks, so we will run one over your brother." He sometimes stands on other people's rooftops and whistles. My sister did not tell anyone because she was afraid. When I asked her, she said, "Brother, he threatens and intimidates me like this." But today, he came directly with a wedding procession and some boys and tried to take my sister away. This was nothing short of blatant hooliganism. Brother said: They have money; we are poor people Nikhil lives one neighbourhood away from our home. He is a delinquent and already has cases registered against him. He has previously fired at one of our family members. If the police investigate, his old cases will also come to light. He has money; it is being reported that his father recently sold a plot of land. He may have paid ₹5 lakh from the proceeds of that sale and got out of jail. He has a lot of money, while we are poor people. We earn and eat on a daily basis. SSP assures action When we went to have the report registered, the police made my daughter sign a blank sheet of paper. They wrote whatever they wanted on it and let that boy go. I had filed a complaint of molestation, but the police recorded it as an assault case and let those boys go. When I met the SP, she said, "Action will be taken on your complaint." SP City Babita Singh said "The victim and her family came to meet me today. After hearing their complaint, I directed the Jaswantnagar police to investigate the matter. Further action will be taken after the investigation."
