Women to receive ₹20,000 ahead of UP elections:BJP has formed governments in 7 states with this strategy; will women prove to be game-changers again?
stories.summary: The BJP is preparing to make a major move to woo women voters ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. According to party sources, the state government is planning to transfer ₹20,000 each into the bank accounts of women across the state. For this, a budget provision of ₹40,000 crore may be made during the upcoming winter session of the state legislature. The BJP has used similar strategies to form governments in seven states, including Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. It remains to be seen whether the party can return to power in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term with the support of women voters. Money may be transferred to bank accounts in December Political analysts believe that the Election Commission may issue the notification for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections by January 10. In view of this, the state government may transfer the money to women's bank accounts in December itself, in two instalments of ₹10,000 each, before the Model Code of Conduct comes into force. However, the name of the scheme under which the money will be given has not yet been finalised. Top leadership from Delhi and Lucknow to take final call A crucial meeting is likely to be held soon between Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary to finalise the framework of the scheme. It will be implemented after seeking Prime Minister Narendra Modi's approval. Two categories under consideration for financial assistance The BJP and senior government officials are discussing which category of women should benefit from the proposed financial assistance. Two options are being considered: BPL families: Uttar Pradesh has around 3.64 crore families living below the poverty line (BPL). One proposal is to provide Rs 20,000 in two instalments to one woman from each of these families, preferably the female head of the household. Self-help groups: The second option is to provide assistance to women associated with the State Rural Livelihood Mission. Around 1 crore women in Uttar Pradesh are members of self-help groups (SHGs). The proposal to provide them with the money to promote self-employment is also under discussion. Strategy to repeat the old formula At BJP meetings held in Lucknow, Mathura and Delhi, there has been a consensus that women voters could once again prove to be the 'game-changers' in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The BJP has already experimented with a similar strategy during the Bihar Assembly elections. Under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, ₹10,000 each was transferred to the bank accounts of 1.56 crore women in Bihar. The scheme cost around ₹15,600 crore. Trends during the 2017 and 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections and the 2019 Lok Sabha elections indicated that women voters played a significant role in the BJP's victories. Mega plan to reach 6.20 crore women voters Women voters hold a decisive position in Uttar Pradesh. Keeping this in mind, the BJP is planning a special campaign across the state from November 26 to 28 to add more women voters to the electoral rolls and connect them with the party. Voter details: Total voters: 13,58,68,905 Male voters: 7,38,58,510 Female voters: 6,20,06,353 (the number could rise to 6.30 crore after the Special Summary Revision (SSR)) Transgender voters: 4,021 Honorarium hikes and scooter distribution used to woo women voters The BJP leadership believes that if voters have to choose between Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in the elections, women are likely to prefer Yogi because of law and order and government welfare schemes. In recent days, the Yogi government has increased the honorariums of Anganwadi workers, helpers, mid-day meal cooks and ASHA workers. Tablets are also being distributed to female students. In addition, 40,000 meritorious female students will soon receive scooters at a major event in Lucknow. The government is also preparing to increase pensions for destitute women. BJP says government is taking positive steps for women BJP state spokesperson Priyanka Pandey says, "Women have unwavering faith that the Modi-Yogi government is genuinely concerned about their employment, self-employment, dignity, security and self-reliance. With the rule of law established in the state, mothers, sisters and daughters now feel safe. The government will continue to take every possible step in the interest of women." States where the BJP has already used similar strategies The NDA is currently in power in 22 states across the country. The BJP has chief ministers in 17 of these states, while its allies have chief ministers in the remaining five. In several of these states, schemes involving direct financial assistance to women ahead of Assembly elections have delivered favourable electoral results for the BJP. Three different situations can be identified: First situation: BJP was not in power, promised financial assistance to women, and formed the government Odisha: During the June 2024 Assembly elections, the BJP promised to provide ₹10,000 annually in two instalments of ₹5,000 each. It defeated the Biju Janata Dal, ending its 24-year rule, and formed the government. The Subhadra Yojana was launched in September 2024. Chhattisgarh: In November 2023, the BJP promised to provide ₹1,000 every month to women. It defeated the Congress and formed the government. The Mahtari Vandan Yojana was launched in March 2024. Second situation: BJP was already in power, introduced financial assistance schemes for women, and returned to power Madhya Pradesh: Under the Mukhyamantri Ladli Behna Yojana, ₹1,500 per month was transferred to women's bank accounts. The scheme was launched eight months before the Assembly elections. Maharashtra: Under the Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana, ₹1,500 per month was transferred to women's bank accounts. The scheme was launched four months before the elections. Assam: Under the Orunodoi scheme, ₹1,250 per month was provided to women. The scheme was launched five months before the elections. Bihar: Under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, financial assistance of ₹20,000 was announced. The first instalment of Rs 10,000, meant to promote self-employment, was transferred just one-and-a-half months before the elections. Third situation: BJP was in power but did not introduce the scheme before the elections; it only made a promise and provided financial assistance after returning to power Haryana: The BJP promised ₹2,100 per month to women under the Laado Lakshmi Yojana during the October 2024 elections. It returned to power for the third consecutive time, and the scheme was launched in 2025. The trend suggests that in states where governments introduced schemes to transfer money directly into women's bank accounts shortly before Assembly elections, the BJP returned to power. In Chhattisgarh and Odisha, the BJP made promises of financial assistance before the elections and subsequently came to power.

stories.title: Chitrakoot SDM appears before High Court from drawing room:Judge asks why he did not join from office; SDM says home internet connection is better
stories.summary: Chitrakoot SDM (Judicial) appeared before the Allahabad High Court through video conference from his drawing room. The court strongly objected to the way he joined the hearing and sought an explanation from both the District Magistrate (DM) and the SDM. A bench led by Justice Saurabh Shyam Shamshery asked the SDM why he had joined the hearing from his drawing room instead of his office. The SDM replied that his home had a better internet connection. He also said he had joined from home with the DM's permission. The court has directed that a copy of its order be sent to the Chief Secretary of the state's Panchayati Raj Department. If the Chief Secretary is not satisfied with the SDM's reply, he will decide on further action and whether an inquiry should be conducted against him. High Court says SDM could have joined from DM's office The High Court said that if the SDM's office did not have an internet connection, the DM could have allowed him to join the hearing through video conference from his office. The court also told the DM, "Advise government officials to maintain proper conduct and respect when appearing before the court." Read the full case in detail The matter came to light during the hearing of a writ petition filed by Sunil. Taneesha Jahangir Munir represented Sunil, the petitioner and head of Achalpur Gram Panchayat in Ghiror tehsil. The candidate who was defeated in the election had filed an application in the SDM court against the petitioner, but it was dismissed on 5 July 2024. A review application was filed on 25 July 2024. On 1 April 2025, the application was accepted and the earlier order dismissing the election petition was set aside through an order of just five lines. The then SDM, who is now the SDM (Judicial) in Chitrakoot, allowed the review in a five-line order on 1 April 2025 and set aside the order dated 5 July 2024. No reason was given, nor was it stated whether the parties had been heard. Subsequently, on 30 July 2025, the review application was allowed again and the order dated 5 July 2024 was set aside. The court asked, "How can an order that has already been set aside be set aside again?" No satisfactory answer was received. SDM could not even state the legal basis The High Court had directed Prasoon Kashyap, the SDM (Judicial) of Chitrakoot who passed both disputed orders, to appear via video conference. During the hearing, SDM Prasoon Kashyap said the order dated 1 April 2025 had been passed because the other party had not filed its response to the review application. However, he could not explain why the order recorded no reason for accepting the application. SDM Prasoon Kashyap said, "Reasons had been given in the order passed after 30 July 2025." The High Court then asked what the legal basis was for cancelling again an order that had already been cancelled. According to the court, the SDM was also unable to cite any legal provision that permitted such action. Both orders quashed, fresh hearing directed The High Court quashed both orders dated 1 April 2025 and 30 July 2025. It also directed the relevant authority to conduct a fresh hearing on the review application and take a decision within four weeks. The court directed both parties to appear before the relevant authority on 26 November and present their replies and arguments. It also ordered that a copy of the order be sent to the Chief Secretary of the state's Panchayati Raj Department, so that a decision could be taken on initiating an inquiry against the SDM based on his explanation.

stories.title: Father son die 9 days before daughter's wedding:Sister-in-law, nephew injured in cylinder blast while cooking in Noida
stories.summary: A gas cylinder exploded at a house in Greater Noida, leaving four family members with serious burn injuries. The father and son later died during treatment, while the daughter-in-law and grandson remain in critical condition. The deceased were identified as Veerpal (55) and his son Abhishek (26), residents of Dayanatpur village in Jewar. Abhishek's wife and son are undergoing treatment in serious condition. Veerpal's daughter was scheduled to get married on December 2. The father and son were busy making preparations for the wedding. Several gas cylinders had been brought and stored at the house for the event. One of them exploded at around 6 pm in the Jewar police station area. See 2 pictures below : Veerpal Singh's daughter, a resident of Dayanatpur village in the Jewar police station area, was scheduled to get married on December 2. The family was busy with wedding preparations, and relatives had started arriving at the house. Meanwhile, a gas cylinder exploded in the kitchen at around 6 pm on Monday while food was being prepared. The blast was so loud that people in the nearby areas were left frightened. Hearing the sound, hundreds of villagers rushed to the spot. They worked hard to rescue the injured family members trapped inside the burning house and took them to the hospital. Veerpal Singh and his son Abhishek died during treatment. Abhishek's wife Kajal and their son Aditya suffered serious injuries. Both are undergoing treatment at the hospital. MLA seeks financial help for the family MLA Dhirendra Singh expressed grief over the incident. He met the affected family and offered his support. He assured them that the injured would receive the best possible treatment. He also wrote to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, seeking financial help from the Chief Minister's Relief Fund for the families of those who died in the incident.

stories.title: BJP holds key meeting ahead of UP elections:SIR coordination with allies discussed; CM Yogi, Pankaj Chaudhary attend
stories.summary: The BJP core committee held a meeting in Lucknow to discuss preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, organisational minister Dharampal Singh, state president Pankaj Chaudhary, Deputy Chief Ministers Brajesh Pathak and Keshav Prasad Maurya attended the meeting. The meeting discussed adding names to the voter list, party activities and seat-sharing plans with alliance partners. Leaders also discussed the government's performance, caste and regional factors, the Opposition's plans and coordination with NDA allies. The meeting was held at Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's residence at 5 pm on Monday. It is being seen as an important step in the party's preparations for the elections. The BJP has formed special teams in every Assembly constituency to help add deleted names back to the voter list. Local councillors and party leaders have been given this responsibility. The party has also started a door-to-door campaign to help people fill out forms and submit the required documents. Feedback taken on all 403 seats At the meeting, leaders reviewed the party's position, local political factors and the work of party workers in all 403 Assembly constituencies in the state. The party leadership has stressed the need to strengthen booth-level management in every constituency well before the election is announced. What leaders said after the meeting Keshav says party has resolved to make the lotus bloom for the third time Keshav Prasad Maurya said the party has taken a resolve to win for the third time and make the lotus bloom again. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya said that the party had resolved to make the lotus bloom for the third time in 2027. Meetings are being held continuously to prepare for this. Such meetings will continue to be held in the future as well. On the meeting being held between the SP and Congress over seat-sharing, Keshav Maurya said the alliance posed no problem for the BJP. The SP-Congress alliance would suffer a crushing defeat, and the BJP would form the government with a full majority. He said the BJP's election preparations were very strong and extensive, which was why the party did not take these meetings seriously. Brajesh Pathak said: The SP now remembers 'Radhe-Radhe' Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said that the SP and its leaders should be asked whether they had ever thought about Sanatan culture, or about saying "Radhe-Radhe" and "Ram-Ram", before. He said these were the same people who used to wear skullcaps and host iftar feasts every day. Now they are remembering "Radhe-Radhe" and "Ram-Ram". Samajwadi Party leaders should make their intentions clear. Today, India's Sanatan culture is at its highest point, and Uttar Pradesh is proud of its heritage. 3 BJP meetings in one day A series of BJP meetings continued in Uttar Pradesh on Monday. The first meeting was attended by Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde, the state president, the organisation general secretary and district presidents. The meeting discussed the voter enrolment drive and the Prabuddh Jansamvad programme beginning on 26 November. MPs were also tasked with holding chaupal meetings. The second meeting discussed the election strategy, rallies and potential candidates. The third meeting was held in the presence of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. It discussed preparations for the voter enrolment campaign. Story being updated

stories.title: 35-year-old man marries 15 women:Blackmail them with obscene photos videos; Ghaziabad Police sends him to jail
stories.summary: Thirty-five-year-old Narendra Sharma in Ghaziabad married 15 women one after another. He then took their money and jewellery and blackmailed them by making obscene photographs and videos of them. Narendra married women from Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Rajasthan and Maharashtra. One of them was a woman living in Meerut, after which he began living with her in Ghaziabad. When the woman began to suspect Narendra, she lodged a complaint. The police then launched a search for Narendra and arrested him on Sunday. The woman who fell victim to Narendra's fraud also reached the Ghaziabad court during his appearance. She said that he had ruined her life. He had married 15 women, not just one. By claiming to be wealthy, he had ruined the lives of women and played with their honour. Photographs of the young man with different women... Now read what the woman who reached the court said Met on a matrimonial site, woman cheated of ₹18 lakh after marriage The woman who approached a Ghaziabad court is a resident of a village in the Jani police station area of Meerut. The 26-year-old has completed a B.Ed. She currently lives with her family in Ghaziabad's Nandgram area. The woman said, "I had registered on the Jeevansathi app to find a life partner. That is where I was introduced to Narendra, who lives in the Runwal Park Sindhi Society in Mumbai. As our conversations progressed, Narendra came to Meerut to meet my family on 1 July 2025." Narendra told my family that his family was originally from Bikaner in Rajasthan but had been living in Mumbai for the past 30 years. His father, Brahmaprakash Sharma, is a chartered accountant. Narendra also said that he owned a resort in Goa and five hotels in Khatu Shyam. He said he did not want dowry and wanted to marry a girl from a poor family. Influenced by what he said, my family arranged my marriage to Narendra a year ago. After that, we both moved to Ghaziabad. Kept her in flat for a month, discovered his second marriage The woman said, "After the marriage, Narendra got me to transfer ₹18 lakh to an online account in the name of share trading. Meanwhile, I began to suspect Narendra. I saw him secretly speaking to other women on video calls. He always kept his mobile switched off in front of me." Narendra lived with me in the flat for around a month. Later, I found out that he had also married another woman in Delhi. He was living with her in a rented flat in Gurugram. I then went to Narendra's house in Mumbai. His father told me that he was disinheriting Narendra. During this time, I learnt that Narendra had previously married several other women. When I confronted Narendra, he beat me The woman said that when she asked Narendra about his other marriages, he beat her severely. He raped her and began threatening to kill her. Meanwhile, I learnt that Narendra had secretly taken obscene photos and videos of me. When I said I would complain to the police, he began blackmailing me, threatening to make the photos and videos go viral. Distressed by this, I filed a case against Narendra Sharma at Nandgram police station on 21 May. Photos of 15 marriages handed over to police The woman has also handed the police photos of Narendra's 15 marriages. The police are now investigating Narendra's criminal record. They are also probing allegations that he married other women and defrauded them. Nandgram SHO Santosh Tripathi said- The accused youth was arrested and sent to jail. The claims made by the young woman regarding the accused marrying other girls are also being investigated.

stories.title: Kashi to glow tomorrow, CM Yogi to light first lamp:1.5 million tourists and guests from 40 countries expected; traffic diversions special drone show planned
stories.summary: Dev Deepawali will be celebrated in Kashi on 24 November. This year, 11 lakh lamps will light up the ghats along the Ganga. Guests from 40 countries are expected to attend the event, while around 15 lakh tourists are likely to visit the city. The lamps will light up the stretch from Sant Ravidas Ghat to Adikeshav Ghat. The riverbank along the Varuna, as well as monasteries and temples, will also be decorated with lamps. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will begin the celebrations by lighting the first lamp at Namo Ghat. He will then watch the Ganga Aarti, laser show, drone show and fireworks from a cruise. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will also watch the celebrations live, as he does every year. The district administration will make arrangements for the live streaming. How was the tradition started? Boys playing cricket started the tradition The present-day celebration of Dev Deepawali in Kashi began just 41 years ago. In 1985, a group of boys playing cricket at the ghat collected money from devotees to buy lamps and oil. They then lit five lamps at Panchganga Ghat. In 1986, the festival was celebrated at five ghats in Banaras: Panchganga, Balaji, Scindia, Man Mandir and Ahilyabai. In 1987, more people joined the celebrations, and Dev Deepawali was celebrated at 15 ghats, including Dashashwamedh Ghat. The following year, the festival was also celebrated at Assi Ghat. By the fifth year, the celebrations had spread to 27 ghats. Today, Dev Deepawali is celebrated as a grand festival at more than 85 ghats along the Ganga. Read about the arrangements at the ghats and what will be special Dashashwamedh Ghat to host the grandest celebrations This year, the celebrations will begin with the lighting of lamps at Panchganga Ghat. A grand Ganga Aarti will be held at Dashashwamedh Ghat. Different communities will light lamps at all 84 ghats along the Ganga. At Pandey Ghat, a special display based on the Kashi Vishwanath Dham will be created using lamps. Of the 11 lakh lamps, around 50,000 will be made from cow dung. The South Indian community will donate 20,000 lamps, while a grand rangoli will also be made at the ghat. Women from the Bengali community will take part in a special puja. Kedar Ghat will also offer a special glimpse of the celebrations. Meanwhile, the Jai Maa Ganga Seva Samiti is preparing a special Ganga Aarti at Assi Ghat. Lamp display based on Kashi Vishwanath Dham theme The main celebrations of Dev Deepawali will take place at the ghats along the Ganga. The event will begin with the lighting of lamps at Panchganga Ghat. The grandest celebrations will be held at Dashashwamedh Ghat, where preparations are under way for a special Ganga Aarti. People from different communities will light lamps at all 84 ghats along the river. At Pandey Ghat, a special display based on the Kashi Vishwanath Dham theme will be created using lamps. A total of 11 lakh lamps will be lit along the ghats, including around 50,000 lamps made from cow dung. South Indian community to create grand rangoli The South Indian community will donate 20,000 lamps for the celebrations. A grand rangoli will also be created at the ghat. Women from the Bengali community will take part in special prayers and rituals. Kedar Ghat will also see special decorations and celebrations. Meanwhile, the Jai Maa Ganga Seva Samiti has been given the responsibility of organising a special Ganga Aarti at Assi Ghat. Now find out the charges for cruises and rooms Cruise room booked for ₹3 lakh Tourists are having to spend a large amount even for boating on the Ganga. Booking a barge with a capacity of 40 people now costs between ₹2 lakh and ₹2.5 lakh. Small boats are available for ₹20,000 to ₹30,000, while motorboat fares range from ₹50,000 to ₹1 lakh. One room on the Gangotri cruise has been booked for ₹3 lakh. Hotel room rent goes up to ₹80,000 for one night Hotel rooms near the ghats in Kashi are available for ₹40,000 to ₹80,000 per night. On normal days, these rooms cost around ₹20,000 to ₹25,000. Homestay rates have also increased. A room that usually costs around ₹800 is now being offered for ₹4,000 to ₹8,000 per night. Meanwhile, preparations for Dev Deepawali are in full swing. Painting and whitewashing work is under way at the ghats. The places where Ganga Aarti is held are being decorated with flowers, while lighting work is also nearing completion. Auspicious timing for Dev Deepawali : Now understand the traffic plan Buses will not be allowed inside the city Buses operating from the Kashi and Cantt bus stations, as well as private buses, will not be allowed to enter the city. Designated locations have been assigned for them. Buses to Jaunpur, Azamgarh and Ghazipur will stop at Ring Road Harhua, Bawan Bigha and near the Sandaha underpass, respectively, and will operate from there. Buses to Chandauli, Prayagraj, Sonbhadra and Mirzapur will operate from near Thikana Dhaba in Mohansarai. Buses to Bhadohi will travel as far as the Parampur underpass and return from there. Passengers arriving by bus will be able to reach the city by city bus or passenger vehicles. Five holding areas and 57 parking sites created Fifty-seven parking sites have been created for vehicles. These include Benia Bagh parking, Godaulia multi-level parking, Town Hall, Sanskrit University, Queen's College, Sanatan Dharma Inter College, Majda parking, Harishchandra Degree College, BHU, Anglo-Bengali Inter College, Dwarikadhish Temple, the CHS school ground, the area opposite Baba Keenaram Ashram, Harsewanand School, Lautubir parking, Garhwa Ghat, Vidyapeeth ground, the NER railway ground, Cantt station, Chhota and Bada Cutting Memorial School, UP College, LT College, Paharia Mandi, Durga Temple-Ramnagar, the PAC ground, Rambagh ground, Panchvati ground and Lanka ground. Meanwhile, in Ramnagar, Durga Temple, Lanka Maidan, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, the BHU campus and the UP College campus have been designated as holding areas. 25 IPS officers, over 3,000 police personnel to oversee security Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal said 25 IPS officers, 50 PPS officers and other senior police officials would be deployed for security during Dev Deepawali. More than 3,000 police personnel would also be on duty. Fifty rescue boats, the water police and NDRF teams would remain on alert on the Ganga. The ATS, QRT and anti-drone systems would also be deployed to ensure security. Security arrangements would be made at three levels. The ghat area would be divided into 10 zones, 21 sectors and 36 sub-sectors for better monitoring.

stories.title: Circle Officer who gave Owaisi guard of honour removed:Saharanpur Police asks X to delete video, says it is damaging its image
stories.summary: Circle Officer Sadar Pawan Kumar, who gave a guard of honour to AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi in Saharanpur, has been removed from his post. He has been transferred to the Traffic Department as Circle Officer Traffic. SP Rural Mayank Pathak confirmed the change. The police have also written to X (formerly Twitter), asking it to remove the video and related posts shared on the platform. According to the police, some people are sharing the video in a way that suggests Owaisi was mistakenly given a guard of honour. The police say this is damaging their image. Check out visuals below : Cyber Crime Cell investigating officer sends letter The Crime Branch's Cyber Crime Cell is investigating the giving of a guard of honour to Owaisi. The investigation is being led by Surendra Kumar. He has sent a letter to X Corp's Safety and Legal Policy Department, identifying the 19 X accounts from which the video is being circulated. The letter also contains the address of the company's office in Texas, USA. SSP Abhinandan said that Surendra Kumar, the investigating officer handling the case in the Cyber Crime Cell, had written to the company. A list of the 19 X accounts was enclosed, along with a request to remove the related videos and posts. Guard of honour given on 21 November Police personnel mistakenly gave AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi a guard of honour at the Circuit House in Saharanpur on Saturday (21 November). A Supreme Court judge was scheduled to arrive at the Circuit House at 11 a.m. The police team had gone there to welcome the judge with a guard of honour. The judge did not arrive at the scheduled time. Meanwhile, Owaisi suddenly reached the Circuit House. The police team mistook him for the judge and saluted him. Now, read about what a 'guard of honour' is According to former Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police Sulkhan Singh, a guard of honour involves a contingent of the police or armed forces conducting a formal parade and expressing respect with a salute. It is presented in accordance with established protocols, rules and constitutional traditions. The police giving a guard salute is entirely a departmental process. Outside the department, a guard salute is given to an individual only on the occasion of state functions. MPs and MLAs do not receive a guard of honour When an officer or employee of the armed forces dies, their mortal remains are given a gun salute. The mortal remains of other dignitaries are also given a salute when a state funeral is declared for them. However, MPs and MLAs cannot be given such a guard of honour.

stories.title: Baba Ramdev calls Dhirendra Shastri a fraud hypocrite:Says he exploits people by frightening them in the name of ghosts and spirits
stories.summary: Yoga guru Baba Ramdev launched an attack on Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, the head priest of Bageshwar Dham. Without taking his name, Ramdev called him "deranged", "hypocrite", "fraud" and "cunning". Ramdev alleged that some religious speakers frighten and exploit people in the name of religion and claims of ghosts and spirits. He said some people neither read the Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas, Ramayana and Mahabharata nor understand the Constitution and democracy. Despite this, they call themselves Sanatanis and claim to be working to protect Hinduism. He said, "You should first save yourself, you deranged hypocrite and fraud!" Said comparing Ram and Krishna is wrong Ramdev also objected to people comparing Lord Ram and Lord Krishna. He said it was wrong to make disrespectful remarks about gods and goddesses and then repeat them after apologising. He added that everything has its own limits and discipline. Baba Ramdev made these remarks in Jamshedpur, Jharkhand. He was speaking at a women's conference organised by Patanjali on Sunday. News is being updated…

stories.title: Paid ₹17 lakh fine over ₹5 'khaini':Spent 18 days in jail; UP man caught at Bahrain airport shares ordeal
stories.summary: Carrying khaini (chewing tobacco) and slaked lime to Bahrain proved costly for Saurabh Rai, a resident of Azamgarh, Uttar Pradesh. During a luggage check at the airport, officials found khaini and lime in a container in his bag. He was then taken into custody. Saurabh had to pay nearly ₹18 lakh over items worth just ₹5. He spent 20 days in difficult conditions abroad before finally returning home safely on Saturday. On Monday, Saurabh shared his experience with Dainik Bhaskar. Kept in a cold room for 18 days without a blanket Saurabh said, "I was kept in an air-conditioned room at 16 degrees Celsius for 18 days while in the custody of Bahrain Police and the CID. I was not even given a blanket to protect myself from the cold. I had to spend the entire night with only a thin sheet." He said officers repeatedly asked him during questioning why he was carrying khaini and lime together. He had to answer the same question each time. His health also worsened while he was in prison. He is now undergoing treatment. Read the full story... Saurabh Rai (35), a resident of Bhavarupur in the Ahraula police station area of Azamgarh, works as a driver in Al-Qatif, Dammam, Saudi Arabia. Saurabh said that when he reached Bahrain airport from Mumbai on 29 October, the customs department searched his belongings. During the search, he was detained after chunauti, khaini and lime were found in his bag. His mobile phone and bag were also seized. He was then handed over to the Bahrain Police and the Criminal Investigation Department (CID). He was repeatedly questioned there about whether he was carrying the items for smuggling or whether there was another reason behind it. Paid 7,200 Bahraini dinars, including lawyer's fee and fine Saurabh said that during his detention, he was kept in a room where the temperature was 16 degrees. The air conditioner ran continuously, but he was given neither a blanket nor warm clothes to protect him from the cold. He had to spend around 18 days with only a light sheet. Meanwhile, his family arranged a lawyer through acquaintances in Bahrain. According to Saurabh, he was given the option of paying a fine or serving a jail sentence. Eventually, he was released from court on 18 November after paying a total of 7,200 Bahraini dinars, or approximately ₹17.80 lakh, including the lawyer's fees and fine. After his release, he reached Saudi Arabia. From there, he travelled home by road via Chennai and Delhi. His health deteriorated during his detention and the journey back. He is currently suffering from typhoid and malaria and is undergoing treatment. The family had sought help from officials Saurabh's elder brother, Rishabh Rai, said that contact with his brother was lost after he reached Bahrain Airport on 29 October. When no information could be obtained despite considerable efforts, an application was submitted to the divisional commissioner, district magistrate and Azamgarh superintendent of police on 12 November. The application sought help through the Ministry of External Affairs. Later, with the help of acquaintances in Bahrain, a lawyer was arranged. Rishabh thanked the Azamgarh superintendent of police and other officials for their assistance in Saurabh's return. After receiving information about Saurabh's safe return, local police also went to his house and recorded his statement. Circle officer Budhanpur Vijay Singh Gaur said they had received information that the young man had returned home. Police personnel were sent from the concerned police station to gather details of the entire case. Senior officials were also informed. What punishment does Bahrain impose for khaini and lime? For possessing khaini or gutka: Importing or possessing banned tobacco is reportedly punishable by a fine of between 2,000 and 5,000 Bahraini dinars. The fine may be doubled for a repeat offence. For bringing lime or areca nut: Under the April 2025 amendment to the law, importing or selling substances used with tobacco may result in at least one year in prison and a fine of between 1,000 and 1 lakh Bahraini dinars. Violations in public places: Violating smoking-related regulations may attract a fine of between 20 and 50 Bahraini dinars, and the items may be confiscated.

stories.title: Parents and 17-year-old son killed after car runs them over:Family had come from Mathura to attend a wedding in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: A speeding XUV-700 ran over a husband, his wife and their 17-year-old son as they were crossing the road in Ghaziabad. All three died in the accident. The impact was so severe that the car went out of control and crashed into the divider. The accused driver then abandoned the vehicle and fled. The accident took place at 10:45 a.m. on Monday in front of an HP petrol pump in the Crossing Republic police station area on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway. The family was from Mathura. The three had come to Ghaziabad to attend a relative's wedding. See the pictures of the accident... Here's the full story... ACP Wave City Priya Shripal said Harlal (54), a resident of Kosi Kalan in Mathura, his wife Rajkumari (50) and their 17-year-old son Tejveer had come to Crossings Republik in Ghaziabad to attend a relative's wedding. All three attended the wedding on 21 November. On Monday, Harlal, Rajkumari and Tejveer were travelling to the railway station to return to Mathura. During this time, the three began crossing the Delhi-Meerut Expressway. A speeding car then ran them over. After the accident, all three were taken to hospital. The couple died at the district hospital, while their son Tejveer died at Max Hospital. Police used a crane to remove the damaged car and took it into custody. Traffic on the expressway was then restored. The bodies of all three victims have been sent for post-mortem examinations. Son-in-law said: The three did not know that roads must not be crossed on expressways Madan, the son-in-law, told the police that his mother-in-law, father-in-law and younger brother-in-law were killed in the accident. The three did not know that roads must not be crossed on expressways. An iron footbridge or an underpass built below must be used instead. However, all three climbed over the divider and reached the expressway. ACP says - driver being traced ACP Wave City Priya Shripal said - The accused driver abandoned the vehicle and fled. Police are searching for him.

stories.title: Woman lists five girls for sacrifice:Draws sketches on wall; Bulandshahr Police find room after girl's murder
stories.summary: A shocking revelation has emerged in the case of the murder of three-year-old Manya during an occult ritual in Bulandshahr. The accused neighbour, Sonam, had selected five girls from the neighbourhood. All of them were under eight years old. Manya was the youngest of them. Sonam had been keeping an eye on the girls for several days. She would often lure them with toffees and chocolates. She had drawn sketches of all five girls on the wall of her room, with their names written beside them. Below them, she had written: "Five murders." According to police sources, the investigation found that Sonam had been living separately from her husband for 10 years. Her eight-year-old daughter also lived with her grandmother. She believed that performing black magic and offering a sacrifice would bring her daughter back to her. The incident took place in the Dehat Kotwali area, 1 km from the district headquarters. Sonam strangled Manya to death during an occult ritual. Sindoor and sandalwood paste had been applied to the body. A lemon had been placed on her forehead. Her fingers had been cut off. 2 pictures- Aunt said: The word 'blood' was written before the girls' names Manya's aunt, Pinky, said, "When the police broke open the room door, I went inside with them. I saw Manya's body lying under the bed. Figures resembling little girls had been drawn on the wall. Some names had been written there. Manya's name was at the top. In addition, the name of a hotel and a mobile number had been written. Seven zeroes had been drawn on the wall. There was a strange smell coming from the room." Grandmother said, "I want blood for blood" Manya's grandmother, Geeta, said, "Sonam was strange. She would sit outside the house and smoke bidis. Whenever she walked around the neighbourhood, it seemed as if she might do something. Her eyes were strange." Crying, she said, "I want blood for blood. She should not be given such a life sentence that she can serve her time in prison and come out again. Let someone ask us what we are going through." Here is the full sequence of events... Manya, alias Vania, the three-year-old daughter of Sachin, who lives in the Bhud locality, went missing from outside her home at around 11 a.m. Sachin's wife, Sharda, called him and informed him that the child was missing. Sachin first searched for the child. When he could not find her, he informed the police at around 2.30 p.m. Along with searching houses in the locality, the police examined more than 150 CCTV cameras. During this process, the child was seen on one of the cameras. A nearby house had been found locked for quite some time. Suspecting something was wrong, the police broke open the lock at around 9 p.m. and searched the house. The body of a girl was found inside. The police learned that a woman named Sonam lived in the house as a tenant. Married 10 years ago, began living with her 8-year-old daughter after husband left her Sonam is originally from Dhaturi village in the Salempur area. She was later apprehended from the bus stand. She married Dinesh, who lived in Jewar in Gautam Buddh Nagar, around 10 years ago. They have an eight-year-old daughter named Bulbul. The couple began quarrelling about a year and a half after their marriage. Dinesh later abandoned Sonam and married another woman in Delhi. He has two children from his second marriage. After this, Sonam began living in different places with her daughter. Sonam's maternal family was unhappy about this and also distanced themselves from her. In-laws took daughter away after Sonam pushed her from the roof 10 days ago During police questioning, Sonam said that about 10 days ago, she had pushed her daughter from the roof, causing her injuries. After this, her maternal family sent Bulbul to her father under a compromise agreement. Sonam had been under stress ever since. She wanted to get her daughter back. She already knew occult rituals. For this purpose, she chose children under eight years of age. She believed that sacrificing children would bring her daughter back to her.

stories.title: Woman sets herself on fire outside hospital in UP:Suffers 55% burns, walks to ambulance on her own
stories.summary: On Monday, a young woman doused herself with petrol and set herself on fire on the premises of Maharajganj District Hospital. Patients and their attendants raised an alarm after suddenly seeing her engulfed in flames. The young woman poured petrol over her body and set herself on fire. Within moments, she was engulfed in flames. Hearing her screams, people nearby rushed over and began trying to put out the fire. She was rescued with their help. The young woman has suffered 55% burns. Her condition is reported to be critical. She has been identified as Sunita, a resident of the Thuthibari area. She is currently undergoing treatment under doctors' supervision. See 2 pictures... According to local residents, the young woman's name is Sunita and she is a resident of the Thuthibari area. For around the past six months, she had been seen living and wandering around the district hospital. She fed herself by asking people for money. Local residents said that her mental health was not good. However, her family background and the reason behind this step have not yet been clarified. Treatment under way in private ward After the incident, the young woman was immediately admitted to the district hospital. CMS Dr AK Dwivedi said the young woman was receiving treatment in the private ward. A team of doctors is monitoring her. According to the hospital administration, she is currently receiving treatment.

stories.title: Brajesh Pathak says Owaisi-Congress-SP alliances will fail:Rajbhar asks why Akhilesh did not meet Azam after his release
stories.summary: Political activity over seat-sharing between the Samajwadi Party and Congress in Uttar Pradesh has intensified. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said that any alliance involving the Congress, SP and Asaduddin Owaisi in Uttar Pradesh would fail miserably. The BJP will return to power for the third time with a massive majority. Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar targeted SP chief Akhilesh Yadav over Azam Khan. He said that Akhilesh had not spoken to Azam even after his release from jail. He added that it did not appear that Akhilesh was particularly happy. stories.title: GRP constable assaults beautician on moving train:Hits her on head, slaps daughter; fight over seat while returning from Bihar in UP
stories.summary: A GRP constable brutally assaulted a beautician from Ludhiana on a moving train. The incident took place at Uttar Pradesh's Moradabad railway station. The woman was returning to Ludhiana from Motihari in Bihar on the Jan Nayak Express. The woman was travelling with her three daughters. Her head was split open in the assault, leaving her covered in blood. The incident took place on 17 November, and a 1-minute-13-second video of it has now emerged. The GRP constable was angered because the woman was lying on a seat in the general coach. He wanted to seat a passenger travelling with him there. The beautician said four tickets had been booked and that the entire seat was theirs. She also had low blood pressure. The beautician alleged that her daughter was slapped as well. They were then made to get off the train at Najibabad station after the chain was pulled, and were kept at the police station throughout the night, where they were threatened with being forced to give false statements. Amid the commotion, their bag containing jewellery and cash was left on the train. After reaching Ludhiana, the victim underwent a medical examination and will now lodge a complaint at the local GRP station. The story of the attack on the train, in the beautician's own words... Read exactly what happened in the video of the scuffle on the train A GRP officer came into the train compartment's corridor, grabbed Ruby's hand and began scuffling with her. Ruby's daughter intervened to save her. Her other daughter tried to pull her back. Her daughters kept saying, "Mummy, sir, sir, you are misbehaving." Meanwhile, the police officer knocked the woman to the floor and fell on top of her himself. Meanwhile, the police officer repeatedly attacks the woman. Ruby's daughter then grabs the police officer by the collar and tries to push him backwards. The police officer tries to free himself from her grip. During this, another girl pulls the police officer from behind. By the time Ruby gets up, blood is coming from her head. Passengers nearby stand on their seats and begin recording the incident on their mobile phones. The passengers then start trying to catch them. When the woman is injured, the police officer tries to move away from the spot. One of the woman's daughters holds on to the police officer's collar, while the other stands in his way. Holding her head, the woman comes forward and also keeps the police officer surrounded. The other police officer bends down and tries to free him from their grip. Both police officers try to free themselves from the woman and her daughters. During this, the shirt buttons of the police officer who attacked them come undone. Ruby tells people to record a video of this. The woman and her daughters did not let go of the police officer. Ruby then grabbed the officer and asked him why he had attacked her. Some passengers also stepped in to intervene, along with another police officer. The constable and the passengers repeatedly shouted, "Let go, let go." The other police officer tried to free the first constable's collar by twisting the women's fingers. A large crowd gathered in the coach, and passengers continued recording the incident. Meanwhile, some people kept telling Ruby and her daughters, "Let go of his neck, let go," while Ruby kept saying, "Keep recording the video." Eventually, the constable managed to free his shirt collar, but the injured woman and her daughter were still holding his hand and baton. Blood was clearly visible on the woman's forehead, face and hands, and she looked angrily at the constable.

stories.title: Pramod Tiwari to host Samajwadi Party-Congress seat-sharing talks:Azam Khan says party ready to offer more seats to keep alliance intact
stories.summary: Negotiations between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress over seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections will begin on Monday. Leaders of the two parties will meet at the Delhi residence of senior Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari at around noon. Ajay Maken will lead the Congress delegation, while Prof Ram Gopal Yadav will represent the SP. Both parties have formed committees to negotiate the seat-sharing arrangement. Discussions between the panels will continue for three days, with the aim of working out an electoral understanding for all 403 Assembly constituencies in Uttar Pradesh. The talks will focus on how many seats each party will contest and which party will field candidates in different constituencies. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has formed a four-member committee to discuss the alliance and seat-sharing arrangement with the Congress. It includes the party's national principal general secretary, Prof Ram Gopal Yadav; state president Shyamlal Pal; Ghosi MP Rajeev Rai; and Kairana MP Iqra Hasan. Congress panel includes Priyanka and KC Venugopal The Congress has also formed a five-member panel to negotiate seat-sharing with the SP. The committee comprises Ajay Maken, Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona', working president Imran Masood and Congress Legislature Party leader Virendra Chaudhary. Meeting to be held at Pramod Tiwari's residence The meeting between the two parties was initially scheduled for November 17 but was postponed because preparations had not been completed. It will now be held at the Delhi residence of Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari, father of Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona'. Discussions are expected to begin around noon. Representatives of both parties have left for Delhi. Congress initially sought 181 seats, SP reportedly firm on 55-60 There is a significant difference between the two parties over the number of seats to be contested. The Congress had initially demanded 181 seats, while the SP is reportedly unwilling to offer more than 55-60 seats. This leaves both parties with the challenge of reaching an agreement on the number of constituencies each will contest. Meanwhile, senior SP leader Azam Khan told Dainik Bhaskar that the Congress of today was different from what it used to be and that the distinction needed to be understood. He said Rahul Gandhi did not speak like leaders of the earlier generation. Regional parties play an important role in states because local problems and circumstances differ from one region to another. Azam Khan said leaders based at the Centre often neither fully understand nor recognise regional issues. They tend to focus more on national concerns, leaving local problems overlooked. He said the Congress had faced a similar situation in Uttar Pradesh because of three major issues concerning Ayodhya, Mathura and Kashi, which did not have the same significance in other states. He stressed that experience and understanding were essential to maintaining an alliance. The same principle applied to the SP, he said. "If we have to offer a few more seats to keep the alliance intact, we are ready to do so. The Congress should also be prepared to give up some seats if necessary. Our objective is not just to win seats but to ensure justice for people," he said. Congress prepares three-phase strategy for seat-sharing talks The Congress has prepared a revised list of constituencies after its initial demand for 181 seats. The list has reportedly received Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's approval. The party has now shifted its focus from the total number of seats to their electoral viability. It plans to stake a claim to constituencies where it has a stronger organisational presence and performed relatively well in previous elections. The proposed list reportedly includes a larger number of constituencies in western Uttar Pradesh and the Bundelkhand region. The Congress has drawn up a three-phase strategy to present its demands. First phase: 60 seats With Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's approval, the Congress has identified 60 seats that it wants to retain under its quota under all circumstances. These constituencies are spread across regions ranging from Purvanchal to western Uttar Pradesh. Second phase: 50 seats The second phase will focus on 50 constituencies where the Congress has performed in previous elections. The party will pay particular attention to seats in the Saharanpur, Meerut and Moradabad regions of western Uttar Pradesh. Third phase: 70 seats In the third phase, the Congress will stake its claim to another 70 seats based on the strength of its organisation and its prospects in those constituencies. These include seats linked to parliamentary constituencies such as Rae Bareli, Amethi and Prayagraj. SP and Congress to discuss constituencies individually According to Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress's Uttar Pradesh in-charge, the meeting will focus on discussing each Assembly constituency individually rather than deciding the total number of seats to be shared. Congress leaders say the objective of seat-sharing is not to create differences within the alliance but to ensure its electoral success. The party argues that it should be given an opportunity to contest constituencies where its position is stronger than that of the SP. Meanwhile, the SP has advised its leaders against making public statements on seat-sharing. After the meetings in Delhi on Monday and Tuesday, representatives of both parties will submit reports on the discussions to their respective top leaderships. The next round of negotiations will be planned based on these reports.

stories.title: Sister ties Rakhi on wrist of martyred brother:Wife faints, mother pleads to see his face one last time; 2 soldiers died during military exercise
stories.summary: The bodies of two soldiers killed during a military exercise in Haryana reached Uttar Pradesh on Monday morning. As Naik Manish Kumar's (26) body reached Shamli, the family was overwhelmed with grief. His sisters tied rakhis on their martyred soldier brother's wrist. His wife fainted while crying. His mother broke down as she pleaded to see her son's face one last time. As the bier was lifted for the funeral procession, his mother ran over and clung to his body. She kept saying, "Show me my beloved son's face one last time." Meanwhile, the body of Naik Ankush Kumar (29) reached Badaun. The entire village turned out to pay tribute. Family members kept consoling his wife. Their young children repeatedly asked their mother, "What happened to Papa? Will he never come back?" Manish and Ankush were run over by a tank during a routine military exercise. The tank passed over both soldiers. They died on the spot. Three heartbreaking pictures- As soon as the army personnel closed the coffin, the mother began sobbing uncontrollably. She pleaded, "Let me see my son's face one last time." First, let us learn about Naik Manish Kumar... Naik Manish Kumar was the only son in his family. He had three sisters. Two of his sisters, Guddan and Meenakshi, are married. His younger sister Ritu lives at home with their father Ramkumar, mother Manju and Manish's wife, Bulbul. Manish's body was brought to Bajjhu village in Shamli at 9 a.m. in a flower-decorated vehicle. As soon as the body reached the house, his mother, Manju, and wife, Bulbul, broke down. When Army personnel opened the coffin and showed them his face, they began wailing uncontrollably. When family members tried to console them and move them away, they continued staring intently at Manish's face. As Bulbul began to lose consciousness, a woman supported her. When she patted her face, Bulbul let out a scream. Her brother then helped support her. Clinging to their brother's photograph, his sisters kept saying that the light of the household had gone out. "With whom will we celebrate Raksha Bandhan now? Whom will we tie the rakhi to? We have lost our only support." Manish's father, Ramveer, is also a retired Army personnel. He said that if he had had more sons, he would have sent them to the Army as well. After the final viewing, the funeral procession travelled about 2 km to the village cremation ground. His cousin, Suraj, lit the funeral pyre. BKU president Naresh Tikait, former Cabinet minister Sanjeev Balyan and Lok Dal MLA Prasann Chaudhary also attended the funeral procession. Now learn about Badaun's Ankush... Naik Ankush Kumar lived in Aamgaon under the Civil Lines police station area in Badaun. His cousin Amit Kumar said that Ankush had spoken to his children over the phone at around 2 p.m. on Saturday. He was due to return home on Sunday. But the accident occurred before that. He is survived by his wife, Pooja, son Harsh (7) and daughter Nandini (11). His younger brother Vineet has a job. Ankur joined the Indian Army in 2010 from Kanthi in Nagpur. He was promoted two years ago. Ankur's father, Adesh Kumar, is also a retired Army personnel. His uncle Ghanendra Singh and his elder uncle's son, Amit Kumar, have also served in the Army and have since retired. Find out how the accident happened involving a tank... A routine military exercise was underway in the Bhojraj area, with around 32 tanks moving together. The movement of the heavy tanks raised a thick cloud of dust in the area, significantly reducing visibility ahead. During this, a tank driver could not see the personnel deployed at the front, and the tank ran over both of them. They were taken to a military hospital in critical condition Immediately after the accident, Army personnel and officers present at the site attended to both injured men. They were taken to the military hospital in Hisar without delay, but doctors could not save them because their injuries were severe.

stories.title: 'Study hard and become a prince':CM Yogi assures Class 8 student of cricket coaching after hearing his dream at Janata Darshan
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took on the role of a mentor during his Janata Darshan programme on Monday, where he heard people's grievances and encouraged a young boy to pursue his sporting ambitions. Prince Sahu, a Class 8 student from Gonda, told the Chief Minister that he wanted to become a cricketer but his family's poor financial condition made it difficult to afford coaching fees and cricket equipment. Yogi assured him that financial constraints would not come in the way of his dream. He said the government would arrange cricket coaching and admission for him. CM advises student to balance studies and cricket Prince, a resident of Padri Parasray village in the Itiathok area of Gonda district, told the Chief Minister that he had been interested in cricket since childhood and wanted to pursue a career in the sport. However, his family's financial difficulties made it difficult to pay for coaching and buy a cricket kit. The Chief Minister spoke to the boy for around four to five minutes and guided him. He advised Prince to focus on his studies alongside cricket, pointing out that he was currently in Class 8. Yogi said arrangements for his admission to cricket coaching would be made after he passed his examinations with good marks. "Son, your name is Prince, so study hard and become a prince. Play as much as you want, but education is equally important," the Chief Minister told him. CM directs officials to resolve public grievances During the Janata Darshan programme, Yogi met people individually, received their written complaints and listened to their problems. He directed officials present at the venue to ensure that all complaints were resolved within a stipulated timeframe. He also stressed the need for fairness and sensitivity so that complainants were satisfied with the action taken. Assures financial assistance for medical treatment The Chief Minister also assured people seeking financial assistance for medical treatment that no needy patient would be denied treatment because of a lack of money. He said the government would provide financial assistance as soon as it received the estimated cost of the patient's treatment.

stories.title: ‘Dream big, build character, not just CVs’:Air Force Chief in Lucknow urges students to aim high; Shubhanshu Shukla says their experiments could reach space
stories.summary: A science fair was organised at CMS Golf City campus in Lucknow. Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Chief of the Air Staff, and astronaut Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla attended the event. They visited the students’ science exhibition and learnt about their models and experiments. During the event, Ashutosh Dixit urged young people to dream big, work hard and build strong character. He said students should not focus only on building their CVs but also on strengthening their character. He advised them to remain humble after achieving success. He also said Shubhanshu Shukla’s achievements remind us that the sky is not the limit. CMS students’ experiments are being prepared for possible testing in space. The Voyager Mixstix Microgravity Student Research Programme has been launched for this purpose. In collaboration with Earthizen and Israel’s Rakia mission, students from Classes 6 to 12 will develop experiments. Selected experiments may be tested aboard the International Space Station (ISS) in 2027. Robotics, drones and mobile planetarium among the attractions The fair will feature live demonstrations of scientific experiments, research presentations and discussions on space science. Students will get to see a mobile planetarium, a giant replica of the Moon, Arthaizen's space chariot and the Infosys Mobile Experience Bus. Floating models of Indian Navy warships will also be displayed.

stories.title: Four, including mother and son, killed in Mathura:Swift car crashes into truck, 5 injured; family had come from Madhya Pradesh to visit Vrindavan
stories.summary: A speeding Maruti Swift car rammed into the rear of a truck in Mathura. Four people, including a mother and her son, died in the accident. The deceased include two children and two women. Five other occupants of the car were injured. The family had travelled from Bhind in Madhya Pradesh to visit Mathura. The accident took place on the National Highway in the Jaint area at around 7.30 am on Monday, when the family was travelling from Barsana to Ramanreti. The collision was so severe that the car was badly mangled. The people inside were trapped in the wreckage. Police reached the spot, rescued those trapped in the car and rushed them to hospital. Police said Devashish was driving the car, which had nine people on board, including his wife and children. Devashish's son Rudra (4), his maternal aunt Ruby (32), Ruby's son Kanhaiya (10) and Ruby's friend Jyoti (30) died in the accident. Devashish, his mother Asha Devi, his wife Girja Devi, his daughter Gauri (5) and Jyoti's daughter Palak (12) were injured. Take a look at the pictures… Family performed parikrama throughout the night; accident suspected to have occurred due to driver dozing off According to the police, the car rammed into the truck from behind. The investigation revealed that the family had spent the entire night visiting temples and performing parikrama in Mathura-Vrindavan. This meant they had not slept. Devashish was driving the car, and police suspect that he may have dozed off, causing the vehicle to crash into a stationary truck. The injured have been admitted to Sarvodaya Hospital. One of them is in critical condition. District Magistrate Chandra Prakash Singh said the government would bear the entire cost of treatment for the injured. Yogi Adityanath has announced financial assistance of ₹1.5 lakh each for the families of the deceased.

stories.summary: An IndiGo flight travelling from Pune to Patna was diverted to Lucknow late on Sunday night because of bad weather in Patna. The aircraft was landed at Lucknow Airport as weather conditions in Patna were unsuitable. Flight 6E 653 landed safely in Lucknow at 2:45 a.m. on 23 November. 187 passengers and 5 infants were on board According to information from the airport, the IndiGo flight had departed from Pune for Patna. There were 187 passengers, five infants and six crew members on board. A total of 198 people were travelling on the aircraft. The flight was commanded by pilot in command Amit Sharma. Due to bad weather in Patna, the aircraft was sent to Lucknow instead of landing at its scheduled destination. Departed for Patna after around five hours After remaining at Lucknow Airport for around five hours, the aircraft departed for Patna at 8 a.m. The flight schedule was disrupted due to the bad weather, and passengers faced delays.

stories.title: Yogi gets emotional remembering his mother:She could not believe it when he arrived seeking alms; asked, 'Son, what have you done to yourself?'
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi wrote an emotional letter remembering his mother. He wrote that a mother can take everyone's place, but no one can take a mother's place. He also shared with people the story of asking his mother for alms after renouncing worldly life. In 'Yogi's Letter', the Chief Minister wrote, "Following the rules of monastic life, I called out for alms at the door. Hearing my voice, my mother came outside. Before she could say anything, I said, 'Mother, please give me alms.'" Composing herself, his mother said, "Son, what have you done to yourself? What was lacking at home that you are begging?" I replied, "Mother, monastic life is now my dharma, and a yogi's hunger can be satisfied only through alms." "I have not come here to stay, but to receive alms. Whatever you give me as alms will help fulfil my resolve." His mother then respected her monk son's decision and gave him alms. Yogi's mother, Savitri Devi, died at her home in Panchur, her ancestral village in Pauri, Uttarakhand, on Friday. She was 91. Her last rites were performed at Chandi Ghat in Haridwar on Saturday. Yogi lit the funeral pyre along with his younger brother. What did Yogi write? Read it in five points 1. Without mothers, neither would we exist nor would any living being Yogi wrote, "This letter is dedicated to every mother, without whom life would not be possible. If there were no mothers, neither would we exist nor would any living being, and this world would not exist either. A mother is not merely the one who gives birth; she is the creator of the entire universe. Even God is born to a mother." 2. Remembering my mother brings tears to my eyes Today, remembering my mother, my eyes are welling up with tears. Losing one's mother is not merely like losing a person; it feels as though a dense shade from over one's head, unconditional love and emotional support have all been taken away. 3. An old moment suddenly flashed before my eyes When my first teacher and the mother who taught me my letters departed this world, an old moment suddenly flashed before my eyes: after more than three years of becoming a monk, I was standing outside the door of my home in saffron robes. During that journey from Gorakhpur to my village, Panchur, a flood of emotions was surging through my mind. 4. Trying to fulfil my duty towards all mothers and sisters There are some debts in life that can never be repaid, but we can certainly fulfil our duty. Since entering politics and social service, I have been trying to fulfil this duty towards all the mothers and sisters in the state. Our true respect for every mother will be shown when every citizen of the state takes a pledge today to support a mother who has no one to rely on, understand the suffering of a mother in need and bring a smile to the face of a distressed mother.

stories.title: Cylinder blast at councillor's house in Jalaun, 23 injured:13 children and 5 women among them; 5 children critical, burns of up to 60%
stories.summary: A gas cylinder exploded at councillor Mata Prasad's house in Orai, Jalaun. The incident left 23 people with burns, including 13 children, 5 women and 5 men. Nineteen people who suffered serious burns have been referred to Jhansi Medical College. Ten of them, including 5 young children, remain in critical condition. They have suffered burns to between 20% and 60% of their bodies. At midnight late on Sunday, Jhansi Range Inspector General Akash Kulhari reached the medical college. He spoke to the injured and their family members to gather information about the incident. The IG said, "A fire broke out after the gas cylinder leaked. Some children and women from the settlement went to watch the fire, when the cylinder exploded. A team of 15 doctors is treating the injured." See two pictures- Here is the full sequence of events... Family members were making tea at the home of councillor Mata Prasad, a resident of Shantinagar in Orai, on Sunday evening. During this, the gas cylinder suddenly caught fire. Before the family could understand what was happening, the fire had already intensified and the cylinder exploded with a loud blast. The force of the explosion sent pieces of the cylinder flying into the surrounding area. More than 10 members of the councillor's family, along with people from the neighbourhood, were caught in the blast. The loud explosion caused panic in the area. A crowd gathered at the scene. Fire brigade douses blaze, 19 people with burn injuries brought to Jhansi As soon as the accident was reported, police and fire brigade teams reached the spot. Fire brigade personnel brought the fire under control after a strenuous operation. With the help of local residents and the police, the injured were taken to the district hospital and Government Medical College, Orai. From there, doctors referred 19 seriously burned people to Jhansi Medical College. 15 doctors deployed in Jhansi, principal takes charge The administration went on alert after the cylinder blast. The AD Health officer called Jhansi Medical College Principal Dr Sudhir Singh and instructed him to make arrangements. Jhansi District Magistrate Gaurang Rathi also alerted the hospital administration. A team of 15 doctors from the surgery and plastic surgery departments was then deployed. The beds in the plastic surgery ward were also vacated. The injured began arriving from 10 p.m. The 19th injured person, Pushpendra, reached the medical college at 12:35 a.m. All the injured have been admitted, and treatment has begun. These people suffered serious burns Dayawati (32) and Bablu (45), admitted to Jhansi Medical College, have suffered 60% burns; Vaishnavi (8) has suffered 55% burns; Dayanand (41) and Munni Devi (62) have suffered 50% burns; and Somwati (45) has suffered 40% burns. Krish (7) has suffered 40% burns, while Anshika (10) and Umang (9) have suffered 30% burns, and Dipesh (8) up to 25% burns. The remaining injured people have suffered burns ranging from 5% to 20%.

stories.title: Truck that killed elephant in Gorakhpur seized:CCTV helped identify vehicle; driver fled after delivering milk and parking it in Baghagada
stories.summary: Police have identified the truck that hit an elephant returning from a wedding procession in the Belipar area of Gorakhpur. The elephant, which was seriously injured in the accident, died during treatment. Two men riding on it were also injured. The accident took place near Mehroli village on the Gorakhpur-Varanasi Highway between 5.30 am and 5.55 am on November 21. Elephant owner Rafi Ullah Ansari was returning from a wedding procession with his elephant when a speeding truck hit it from behind. The driver fled with the truck after the accident. Using CCTV footage, police traced the vehicle bearing registration number UP78 MN 0529 and seized it. A case has been registered based on the mahout's complaint, and efforts are underway to trace the absconding driver. Truck hits elephant while returning from wedding Rafi Ullah Ansari, a resident of Sevai village, had attended a wedding procession in Gajpur with his elephant on November 21. He was returning home the following morning. His sons, Jafar Ansari and Firoz Ansari, were riding on the elephant. The group was travelling on foot towards Gorakhpur. When they reached near Rajkumar's brick kiln in Mehroli village under Belipar police station limits, a speeding truck approached from behind and hit the elephant. The elephant suffered serious injuries, while Jafar and Firoz were also hurt. The truck driver fled the spot immediately after the collision. Elephant dies during treatment at hospital The injured elephant was taken to Rachit Hospital in Gorakhpur for treatment. Doctors tried to save its life, but it died during treatment. Meanwhile, Jafar and Firoz were taken to the district hospital by ambulance. The elephant's death has left its owner and family members mourning. Driver leaves truck in Baghagada after milk delivery After fleeing the accident site, the driver allegedly delivered milk at another location before parking the truck in Baghagada and escaping. Meanwhile, police examined CCTV footage from the accident site and nearby areas. Based on the footage, they identified the truck bearing registration number UP78 MN 0529 and seized it. FIR registered on mahout's complaint; driver yet to be traced A case was registered at Belipar police station on November 22 based on a complaint filed by elephant mahout Rafi Ullah Ansari. The FIR mentions the truck's registration number, UP78 MN 0529, but the driver's name and address are not known. Police have registered a case against the unidentified driver. A sub-inspector has been assigned to investigate the matter. Efforts are underway to trace the driver using CCTV footage and other evidence.

stories.title: Rain alert issued for four UP districts today:Dense fog to cover eastern UP; Hardoi records lowest temperature at 11°C
stories.summary: Rain is likely in four districts of Uttar Pradesh on Monday, while dense fog is expected in the eastern part of the state. The weather has changed in UP due to Cyclone Akvan and snowfall in the mountains. Light rain is likely in Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli and Varanasi. Dense fog is also expected in eastern Uttar Pradesh. On Sunday, Hardoi was the coldest district in the state, recording a minimum temperature of 11°C. Dense fog covered 24 districts in the morning, including Prayagraj, Kaushambi and Pratapgarh. Visibility dropped to such low levels in several places that people could barely see beyond 10 metres on the roads. Amid the rising cold and fog, the Uttar Pradesh Relief Commissioner has urged people to step out in the morning only when necessary. People have also been advised to take special care of children and elderly family members. Temperatures likely to drop further next week Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, said the cyclone that had formed over the Bay of Bengal had weakened. As a result, northerly and north-westerly winds have started gaining strength, replacing easterly winds. He said night temperatures in western Uttar Pradesh would gradually fall. Fog may occur in some areas during the morning. "Cold conditions will intensify from next week. However, people will have to wait a little longer for severe cold," Singh said. Farmers advised to take precautions during sowing and irrigation With rain likely in November, farmers have been advised to take precautions while managing their rabi crops. In particular, farmers in eastern Uttar Pradesh should ensure proper drainage in fields while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard. Waterlogging in low-lying fields could damage crops. Farmers should avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields that already have sufficient moisture due to rainfall. Decisions on sowing and irrigation should be based on weather conditions and soil moisture.
