stories.summary: Mamata Banerjee's younger brother Swapan 'Babun' Banerjee approached Kolkata Police seeking an FIR against nephew and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee, alleging intimidation and obstruction of a blood donation camp. The complaint adds to the family's long-standing feud, which has acquired a political dimension amid Babun's growing proximity to BJP leaders and repeated praise for West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.

stories.title: ‘Today one Deepam, tomorrow temples?’ Vaishnaw slams TVK govt over Thiruparankundram Deepam row
Danish king’s 1495 flagship wreck yields medieval chain mail, raising questions about its soldiers
stories.summary: Recently, underwater archaeologists made a fascinating discovery: well-preserved fragments of medieval chain-mail armor found near an ammunition-tool chest. This remarkable find sheds light on the soldiers and military gear that were present on the Griffin, which tragically sank in 1495. With the armor's notable quality, researchers are keenly examining its historical implications.

stories.title: 'I'd like to have him': Trump on Putin's possible G20 visit amid Ukraine war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said that Vladimir Putin may join the G20 summit if he decides to do so. Trump highlighted the vital role of diplomacy in addressing the ongoing Russia-Ukraine crisis. Trump also said Putin wanted to reach an agreement to end the Russia-Ukraine war, arguing that maintaining a cordial relationship with the Russian leader was important to negotiations.

stories.title: North Dakota Court revives woman’s claim over water main flood damage
'Nuclear holocaust' risk: Trump claims Iran missiles can reach Europe
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed concerns about Iran's missile capabilities and the prospect of regional instability. He stated that Iran could potentially launch nuclear attacks on Israel and surrounding countries in the Middle East. Trump emphasized the necessity of achieving peace in the region while supporting local countries until they can defend themselves. He noted that Iran does not currently possess a nuclear weapon, which is significant under international agreements.

stories.title: 'We love Yogi very much': Sanjay Raut's praise puts spotlight on BJP's biggest UP question
New York mother sought land back from daughter after 2012 transfer; appeals court upheld daughter's ownership
stories.summary: A New York mother transferred four parcels of land to her daughter during financial difficulties in 2012. The mother attempted to reclaim three properties after her daughter planned to sell them in 2024. The court upheld the daughter's ownership, concluding that the transfer was an outright gift without any promise of return. Although the mother maintained some involvement with the properties, this did not imply retained ownership.

stories.title: Trusts move HC to block chair’s casting vote at Tata Sons meet
stories.summary: Tata Trusts have launched a legal challenge against Tata Sons concerning the chairman's casting vote, citing governance issues before a crucial board meeting. They argue that earlier resolutions breach the company’s articles and are seeking compensation. Holding a significant stake in Tata Sons, the Trusts aim to ensure their nominee directors' votes carry equal weight, reflecting the continuing tensions over control in India's largest conglomerate.

stories.title: Cairo fuel tanker inferno: Driver suspect held after explosion left 31 dead
stories.summary: After the tragic incident in Cairo, where fuel tanker overturned and ignited, resulting in 31 fatalities and injuring 26 others. The driver, just 21 years old, is being held for questioning as authorities investigate potential drug influence at the time of the crash. Forensic teams are actively working to identify the remains of the deceased while families utilize social media to locate their missing loved ones.

stories.title: 'Record-setting error': Trump claims fake GDP data before midterms, demands probe
stories.summary: Donald Trump expressed concerns over revised GDP figures, claiming they were previously misrepresented before the midterm elections. He called for an investigation into what he described as a record-setting error in the reported figures. Additionally, he criticized various groups, including immigrants and Minnesota's Somali population, suggesting they contribute negatively to the country. Moreover, he defended ongoing renovations at the White House, emphasizing the need for maintenance due to its age.

stories.title: Florida couple’s claim of toxic mould, snake in daughter’s bedroom gets fresh hearing after appeals court ruling
stories.summary: A Florida couple, William and Ashley Merryman, reported significant damage to their home and health risks. After filing a lawsuit, they sought a preliminary injunction against state agencies linked to environmental changes. The district court initially denied their request, citing delayed action and potential financial remedies. However, the appeals court found faults in the lower court's reasoning and has remanded the case for reconsideration.

stories.title: In September, the first confirmed natural sea turtle nests on the US West Coast were found
stories.summary: In a historic first for Southern California, two olive ridley sea turtle nests were discovered in September 2026. Due to an imminent tropical storm, the eggs were carefully relocated and monitored at the Aquarium of the Pacific. On November 14, 54 hatchlings emerged and were released into the ocean, followed by another 21 from a second nest on Huntington Beach the next day.

stories.title: Big, fat Bihar wedding makes global headlines
stories.summary: Mokama MLA Anant Singh's daughter Shivangi's wedding attracted attention due to its enormous scale and extravagant displays. Over 400,000 guests were invited, with six helipads and a massive feast prepared by 500 cooks. However, food distribution led to chaos as guests struggled to find plates amidst the crowd. Animal welfare concerns arose from the event, particularly regarding horse racing and a captive elephant.

stories.title: India playing leading role in global war on terror, says Amit Shah
stories.summary: Amit Shah, the Union home minister, reaffirmed India's unwavering dedication to fighting terrorism while honoring the memories of those affected by the 26/11 attacks. He praised the bravery of both soldiers and innocent civilians, asserting that the Modi government’s unwavering stance against terrorism is garnering global recognition. Shah also highlighted that united action is essential, as terrorism remains a grave threat to humanity.

stories.title: Colombo Security Conclave reaffirms commitment to promote regional peace
stories.summary: The Maldives hosted the 8th NSA-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave, uniting member states in their shared goal of enhancing regional peace and security. By emphasizing capacity-building and collaboration, the attendees laid out a roadmap for security cooperation through 2026-27, marking a commitment to address evolving challenges. India reaffirmed its resolve to engage actively with CSC countries to foster stronger ties and collective security measures.

stories.title: Mumbai police issue lookout circulars against CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das
stories.summary: CJP co-convener Saurav Das was barred from flying to London due to a lookout circular. The Centre informed the Delhi high court that this action was taken at Mumbai police's request. Saurav Das's passport is under scrutiny for several discrepancies regarding his identity. His legal team argued that the travel ban infringes upon his fundamental rights. The court proceedings continue as he prepares to respond to the notice issued.

stories.title: An Ohio lawyer denied partnership over gender wins $2 million award upheld after 9-year legal fight
stories.summary: In a landmark ruling, Pamela Pantages, a lawyer from Ohio, has triumphed in her discrimination lawsuit against her previous employer. The Eighth District Court of Appeals upheld a $2 million jury award, affirming her allegations of being denied partnership due to age and gender bias, as noted in the firm's owner’s comments. This decision corroborates the jury's findings of sex discrimination and contract breaches at The Becker Law Firm.

stories.title: South African father-son duo build record-breaking drone reaching 408 mph
stories.summary: On December 11, 2025, Mike and Luke Bell shattered records by piloting their Peregreen V4 quadcopter to an astonishing average speed of 408.60 mph, making it the fastest battery-powered quadcopter in history. This remarkable achievement resulted from their dedication to innovative design and rigorous testing, employing advanced aerodynamics and cutting-edge 3D printing techniques. It is a monumental step forward in the realm of drone racing.

stories.title: 'Very strange': Zelenskyy questions Trump's Putin bonhomie, US support for Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy voiced serious concerns regarding US President Donald Trump's close ties with Vladimir Putin, whom he labeled an aggressor resembling Hitler. He expressed disappointment over Trump's positive remarks about Putin while Ukraine faces ongoing conflict. In contrast, Trump described Putin as a friend who genuinely seeks to end the war, revealing the complexities both leaders face in resolving this crisis.

stories.title: 28 ancient Gallic coins and skull fragments hint at lost sanctuary in France
stories.summary: Archaeologists exploring Bure in northeastern France uncovered 28 ancient Gallic coins alongside human skull fragments. The site is believed to be a Late Iron Age sanctuary used by the Leuci. In addition to the coins, a miniature bronze wagon wheel was also found, suggesting ritual significance. The discovery contributes to understanding the cultural and religious practices of ancient Gaul. Ongoing studies aim to clarify the site's history and purpose.

stories.title: Delhi high court nixes order to cancel NGO’s FCRA licence
stories.summary: In a pivotal decision, the Delhi High Court has ruled in favor of the Socio Legal Information Centre, restoring its FCRA licence that was previously annulled by the Home Ministry. The court indicated that there was a lack of evidence to support accusations of the NGO's anti-government actions. Moreover, the court deemed the assertions of the NGO negatively impacting India's image on the global stage as without merit.

stories.title: Jolly Cheery’s Journey: Tree travels with low-emission transport; tradition links Norway and Britain
stories.summary: This year, London welcomes a spectacular 21-metre Norwegian spruce named Jolly Cheery for its Christmas display. Selected through public voting, this tree represents the enduring friendship between Norway and the UK. To minimize environmental impact, it will be transported in an eco-friendly manner and adorned with energy-efficient lights, set to be unveiled on December 3. Post-Christmas, it will be composted, promoting sustainability.

stories.title: Judicial member must on bench to confirm PMLA attachment, says Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that a judicial member must be present in the bench deciding asset attachments. This decision focuses on ensuring legal objectivity in the proceedings related to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The ruling addresses the competence of administrative members in handling questions of law and conflicting judgments. The judgment is applicable prospectively and does not allow reopening of past decisions.

stories.title: Bihar move illegal, says Supreme Court, quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, the Supreme Court has annulled the Bihar government's controversial decision to release Anand Mohan, who was serving time for murder. The state's attempt to modify prison regulations for his early exit was found unconstitutional. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu criticized the justification threshold for such a change, ultimately mandating that Anand Mohan must surrender within a month.

stories.title: Supreme Court to banks: Give nod to try officials in 7 days
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has demanded that HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital, and PNB Home Finance provide unconditional sanctions. These sanctions involve officials implicated in collusion with builders in housing fraud schemes. The banks' CMDs must articulate their non-compliance in court if not met within a week. CBI’s investigations have led to chargesheets, and trials will commence once the necessary sanctions are secured, underscoring the urgency for timely judicial processes.

stories.title: 7 months on, mediation in Sunjay Kapur case hits deadlock
stories.summary: Mediation efforts between Rani Kapur and Priya Sachdev Kapur over Sunjay Kapur's estate ended without resolution. Former Chief Justice DY Chandrachud, who mediated the dispute, reported reaching an impasse. Despite 15 sessions aimed at settlement, both parties did not show flexibility or understanding. The Supreme Court noted that no settlement can be forced upon unwilling parties. The court decided to close the mediation process and will issue a ruling soon.

stories.title: Opposition worried, feels government won’t risk another defeat
stories.summary: The call for a Parliament session by the BJP to discuss the delimitation bill has taken the opposition by surprise. As uncertainty looms, there are rising concerns among opposition parties about the potential impact on their voting power. The DMK, having previously opposed similar measures, now adopts a cautious stance. In contrast, Congress leaders maintain confidence, even as the government's influence grows.

stories.title: Special Parliament session from November 30; women’s quota on agenda
stories.summary: Beginning November 30, the government is set to convene a brief session of Parliament focused on critical delimitation bills. These proposed laws are designed to establish a women's quota in the Lok Sabha by 2029, boosting its membership to 850 seats. Despite previous challenges in passing the bill, the government is optimistic about rallying support.

stories.title: Supreme Court raps MNCs for ‘double standard’ on food quality
stories.summary: The Supreme Court addressed concerns regarding the quality of food products offered by multinational companies in India. It emphasized the need for uniform standards across different countries to protect Indian consumers. The court directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to enforce strict labeling regulations. Companies must not alter product compositions or conceal ingredient information. This ruling aims to ensure consumer health and transparency in labeling practices.

stories.title: Funeral director wins A$48,966 after employer sacks him over police clearance
stories.summary: A 65-year-old Australian funeral director was dismissed after police revoked a clearance required for body-transfer duties he had stopped performing months earlier. The Fair Work Commission found the dismissal unfair, noting that the employee was unlikely to resume the work and that the employer had not properly challenged the police decision.

stories.title: 314 years after Dutch ship sank off Australia, 23 stolen silver coins return from California and Amsterdam
stories.summary: After extensive efforts, Australia has reclaimed twenty-three silver coins from the infamous Zuytdorp shipwreck, which was lost at sea in 1712. The recovery operations spanned both the Netherlands and the United States, revealing a surge in illicit interest since 2019. In light of this, Australian authorities ramped up their monitoring, culminating in local resident Ashley Patterson's guilty plea for breaching underwater heritage laws linked to these invaluable artifacts.

stories.title: Pension, insurance for 15 lakh gig workers likely by year-end
stories.summary: The government plans to announce a pension scheme and health insurance for gig workers soon. Workers enrolled on the e-Shram portal will be the primary beneficiaries of these initiatives. The National Social Security Board will discuss contributory models, including a 2% turnover-based contribution from platforms. Trade unions have suggested immediate health and accident cover for these workers during onboarding.

stories.title: US pilot's eBay purchase turns into a discovery linked to the Tuskegee Airmen
No content from Pakistan to be shown in India, government reminds Netflix
stories.summary: In a move reflecting ongoing tensions, the Indian Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has urged Netflix to limit access to Pakistani content, particularly an upcoming series set to debut on December 4. This action follows previous advisories related to national security concerns amid the India-Pakistan conflict. Netflix has not clarified the series' availability in India, as industry groups pursue legal actions against Pakistani media.

stories.title: Supreme Court sets timer for FSSAI, companies to implement warning labels
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has instructed the FSSAI to implement front-of-package labeling within four months. Companies will have one year to comply with these regulations after the notification. Labels will indicate high levels of sugar, saturated fat, and salt inside red hexagonal shapes to protect consumer health. The court emphasized the importance of preventing public health crises associated with unhealthy food consumption.

stories.title: Oregon family renovates free abandoned mobile home for $14k so mom and twins host Thanksgiving
stories.summary: An Oregon family took on the challenge of revamping a deserted mobile home into a cozy space for their relatives. Lyman Branson II and his family poured months of effort into fixing the property for Betty Branson and her daughters. Despite budget hurdles, they created a safe haven. Just in time for Thanksgiving, they received the occupancy certificate, allowing them to celebrate their first holiday together in their new home.

stories.title: Federal Appeals Court reopens Trump's route to challenge his New York conviction
stories.summary: In a surprising turn of events, Donald Trump’s legal team has been afforded a fresh opportunity to challenge his criminal conviction. A federal appeals court has chosen to revisit his application to shift jurisdiction from New York. This could pave the way for Trump to assert presidential immunity, potentially leading to an overturn of his conviction.

stories.title: Tamworth Castle restorers uncover 1960s cigarette packet and hidden treasures
stories.summary: The £1.9 million restoration of Tamworth Castle is revealing intriguing historical artifacts. Among the recent discoveries are a cigarette packet from the 1950s and a 1968 newspaper, shedding light on the lives of its past inhabitants. Additionally, restorers found an 18th or 19th-century lead-lined sink, enhancing our understanding of the castle's historical usage.

stories.title: Coastal Topi Numbers Rebound: Raabia Hawa wins Tusk award; ranger teams and communities protect ecosystems
stories.summary: Raabia Hawa has been honored with the 2026 Tusk Award for her exceptional dedication to wildlife conservation. As a former radio personality, she pivoted her career to enhance efforts in protecting endangered species in Kenya. Through her founded Ulinzi Africa Foundation, she has championed anti-poaching campaigns, directly aiding in the resurgence of coastal topi populations, and emphasizing the essential role of community engagement in conservation success.

stories.title: California recycling business faces eviction after Metro buys leased land for light rail project, appeals court rules
stories.summary: A recycling company in Van Nuys is contesting its eviction following the acquisition of its property by the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority. The California Court of Appeal has decided that the sale to Metro terminated the existing lease. The business owners argued that eminent domain processes should have applied, but the court disagreed, allowing Metro's unlawful detainer case to continue.

stories.title: Ex-terrorist fugitive’s 19-year run ends in arrest
stories.summary: Mohammad Mansha, a former terrorist, was arrested by a joint police team in Tral. He had evaded law enforcement for nearly two decades since laying down arms in 2007. Authorities revealed he was wanted in at least 13 criminal cases, including murder and conspiracy. His criminal activities included the killing of a police officer back in 2000. The operation involved meticulous planning and credible intelligence from various police units.

stories.title: Sheshnag Lake row: Karan Singh questions need for wider road, PDP steps up heat
stories.summary: The ongoing debate about heavy machinery's presence near Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath Yatra route is drawing intense scrutiny. Karan Singh pointed out that not all pilgrimage paths necessitate vehicle accessibility for pilgrims. Meanwhile, Mehbooba Mufti demanded transparency and public disclosure of any agreements linked to construction efforts. The J&K government refuted claims about construction, insisting that machinery is operating at a considerable distance.

stories.title: Ashley Cain's Foundation raises £3 million for childhood cancer research and treatment
stories.summary: In loving memory of their daughter, Azaylia Diamond Cain, Ashley Cain and Safiyya Vorajee founded The Azaylia Foundation. This charity is dedicated to enhancing childhood cancer treatment and funding research, having raised over £3 million since its launch. With its commitment to boosting early diagnosis and innovative therapies, the foundation collaborates with UK universities and offers Treatment Pathway Grants to broaden treatment options.

stories.title: 17-year-old's website lets people send messages from beyond the grave
stories.summary: 17-year-old Alice Footer from Australia's Gold Coast has developed FromBeyond.co, a website that lets people record personal messages and schedule their delivery to loved ones on birthdays, Christmas and other occasions, even after their death. Inspired by her grandmother's stories and worried that younger family members might lose touch with their family's past, Alice created the platform to preserve memories for future generations.

stories.title: India-Germany submarine partnership can act as a catalyst for Indo-Pacific security: German envoy
stories.summary: Germany's commitment to technology transfer under the P-75I submarine project with India is being emphasized. This partnership aims to enhance India's capabilities in undersea warfare technology, including Air-Independent Propulsion. Both nations share mutual trust regarding the protection of sensitive technologies and strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region. The deal may also lead India to become a hub for submarine manufacturing for Southeast Asian nations.

stories.title: Kashmir clerics split over Vande Mataram
stories.summary: A religious dispute over the national song Vande Mataram has intensified among clerics in Kashmir. Sunni scholar Maulana Abdul Rashid Dawoodi urged for a fatwa regarding standing during its rendition. Meanwhile, grand mufti Nasir-ul-Islam declared participation as impermissible under Islamic law. Several clerics expressed regret after attending a function where Vande Mataram was played. The controversy stems from a recent Union home ministry directive mandating its performance at official events.

stories.title: Ohio court says lawyers must prove fair fees after client secures $250,000 car settlement herself
stories.summary: Amber Kopanski settled her car crash claim directly with Progressive Direct Insurance Company for $250,000 after parting ways with her lawyers. Her former law firm, Rumizen Weisman Co., Ltd., sought payment for its legal fees and costs after her settlement. The appeals court ruled that the firm cannot simply apply its contract percentage for payment determination.

stories.title: US customs uncover 440 fake luxury jewellery pieces worth $2.4 million
30 missing ultras working from Pakistan & PoK to revive terrorism in J&K: Police
stories.summary: Thirty terrorists from Reasi district crossed over to Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir between 1991 and 2003. They obtained training and arms to launch activities against India while disrupting peace in Jammu and Kashmir. These individuals are now associated with Hizbul Mujahideen, facilitating the supply of arms and funds. Police have registered an FIR against them under various laws, including the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

stories.title: I’m no troublemaker, won’t sign peace bond: Wangchuk
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk, representing the Leh Apex Body, was called upon by the district administration to discuss a peace bond. While he attended the meeting, Wangchuk declined to endorse any bond, deeming it unnecessary. He was given one week to address an extensive notice filled with allegations; however, his attorney later received a demand for a quicker response by November 28, prompting concerns about administrative transparency.

stories.title: Road ministry tightens bidding norms to keep poor performers out of fully govt-funded projects
stories.summary: The road transport ministry has updated the bidding process for contractors to ensure better project execution. Performance ratings will now determine contractors’ eligibility for new projects, replacing the old financial year assessment approach. Stricter norms for joint ventures and improved technical eligibility conditions for major infrastructure projects have also been implemented. The revised Request for Proposal framework emphasizes transparency by requiring bidders to disclose ongoing disputes.

stories.title: Florida court overturns fraud findings in $34.7m tobacco death case, orders new damages trial
stories.summary: In a significant development, Frances Bessent-Dixon's lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds was impacted by a recent court ruling. The appeals court dismissed the prior jury's fraud verdict, necessitating a new trial focused on damages. Tyrone M. Dixon, Bessent-Dixon's late husband, passed away from throat cancer caused by smoking, with R.J. Reynolds asserting that he was aware of the dangers of tobacco.

stories.title: English detectorist finds rare 380-year-old coin in Essex field after months of searching
stories.summary: Discoveries like this don't happen every day! A metal detector enthusiast in Essex came across a remarkable silver coin, dating to 1646, in a farmer's field. Dubbed a siege piece from the English Civil War that spanned 1642 to 1651, the coin bears the initials of King Charles I, suggesting a Royalist connection.

stories.title: Govt asks industry to curb urea diversion, cut costs as subsidy burden mounts
stories.summary: The government has called on the industry to cease the diversion of subsidised farm-grade urea for industrial purposes. Fertiliser secretary Rajat Kumar Mishra highlighted the disparity in pricing between agricultural and industrial-grade urea, urging adherence to misuse regulations. He expressed concern over fertiliser tagging practices by dealers that contribute to such diversion. The Fertiliser Association of India emphasized the need for increased domestic production and raw material diversification.

stories.title: AI Identifies Three Brain Patterns: Stanford study finds 3 child biotypes; patterns may inform targeted care
stories.summary: Stanford Medicine researchers identified three distinct brain patterns in children diagnosed with ADHD and anxiety. Their study suggests differences in brain connectivity can predict the development of these conditions. Researchers analyzed data from children aged 9 to 11 in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study. The findings may lead to more tailored treatment approaches for those experiencing attention and emotional difficulties.

stories.title: US court rules late husband's $319,000 retirement savings belong to estate, not surviving wife
India at disadvantage? US tariff uncertainty puts Indian exporters, buyers on edge
stories.summary: Indian exporters may face significant hurdles in the US market as new tariffs loom over their imports. Experts note that countries like Pakistan and Sri Lanka are not included in this investigation, likely giving them a competitive edge. A proposed 25 percent tariff could potentially decrease with future trade negotiations, leaving Indian businesses in a state of uncertainty regarding their trade dynamics with the US.

stories.title: Florida couple's $2.77 million custom home project never began; appeals court reverses $126,624 damages award
stories.summary: A couple in Florida faced a reversal of a damages award related to their failed construction project. They had originally paid $257,500 towards a custom home that was never built. The appeals court decided that their claims should be resolved through arbitration, as stipulated in their construction agreement. Allegations of fraudulent misrepresentation against the construction company's owners were thus addressed in this ruling.

stories.title: How two Chinese nationals and their sons cheated US Medicare and Medicaid of $55 million
stories.summary: Two Chinese nationals and their sons have been indicted in the US over an alleged $55 million Medicare and Medicaid fraud scheme. Prosecutors claim the Queens-based family billed government health programmes for unnecessary medicines, including pain patches, and paid beneficiaries cash and supermarket gift cards to fill prescriptions. The family allegedly used shell companies and fake pharmacy ownership records to conceal the money, which was spent on properties, investments, cryptocurrency and luxury vehicles.

stories.title: Louisiana father’s decision to give farm to brother upheld after children challenge inheritance
stories.summary: In Louisiana, a father's decision to transfer property to his brother, while retaining a lifetime residency right, sparked a legal battle after his death. His children contested the transfer, alleging it undermined their inheritance rights. However, the court found a lack of proof regarding inadequate living resources. The appeals court upheld the transfer, affirming the father's legal rights and the validity of his gift to his brother.

stories.title: 'Rahul must apologise': Nitin Nabin targets Congress over Ambedkar at Patna event
stories.summary: At the Samvidhan Gaurav Diwas event in Patna, BJP national president Nitin Nabin took aim at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of belittling Dr. BR Ambedkar's legacy and compromising constitutional values. He pointed out Congress's troubling past of dismissing elected state governments, while commending Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his commitment to constitutional ideals.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Vijay announces paternity leave, Akhilesh releases PDA manifesto and more
‘Spare 15 minutes to understand its spirit’: Amit Shah takes swipe at Rahul Gandhi on Constitution Day
stories.summary: Amit Shah highlighted the importance of instilling the values of the Constitution among India's youth during Constitution Day. He noted that the spirit of the Constitution was overlooked after Independence until November 26 was declared Constitution Day in 2015. Shah recounted the sacrifices made during the freedom struggle, which culminated in the Constitution.

stories.title: Family farm dispute: Canadian court rules son owns one-third after parents added him to title in 2008
stories.summary: In 2008, a Canadian couple designated their son's name on the family farm title, granting him a share in ownership. As family ties deteriorated, a dispute arose over farm ownership between the parents and the son. The Manitoba Court of Appeal upheld the son's one-third stake in the property, rejecting the parents' previous claims and ordering the sale of the farm as per the Law of Property Act.

stories.title: US Army calls Iowa blast of nearly 5 tonnes of toxic explosives a ‘huge success’ after health fears
Titanic sub disaster sparks $50 million lawsuit against OceanGate
Joshua Kutryk watches Katherine’s birth from ISS; her name honours his capsule
stories.summary: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk experienced a unique moment in his life when he witnessed the birth of his daughter, Katherine Grace, from the International Space Station. While his wife Heather welcomed their baby in Houston on November 24, 2026, Kutryk celebrated this milestone with mixed emotions, as he was unable to join them.

stories.title: 'Offering flowers to Babasaheb crime in UP?' CJP's Saurav Das stopped at UP border
Accredited vs self-proclaimed: SC to examine protection for journalists
stories.summary: The Supreme Court is set to review protection levels for accredited journalists compared to self-proclaimed reporters. It has referred the cases involving journalist assaults during protests in Delhi to a high-powered committee. The committee will investigate claims that journalists were unlawfully detained and faced excessive force from police. The Delhi Police has classified established journalists separately from social media content creators regarding protest protections.

stories.title: 'Single-digit parties': Punjab Congress president takes a dig at BJP-SAD alliance
stories.summary: Pargat Singh, the president of Punjab Congress, forecasts that the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal alliance will struggle, projecting they might secure only single-digit seats in the upcoming elections. He attributes this forecast to lingering public discontent from past events such as the farmers' protest. Singh also denounces the Aam Aadmi Party as the 'East India Company' and rules out any potential alliance with them.

stories.title: 'Prayed for death every night': Azam Khan gets emotional about his time in jail
stories.summary: Azam Khan expressed his emotional turmoil regarding his imprisonment during the launch of the SP manifesto. He recalled the fear experienced during jail transfers, emphasizing the pain endured by his family. Khan criticized the government for their treatment and compared it to times of British rule. He reaffirmed his support for Akhilesh Yadav ahead of the upcoming 2027 elections.

stories.title: 'Message to clean-shaven face & head': Owaisi's 'moustache' challenge to Yogi, Akhilesh over CM fight in UP
Court upholds order to move utility pole after years-long neighbour dispute
stories.summary: A Connecticut appeals court has upheld an order requiring neighbours to authorise the removal of a utility pole that has blocked two homeowners from widening their driveway, ending a legal dispute that began in 2019.

stories.title: Titus O'Neil's foundation brings Thanksgiving meals to 500 Tampa families
stories.summary: Titus O'Neil joined forces with Metropolitan Ministries to provide 500 Thanksgiving food boxes to families in Tampa, demonstrating a commitment to community support. The event, hosted at the Thaddeus M. Bullard Academy, saw the involvement of over 50 volunteers. Each box was packed with traditional meal essentials for four to six individuals.

stories.title: Professor loses $475K case to assistant; Nevada home faces court-ordered sale
‘Modi is sitting quietly today’: Kharge hints at BJP top brass rift, jibes at Yogi over PM ambitions
stories.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge expressed gratitude towards the people of Uttar Pradesh for reducing the BJP's electoral prospects. He highlighted that the BJP's promise of winning over 400 seats is now in jeopardy. Kharge criticized the rising inflation and unemployment while questioning the source of the BJP's considerable funding. Additionally, he accused the BJP of misusing investigative agencies to gather money.

stories.title: Rs 5 canteen, 50% PDA quota in govt contracts: Akhilesh unveils SP's UP manifesto
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has unveiled the Samajwadi Party's PDA manifesto on Constitution Day ahead of the upcoming UP Assembly elections. The manifesto emphasizes the party's focus on backward classes, Dalits, and minorities, aiming to connect with diverse societal groups. By releasing it early, the SP intends to communicate its commitments effectively before the campaign begins. The party plans to contest the 2027 elections in alliance with Congress against the BJP.

stories.title: Japan travel warning: UK embassy flags drink-spiking, credit card fraud targeting tourists in Tokyo
Alaska pilot drops frozen turkeys from her plane to remote families, reviving Thanksgiving tradition
stories.summary: Esther Keim has taken up a beloved tradition of delivering frozen turkeys to isolated families in Alaska, initially inspired by the generous actions of local pilot Kenny Hughes. In 2022, her inaugural delivery saw 36 turkeys spread over a vast 75 miles. With growing community support and volunteer involvement, Keim aims to significantly expand the initiative to benefit even more villages in the coming years.

stories.title: Britain net migration falls to 77,000, lowest level since 1997 outside pandemic
Congo Ebola outbreak crosses 12,000 cases as fighting disrupts response
stories.summary: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has now surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases since May. Armed conflicts in the area are significantly obstructing containment efforts and hampering the work of health teams. Tragically, nearly half of those infected have died, marking this as the most deadly outbreak ever recorded in the country.

stories.title: 'Elected to work, not gossip': Supriya Sule rejects NDA buzz, CM post speculation
stories.summary: Supriya Sule addressed rumors about her party's potential alliance with the BJP-led NDA. She emphasized her commitment to fulfilling her responsibilities to the people of Baramati and her work in Parliament. Sule also announced her father Sharad Pawar's hospitalization due to dehydration, attributing it to his busy schedule. She raised concerns about Pune's high crime rates and stressed the importance of accountability in the police.

stories.title: 4 dead, 17 missing after six-storey building collapses in Pakistan's Karachi
stories.summary: On Wednesday, a six-storey under-construction building in Karachi collapsed, killing at least four and injuring 14 individuals. Rescue efforts continued into Thursday to locate 17 more individuals believed to be trapped under the debris. The building was reportedly erected illegally on a site designated for residential use, prompting official concerns. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah ordered the removal of several officials for alleged negligence in construction oversight.

stories.title: 'Focus on action, not words': Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge breaks silence on Imran Masood's aggressive SP attack over UP seat-sharing
stories.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge has urged party member Imran Masood to prioritize proactive strategies rather than criticism amid seat-sharing disputes with the Samajwadi Party. Masood expressed his dissatisfaction over the SP's abrupt candidate declarations during their negotiations. With rising tensions, he has challenged the SP's approach towards Congress within this alliance, showcasing the fragile dynamics as they prepare for the upcoming 2027 elections.

stories.title: 'We were told he was under no investigation': JD Vance on Nvidia CEO Huang amid China spy claims
Australian fish hatchery that failed to raise barramundi for five years released 3,000 young fish
stories.summary: After five years of failing to produce barramundi, the Les Wilson Barramundi Discovery Centre has successfully bred 3,000 fingerlings. David Hammann, who lacks formal aquaculture training, led the turnaround by experimenting with breeding techniques. The fingerlings are crucial for restocking local waterways and ensuring a sustainable fish population. Local fishing groups anticipate improvement in lake populations as they await more fingerlings in the future.

stories.title: £1 charity shop ring turns out to be rare £2,000 Mughal gold treasure
stories.summary: While browsing a charity shop, a woman stumbled upon a ring priced at just £1, assuming it was merely costume jewellery. To her astonishment, when featured on the BBC's Antiques Roadshow, expert John Benjamin revealed its true worth. Dating back to the Georgian period, this 22-carat gold Mughal ring boasted a diamond and ruby stones, proving that hidden treasures often lie in the most unexpected places.

stories.title: Delhi high court rejects Lalu Yadav family's pleas, upholds charges in IRCTC hotel scam
stories.summary: The Delhi high court has affirmed the decision of the trial court to frame charges against Lalu Prasad Yadav and his family. The trial court ordered that they face charges related to corruption, conspiracy, and cheating in the IRCTC hotel scam. Lalu Prasad Yadav's family challenged this decision, arguing insufficient evidence against them. The CBI alleged that hotel leasing irregularities occurred during Lalu Prasad Yadav's tenure as Union railway minister.

stories.title: Vijay govt announces 15-day paternity leave for govt employees for first time
stories.summary: In a progressive move, Tamil Nadu has approved 15 days of paternity leave for male government employees, effective from a specified date. Fathers can use this leave either 15 days before their child arrives or within six months after birth. Acknowledging the crucial support fathers provide during this time, this decision encourages shared responsibilities in childcare and fosters gender equality in the family dynamic.

stories.title: SC asks Centre to submit census SOPs on caste data collection within a week
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Centre to establish a standard operating procedure for conducting the census. This directive comes in light of a plea that raises important questions about the collection of caste-related data. The petitioner seeks assurance on the methodology used and the privacy of individual details. Additionally, an affidavit outlining the verification process for caste information is required.

stories.title: Hexagons for nutrients: Supreme court asks FSSAI to tighten front packet labelling
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has instructed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to change nutrient labeling practices. It mandated the use of total sugars and saturated fat in front-of-package labels for packaged foods. The court has also directed specific warning labels for high fat, sugar, and salt on these products. Furthermore, the FSSAI must reformulate the threshold levels for these nutrients.

stories.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to 4 Southeast Asian countries amid chip scandal; China not on list: Report

Taylor Swift wore a long-discontinued aquarium T-shirt in 'The Life of a Showgirl' film promotion, inspiring fans to revive the 32-year-old design and raise more than $2 million for sea otter conservation
A 1910 New Jersey bridge had to open for ships; its $2.3bn replacement lets trains run uninterrupted
stories.summary: The much-anticipated Portal North Bridge is finally operational after years of diligent construction. This modern fixed-span bridge replaces the outdated swing bridge, which often disrupted crucial train services. Commuters can now enjoy smoother, more efficient travel along this busy railway corridor, with higher speed capabilities and improved overall reliability. The original swing bridge will be dismantled in 2027, signaling a transformative shift in railway operations.

stories.title: 'Are we your servants?' Congress MP Imran Masood continues tirade against ally SP over seat-sharing
Sharad Pawar hospitalised again, admitted to Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai
Supreme Court rules PMLA Adjudicating Authority cannot confirm ED property attachment without judicial member
‘Could be something good’: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule strikes softer tone on delimitation Bill
stories.summary: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule struck a softer tone on the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, saying her party would examine its provisions and support it if it served the country's interests. She said opposing every government proposal was not necessary. Sule also dismissed speculation about her party joining the NDA or her getting a ministerial berth as "gossip".

stories.title: 4 from Keralam among 11 Indians killed in UAE bus accident
Black nurses faced alleged racial abuse at Vermont home; Elderwood agrees to $450,000 settlement
stories.summary: The settlement of $450,000 addresses allegations of racial harassment faced by Black nurses during the COVID-19 pandemic. Employees reported incidents involving racial slurs and threats from residents at Elderwood at Burlington. The lawsuit was filed by the EEOC, claiming the operators failed to protect their employees from harassment. New measures will be introduced, including updated anti-discrimination policies and training programs for staff.

stories.title: Malaysia sues Google over ‘harmful’ content
44 Nvidia trades put Trump’s financial interests under spotlight after CEO’s return
Eisenkot bags 1st coalition pact in govt formation talks
‘Priceless legacy’: PM Modi pays tribute to Ambedkar, Constituent Assembly on Constitution Day
Trouble for Netanyahu? Israeli judges question key charges in corruption trial
Florida employer to pay $112,500 after accounting clerk's cancer-related dismissal claim
stories.summary: After undergoing cancer surgery, a Florida employee sought temporary accommodations, only to be let go by Schumacher Auto Group. The US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission has since accused the company of discrimination under the Americans with Disabilities Act. As part of a settlement, Schumacher will pay $112,500 in damages and revise their disability policies.

stories.title: New homes now cost $40K less than resale in the US
stories.summary: Current housing data shows a significant price gap between newly built homes and existing properties. Builders are implementing price cuts and incentives to attract buyers amid weaker demand. A median family finds new homes slightly more affordable than existing ones, despite high mortgage rates. Certain markets still experience severe housing cost burdens, requiring a significant portion of income for mortgage payments.

stories.title: A commitment to strengthen our Constitution
stories.summary: On Constitution Day, the Prime Minister underscores the pivotal role of the Constitution in shaping Indian democracy and society. He elaborates on various steps taken toward fostering social justice, economic parity, and inclusivity through government initiatives. The article reflects on key amendments enhancing constitutional rights and their benefits for marginalized groups, while also tackling historical governance issues.

stories.title: Chemistry most popular subject after English for 12th CBSE students
stories.summary: In 2027, the CBSE has achieved an impressive milestone with 19 lakh candidates registering for Class 12. An encouraging trend reveals a marked rise in science registrations, notably in chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Notably, the disparity between chemistry and business studies has skyrocketed since 2019. This surge aligns with a national educational shift, showcasing a clear preference for science over commerce fields.

stories.title: 7th high court posting? Justice Rao may be Karnataka Chief Justice
stories.summary: Justice M S Ramachandra Rao has been recommended for the position of Chief Justice of the Karnataka high court. This potential appointment would mark his seventh high court assignment since 2012 when he became a judge. He has previously served as Chief Justice in four high courts over a short period. Justice Rao has experienced multiple transfers throughout his judicial career due to various circumstances.

stories.title: Neighbour blocks couple's waterfront access, court upholds $64,061 legal fee award
stories.summary: A Minnesota couple sued their neighbour after he put up a sign claiming they had no harbour access and parked his boat along their waterfront, disrupting their attempts to sell two properties. An appeals court ruled that their property titles expressly granted water access, upheld findings of slander of title and nuisance, and confirmed a $64,061 attorney-fee award.

stories.title: Florida jury awards $6M to family of man who died during elective neck surgery
‘Fighting against BJP or us?’ Congress slams Samajwadi Party over its list
stories.summary: Congress MP Imran Masood expressed doubts about the intentions of Samajwadi Party during ongoing seat-sharing negotiations. The discussions, which lasted 3.5 hours, were complicated by SP's announcement of five candidates, causing tension. Masood emphasized that Congress seeks a significant number of seats for the 2027 elections while supporting Akhilesh Yadav for CM. SP leaders dismissed Masood's concerns as personal and affirmed no formal objections were raised.

stories.title: Lamp not lit atop deepathoon, Supreme Court to hear contempt case
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has not complied with the Supreme Court's order regarding the Karthigai Deepam lamp lighting. This non-compliance may trigger contempt proceedings against the Madurai Collector, despite his apology. Various political parties and the Madurai district administration oppose the lighting of the lamp atop the deepathoon. The Collector reported efforts to follow the Supreme Court's directive, which were ultimately unsuccessful.

stories.title: India tops in videos removed from YouTube
stories.summary: YouTube took down approximately 34.4 lakh videos from India in the second quarter of 2026. This number represented a 28% increase from the previous quarter's removals. Globally, child safety issues were responsible for the majority of video removals. Additionally, Indian courts and government agencies sent numerous removal requests to Google. Police primarily initiated these requests, reflecting a growing trend in content regulation.

stories.title: Trump slaps new tariffs on 14 nations; India faces additional 17%
stories.summary: Rejecting claims of surplus capacity in any sector, the Indian government emphasises its commitment to forging a strong bilateral trade agreement with the US. Recent tariff negotiations hit a snag following a US Supreme Court ruling, temporarily halting progress. However, prior to this, an accord on extra tariffs was already negotiated. Optimism remains high among Indian officials that the deal can be finalised, contingent on the US's tariff policy developments.

stories.title: ‘Our artists bringing new perspectives to art world’: PM Modi after Venice Biennale award
stories.summary: The India Pavilion received the Visitors’ Lion Award for Best National Participation at the Venice Art Biennale. Curated by Amin Jaffer, it featured five contemporary artists exploring themes of memory and migration. Prime Minister Narendra Modi acknowledged this achievement as a significant moment for India’s cultural landscape. The pavilion returned to Biennale Arte after a seven-year gap, showcasing diverse Indian perspectives and heritage.

stories.title: Meta officials meet Congress over suspended accounts
stories.summary: In New Delhi, Meta representatives held discussions with Congress social media officials amid growing complaints about account suspensions and content deletions affecting the opposition. Supriya Shrinate raised critical concerns about what she deemed interference by Meta in political issues. In response, the officials clarified that they strictly comply with Indian content laws and maintain their stance of political impartiality throughout these processes.

stories.title: Colorado court upholds injunction over ranch road used by a family since 1958
stories.summary: A Colorado ranching family used a road for livestock since 1958 but lost access rights in court. The new owners, Camilletti Ranch Properties LLC, challenged their claim to a prescriptive easement. The court ruled that the family's use was permitted by previous owners during part of the statutory period. The Colorado Court of Appeals affirmed this decision on November 12, 2026.

stories.title: Delhi to Dhaka: Probe minority attacks, Hasina passport a separate issue
stories.summary: In response to escalating violence against minorities in Bangladesh, India has expressed its serious concerns, urging the government there to conduct an extensive investigation. The Ministry of External Affairs noted the unique circumstances surrounding Sheikh Hasina's passport and extradition request, highlighting that these matters are being processed according to established protocols. Furthermore, two Indian nationals suffered injuries in a recent Houthi assault in Riyadh, prompting a strong condemnation from India.

stories.title: Bail to be granted under UAPA when there is delay in trial, says Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has confirmed that its authority to grant bail cannot be overridden by stringent laws. It ruled in favor of a government doctor who has been jailed for over four years. Additionally, the Court granted bail to senior officials involved in a significant corruption case in Rajasthan. These decisions highlight ongoing tensions in bail jurisprudence amid contradictory orders from different benches.

stories.title: Exporters in better position but brace for uncertainty
stories.summary: Indian exporters are adapting to potential tariffs from the United States while they finalize a trade agreement. The impact of these tariffs may create temporary uncertainty for exporters as they manage future orders. Current strategies involve rushing shipments to avoid increased costs before the new tariffs kick in. Exporters believe that negotiating a reduced tariff rate will provide a competitive advantage in the market.

stories.title: Man buys back his 1972 Lotus Europa 35 years after selling it during divorce
Election Commission: Rectify wrong roll entries during SSR via Form
stories.summary: Form 8 is being used for rectifying inaccuracies in the electoral roll during the special summary revision. Booth-level officers will verify mismatched entries to ensure accurate voter information collection. Electors can flag incorrect details, and booth-level officers must confirm these. Changes to demographic particulars must be authorized and verified by the competent authority after proper application. The electoral registration officer will manage the processing of applications according to the regulations.

stories.title: Cabinet ministers advised to avoid foreign travel; Parliament session likely by December 15
stories.summary: Cabinet ministers have been advised to avoid international travel as Parliament may be convened before mid-December. The government aims to introduce a Constitution amendment bill for women's reservation during the next session. This proposal, linked with delimitation, could expand Lok Sabha's strength significantly. Opposition parties have raised concerns regarding its implications, particularly for state representation.

stories.title: Texas appeals court upholds fence removal order and $10,000 statutory damages award
stories.summary: In a Texas property saga, two neighbors, Lebedzinski and Russell, found themselves in a legal feud over a four-acre piece of land, obstructed by a fence. The verdict mandated the fence's removal and rewarded $10,000 in damages. An appeals court upheld this decision but revised aspects related to the deed and attorney's fees, ultimately dismissing Russell's claims of adverse possession and notification.

stories.title: After 30 years in jail, former Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassin seeks parity with Rajiv Gandhi's killer in SC
stories.summary: Balwant Singh Rajoana, who has been incarcerated for over three decades, is seeking mercy to have his death sentence reduced. His appeal references the recent release of AG Perarivalan, a former death row inmate turned lawyer. Senior counsel Mukul Rohatgi stresses Rajoana's transformation during imprisonment, while the Centre, represented by ASG KM Nataraj, counters that Rajoana's historical anti-constitutional statements warrant denial.

stories.title: Missing businessman's non-bailable warrant cancelled in AJL case, ED to move high court
stories.summary: A special MP/MLA court in Rouse Avenue cancelled a non-bailable warrant against businessman Dinesh Pandey. The Enforcement Directorate is surprised and plans to appeal this decision in the Delhi high court. Pandey is reportedly involved in transferring Rs 10.4 crore through a shell company to Associated Journals Ltd. The court criticized the investigating officer for using a sealed cover, which is typically standard practice.

stories.title: Ancient DNA traces infectious diseases across 37,000 years of Eurasian history
Elise Stefanik family’s DC home sells for $2.9m cash after failing to fetch $1.99m, flagged as unusual
stories.summary: In a notable real estate transaction, a Washington home belonging to US Congresswoman Elise Stefanik's family was sold for a substantial $2.9 million in June. This sale came after an earlier unsuccessful attempt to sell at $1.99 million. City tax officials raised eyebrows regarding the deal's unusual price point. The buyer, AFS Real Estate Holdings, remains shrouded in mystery regarding its ownership.

stories.title: Sewer Fees Vary By Property: Charlotte County rolled rates back; homeowners should check current charges
stories.summary: Homeowners in Charlotte County are experiencing increases in sewer connection charges while the local government upgrades wastewater infrastructure. The rising costs are linked to efforts to meet stricter environmental regulations aimed at protecting Charlotte Harbor. Environmental studies indicate a significant decline in seagrass coverage due to nutrient pollution, adversely affecting marine life. The county's planned improvements to sewage facilities are expected to require funding through various sources.

stories.title: London court upholds 2017 will, securing £1m inheritance for two relatives
Lululemon founder Chip Wilson says Canadian women aren't having as many babies as men want; some men may need to import brides from Thailand
Justin Bieber collaborator Poo Bear lists Miami penthouse for $10 million
Bournemouth residents oppose two new padel courts, citing noise and swearing from existing courts
stories.summary: Residents near West Hants Club are voicing opposition to proposed new padel courts due to existing noise issues. They report constant disturbances from shouts and sounds that disrupt their daily lives and enjoyment of outdoor spaces. Complaints have been made to BCP Council regarding noise levels and offensive language from players. The club claims it operates responsibly, with measures to manage noise and ensure member behavior.

stories.title: Michigan court upholds doctor's divorce default, overturns unsupported support orders
Egypt highway inferno kills 30 after fuel tanker overturns
stories.summary: A harrowing event unfolded in Giza's Al-Warraq district when a vehicle turned over and burst into flames. Tragically, over 30 individuals perished, while another 21 suffered injuries. Emergency services quickly arrived at the scene to extinguish the blaze and offer medical assistance. The incident took place on a major ring road in Greater Cairo, raising renewed concerns about the pressing issues of road safety in Egypt.

stories.title: Wisconsin railway tunnel reopens after seven years, recalling a remarkable 1887 construction feat
stories.summary: The Stewart Tunnel in Wisconsin has officially reopened for cyclists after an extensive restoration initiative. It was closed in 2019 due to safety hazards associated with falling rocks, prompting significant renovation work. Originally constructed in 1886 for the Illinois Central Railroad, the tunnel historically facilitated passenger and freight transport until the 1970s. The restoration included adding a metal liner and drainage to enhance safety while maintaining its historic character.

stories.title: Chinese scientist, Arizona State University assistant professor, says he does not know why he was arrested by ICE: 'I still have nightmares'
Michigan widow's $78m truck crash award cut by $24m as court orders retrial on $19m claim
stories.summary: A Michigan appeals court overturned a $24 million award for pre-impact fright in a wrongful death case. The court ruled that state law does not allow compensation for fear experienced before injury. A new trial has been ordered for the $19 million awarded for conscious pain and suffering. The trial originally awarded over $78 million for the negligence of an 18-wheel lorry driver.

stories.title: Vande Mataram at J&K waqf event sparks row
stories.summary: Several Muslim clerics who attended a Waqf Board event in Srinagar expressed their regret after Vande Mataram was played. They said their participation did not endorse the song, and they prayed for forgiveness. The song sparked controversy as it allegedly conflicts with Islamic principles of Tawheed, promoting the oneness of Allah. The Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama criticised the Waqf Board for playing Vande Mataram at a Muslim institution.

stories.title: Omar government breaks silence on Sheshnag row, says lake safe
stories.summary: The J&K government asserted that Sheshnag Lake remains completely safe following allegations of construction by the Border Roads Organisation. Forest minister Altaf Kaloo reported that heavy machinery operated away from the lake, ensuring no soil entered the water body. A 12-member inspection team found no tampering with the lake's track as maintenance is performed before the Amarnath Yatra.

stories.title: Terrorists’ properties attached in J&K’s Reasi, Handwara
stories.summary: Police & security agencies conduct anti-terror drills in Kulgam

stories.title: Alberta family donates 160 acres of native prairie for conservation while allowing cattle grazing
stories.summary: A remarkable commitment to conservation has been made by a ranching family in southern Alberta, who have donated 160 acres of untouched prairie land for long-term protection. This initiative allows cattle grazing to persist while maintaining the delicate balance of the native grassland ecosystem. For nearly a century, the Coppieters family has managed this land, protecting its agricultural history.

stories.title: PM Modi wants ITI courses aligned with industry needs, jobs closer to home
stories.summary: PM Narendra Modi emphasized the need for public sector undertakings to establish connections with Industrial Training Institutes. He highlighted the importance of a 'Classroom–Company–Career' approach to enhance employment opportunities for youth. Modi suggested that PSUs should evaluate future manpower needs and strengthen partnership with ITIs to recruit trained candidates. He also encouraged decentralised solar and wind power projects closer to consumption centers.

stories.title: Idaho Supreme Court dismisses challenge to 100-slip Spokane River marina plan
stories.summary: In a significant legal ruling, the Idaho Supreme Court dismissed a community's challenge to a marina expansion project, finding that four residents had not properly engaged in the necessary administrative procedures. Their public remarks alone were deemed insufficient for legal standing to contest the permit granted by the Department of Lands. This decision underscores the importance of following procedural guidelines to effectively challenge state agency rulings in Idaho.

stories.title: Man nailed himself inside a box to escape slavery in 1849
stories.summary: Henry Box Brown escaped slavery in 1849 by having himself packed inside a wooden box and transported from Richmond, Virginia, to Philadelphia. The 26-27-hour journey involved several changes of transport, and the box was turned upside down twice, nearly costing him his life. After reaching freedom, Brown became an abolitionist speaker and performer, sharing his escape story across the US and England. He later returned to the US and died in Toronto in 1897.

stories.title: Maryland students sue after AI camera mistakes Doritos for a gun
Cheeni Kum: Poor monsoon hits sugar crop, gross output may not meet domestic need
stories.summary: India's sugar production for the 2026-27 season is expected to decrease by 15%, primarily due to weather issues. Maharashtra and Karnataka will contribute significantly to the decline following inadequate rainfall. The expected net sugar production will be around 265 lakh tonne, down from nearly 280 lakh tonne last season. Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association noted various climatic factors affecting sugar crops across key states.

stories.title: Ex-Jagan confidant looks to target Hindu right space with new party in Andhra
Government’s big manufacturing push: Rs 11,000 crore for infrastructure equipment, six new urea plants
stories.summary: The Indian government approved a new scheme to promote domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment. This scheme will incentivize the production of advanced machinery over eight years, reducing import dependence. Additionally, six new brownfield urea plants have been cleared to boost domestic agricultural production. These plants aim to enhance urea production to meet national demand and cut imports.

stories.title: Massachusetts man won $1 million lottery prize, posed for a photo with oversized check; ICE tracked him down, claimed he had a deportation order since 2014
Who was Michael Joseph Moore? DNA identifies former firefighter in 1968 murder of 16-year-old girl
stories.summary: Police in Ontario have identified Michael Joseph Moore as the suspect in the 1968 murder of Jacqueline Dunleavy. Dunleavy, a 16-year-old girl, was found dead shortly after finishing her shift at a convenience store. Investigators used modern DNA testing techniques to link preserved evidence to Moore, who died in 2018. Despite this breakthrough, no criminal charges can be filed against him posthumously.

stories.title: Kyle Rudolph’s $15M Minnesota mansion heads to auction
stories.summary: A lavish mansion in Minnesota, previously owned by NFL star Kyle Rudolph, is set to be auctioned off after failing to attract buyers. Originally priced at $14.95 million, the estate is now being offered for co-ownership, with six shares available starting at $1.55 million each. Interested parties can tour the residence before the auction date of December 10, presenting a unique chance to invest in luxury real estate.

stories.title: A Minnesota dam built in 1910 to generate electricity survived decades of floods
stories.summary: The Rapidan Dam, an engineering marvel established more than a century ago for hydroelectric generation, is facing substantial damage from frequent flooding. The devastating floods of 2024 have rendered the structure unsafe, prompting Blue Earth County to secure significant FEMA funding for remediation. Efforts are now focused on removing the dam and restoring the badly impacted riverbanks, with demolition anticipated to start in 2027, subject to obtaining necessary permits.

stories.title: AAIB for minimum flying requirement for flying school trainers following spate of accidents
Delhi SIR: Nearly 44 lakh voters may remain off final electoral roll after low Form 6 turnout
stories.summary: Nearly 44 lakh voters are at risk of remaining excluded from Delhi's final electoral roll. Only about 3.5 lakh Form 6 applications have been submitted by the deadline. Efforts to trace voters categorized as absent, shifted, deceased, or duplicate have seen limited success due to various challenges. The distribution of enumeration forms is ongoing and will conclude at the end of November.

stories.title: Congress meets Meta amid Youth Congress protest, demads fair treatment
PRAGATI meeting: PM Modi reviews infrastructure projects worth over Rs 78,000 crore, stresses timely execution
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi led a review meeting on key infrastructure projects worth over Rs 78,000 crore. The discussion included strategies to enhance road, railway, power, and coal sectors while addressing delays and implementation issues. A significant focus was placed on improving the Industrial Training Institute ecosystem through the PM-SETU initiative. Partnerships between industries and ITIs were encouraged to align training with job market demands.

stories.title: PM Modi asks ministers to stay put & stay ready; next Parliament session likely before December 15: Report
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has directed ministers to avoid foreign travel and prepare for the upcoming Parliament session. The Cabinet meeting highlighted delays in convening the Winter Session, which has raised questions from opposition parties. The government's focus is on possibly introducing the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill linked to delimitation and women's reservation in Parliament. Changes in political alliances have altered required support dynamics for passing legislation.

stories.title: MSME sector: Govt sets 50% registration target for women entrepreneurs
stories.summary: In a significant move, Union MSME minister Jitan Ram Manjhi shared plans to boost women's registration in Udyam to an ambitious 50%. He highlighted that embracing inclusivity within the MSME sector is crucial for driving economic advancement. Furthermore, the government is dedicated to creating enhanced opportunities for entrepreneurs from marginalized backgrounds, prioritizing access to funding, technology integration, and fortifying global competitiveness across various identified growth sectors.

stories.title: Ex-Jagan confidant looks to target Hindu right space with new party in Andhra
India & Nepal start Suryakiran exercise in Saljhandi to boost military coordination
Aero India 2027 expands exhibition space as demand exceeds capacity
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence is set to enhance the exhibition infrastructure for Aero India 2027 due to growing interest in the event. Scheduled for February 2027 at Air Force Station Yelahanka, the exhibition will feature two new hangars and optional mezzanine floors for exhibitors. These developments will allow a wider array of international aerospace firms and domestic producers to display their innovations effectively.

stories.title: Punjab polls: SAD-BJP reunion pushes Congress towards Left parties for alliance talks
Amid SIR complaints, EC directs states to correct voter list errors
stories.summary: The Election Commission has mandated that officials focus on rectifying inaccuracies in the electoral rolls during the revision phase. Voter information currently on file will be cross-referenced with new data gathered from a Special Intensive Revision process. Booth level officers will validate voter information and process Form 8 applications when needed. Necessary updates to personal information must follow the approved Form 8 after verification.

stories.title: 'No significant impact on India': MeitY secretary on US chip export curbs
stories.summary: S. Krishnan, secretary of MeitY, reassured that the recent US chip export restrictions won't impact India. He stated that India is appreciated as a reliable partner in data centre technology. In addition, over 200 companies have expressed interest in the India Semiconductor Mission 2.0. Krishnan also mentioned the exciting advancements of Chariot One, an innovative text-to-speech AI model developed by Indian graduates, showcasing India's technological prowess.

stories.title: VHP targets TVK govt over Deepam row, seeks SC action
India wins Visitors' Lion for best national pavilion at Venice Art Biennale
stories.summary: India's national pavilion received the Visitors' Lion for Best National Participation at the Venice Art Biennale. The award was announced by Union minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and highlighted India's cultural influence. This national pavilion was titled 'Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home' and featured works from five Indian artists. India returned to the Venice Art Biennale after a seven-year absence, showcasing its contemporary art scene.

stories.title: A British clock house whose time runs 5 minutes ahead of Greenwich time has been restored
stories.summary: The Clock House in Ramsgate has been beautifully restored at a cost of £7.5 million, maintaining its historical essence as a vital community hub. This transformation includes a modern café and exhibition area dedicated to the town's rich maritime heritage. A public celebration is set to mark the renovation's completion, encouraging community interaction and boosting local tourism.

stories.title: A non-venomous snake that does not constrict its prey can still kill with its bite
stories.summary: Recent studies on Drymarchon snakes reveal their impressive biting ability, which they utilize to capture prey with remarkable efficiency. Unlike typical assumptions about non-venomous species, these snakes can exert bite pressures surpassing those of their constrictor counterparts. The research highlights how their jaw anatomy facilitates this concentrated force, emphasizing that their success also hinges on maintaining grip post-bite.

stories.title: Mortgage-Free Home: Army Veteran’s Family Gets New Home; construction begins Nov 20
stories.summary: At a live concert, army veteran Michael King received a heartwarming surprise—a mortgage-free, custom-built home for him and his family. This remarkable announcement, brought forth by Belman Homes and Operation Finally Home, occurred during a Craig Morgan performance. King's military service has resulted in health challenges, and this initiative seeks to ensure lasting stability for veterans.

stories.title: Spain's Canary Islands see record daily influx of migrants as nearly 2,000 reach archipelago
'Whether Yogi ji or someone else': Keshav Prasad Maurya says BJP's CM face will be decided after UP assembly polls
Iowa residents told to take shelter as US Army prepares to detonate 5 tonnes of explosives
Iranian delegation meets MEA officials to discuss multilateral ties
stories.summary: During a significant meeting, Alireza Tootonchian led an Iranian delegation in discussions with officials from India's Ministry of External Affairs. They focused on strengthening multilateral ties within the Indian Ocean Rim Association as they gear up for the important 25th IORA Council of Ministers meeting slated for November 27 in New Delhi.

stories.title: 3 dead, 23 trapped after flood hits illegal gold mine in Indonesia
IShowSpeed beats Kai Cenat in GTA 6 $1 million challenge after making dramatic comeback
stories.summary: IShowSpeed made an astonishing comeback against Kai Cenat in their thrilling GTA 6 challenge. Despite trailing by $500,000 and nearly quitting due to technical glitches with his PS5, Speed seized the opportunity when Kai perished in the game, losing all his progress. In a nail-biting finish, Speed hit the $1 million mark just in time, reveling in his triumph alongside his audience.

stories.title: Bisleri row: FSSAI launches pan-India water quality checks; results within 1-2 months
Trump’s Russia business pitch loses steam as Putin presses for Donbas: Report
North Carolina couple honours late daughter by rescuing hundreds of animals

‘Time for Ram Naam Satya approaching’: CM Yogi Adityanath attacks Akhilesh Yadav ahead of proposed Ayodhya visit
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath criticized the Samajwadi Party's family-centric politics during a recent interview. He accused the party of disrespecting Lord Ram's devotees and failing to apologize for past violence. Adityanath emphasized the need for the SP to respect local religious traditions in their greetings. He highlighted the economic growth and investment in Uttar Pradesh since 2017, contrasting it with previous governance.

stories.title: Illinois court upholds nuisance ruling but voids extra fines
stories.summary: The Illinois appeals court has overturned more than $53,000 in daily fines against property owner Tim Quackenbush, while still affirming a $750 fine. The court recognized the properties as a public nuisance, though Quackenbush claimed the materials were part of his business assets, despite the city's assertion of a dumping ground. The decisions highlighted the necessity for property maintenance and the chance for cleanup efforts.

Had Sharad Pawar joined NDA in 2019, PM Modi may have considered him for President: Union minister Athawale
He raised £86,000 for cancer patients; now he is battling the disease himself
stories.summary: Paul and Jane Bottomley from Sowerby Bridge have raised £86,000 for Calderdale Royal Hospital's Macmillan cancer centre through Christmas hamper raffles, an initiative they started after Jane was diagnosed with ovarian cancer in 2012. Now, 59-year-old Paul has himself been diagnosed with prostate cancer and is due to undergo surgery in December.

stories.title: Nvidia chip scandal: How Alice Huang's $270m network is linked to China's military
California son wins fight over late father's partner's 1978 house
Rahul Gandhi assets case: SC quashes Allahabad HC orders seeking CBI, ED inquiry
Pak astronaut Ali reaches China’s Tiangong station
stories.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first Pakistani astronaut, has reached the Tiangong space station in China. He launched aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft alongside two Chinese astronauts, Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi. The mission is significant as it marks Pakistan's entry into human spaceflight and international collaboration in space exploration. Ali will engage in several science experiments and is expected to stay for a short duration.

stories.title: Kannur murder: 3 BJP-RSS workers get life term for killing CPM leader in 2016
Russian overnight strikes kill two in Odesa, set Kyiv apartment block ablaze
stories.summary: In an overnight assault, Russian forces targeted various regions in Ukraine, including Odesa and Kyiv. The attacks resulted in two fatalities and several injuries, with both civilians and children affected. Additionally, a drone strike in Kyiv sparked a significant fire in a high-rise building, causing two more injuries. Concurrently, a drone incident in Russia's Samara region led to serious consequences, including a death and power outages.
