SC cancels Cong MLA Vinay Kulkarni's bail in Yogesh Godar murder case, directs to surrender in two weeks
SC refuses interim bail to Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam, asks Delhi Police to respond
26 seats vs 120 demand: Why Saharanpur, Gandhi family turfs are testing Congress-SP ties
stories.summary: Congress has sought 120 seats in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections and is unwilling to accept fewer, news agency ANI reported, citing party sources. Its wish list includes constituencies in Amethi and Raebareli, traditional Gandhi family strongholds, as well as two seats in Saharanpur where the SP has announced candidates. The demand has complicated seat-sharing talks between the INDIA bloc allies.

stories.title: 'Reel blocked, visa cancelled': Dhruv Rathee hits out at Centre after Saurav Das denied flight to London
‘Lamp could not be lit at designated spot’: Tamil Nadu govt apologises in Supreme Court, contempt plea to be heard in Karthigai Deepam row
Congress to hold nationwide ‘Samvidhan Raksha’ marches on Thursday; Kharge to lead from Lucknow
stories.summary: Congress is set to hold 'Samvidhan Raksha' Marches on Thursday to honor Constitution Day. Party President Mallikarjun Kharge will join the event in Lucknow. Each Pradesh Congress Committee will begin the marches at notable statues of BR Ambedkar or Mahatma Gandhi. Additionally, party workers will verify voter lists and assist with electoral rights reclamation. Concerns have been raised about alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and the electoral process.

stories.title: ‘Are we beggars?’ Congress fumes as Akhilesh offers 26 seats for UP polls
stories.summary: Tensions have surfaced between the Samajwadi Party and Congress ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, with Congress MP Imran Masood asking, "Are we beggars?" over SP's offer of 26 seats. While Congress is seeking 120 seats, Akhilesh Yadav has stressed winnability and called for further discussions to defeat the BJP.

stories.title: ‘Crores of devotees let down’: BJP slams Vijay govt for defying SC order on Deepam row
‘Not a single bogus vote to be added’: Akhilesh tells SP workers to monitor election commission activities
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has called on Samajwadi Party workers to monitor electoral roll activities ahead of the upcoming elections. He emphasized that no bogus votes should be added and no genuine votes should be removed from the lists. Yadav expressed concerns regarding the credibility of Electronic Voting Machines, reflecting public scepticism and recent controversies. He also urged Congress to identify additional winnable constituencies for the seat-sharing negotiations.

stories.title: 'Passport has discrepancies in place of birth': Saurav Das rendered ineligible for foreign travel
stories.summary: CJP activist Saurav Das has been served a notice by the Regional Passport Office regarding his birth documents. The notice requires him to respond within seven days to clarify discrepancies in his documents. If he fails to provide a satisfactory explanation, his passport may be impounded under the Passports Act. A pending re-verification will determine his eligibility for international travel once cleared.

stories.title: Two arrested after masked men break into Prince William and Kate’s country home
Israel govt formation: Eisenkot, Lieberman join hands in bid to oust Netanyahu
stories.summary: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party has formed a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing Israel Our Home party. This alliance is pivotal as efforts to create a government without Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu intensify. The Knesset was sworn in without a new government after the recent election reduced Netanyahu's majority. Eisenkot aims to establish a government by December 6, with an extension option available.

stories.title: Flights delayed at Chicago O’Hare airport as ground radar system suffers outage
Giving Machines has raised $70 million; whose donations of livestock & business training helped families
stories.summary: The Giving Machines initiative has emerged as a worldwide project facilitating the donation of essential goods to those in need. These innovative vending machines dispense critical items like chickens, goats, and educational resources for financially struggling families. Partner organizations ensure that these donations reach their intended recipients efficiently, while also promoting women's health and girls' education across diverse areas.

stories.title: New Jersey mother, son sue zoning board over rejected bayfront home plan
stories.summary: A New Jersey mother and her son have approached the court after a township zoning board rejected their plan to build a three-storey house on their bayfront plot. They argue that the board failed to properly consider expert evidence and the property's existing limitations. The family wants the rejection overturned and has also sought compensation, claiming that the decision effectively deprives them of the use of their land.

stories.title: 1st privately built PSLV set for launch early next year: Isro chief
stories.summary: Isro Chairman V Narayanan announced the first privately built Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle is ready for launch. This PSLV-N1 rocket is being developed by a consortium including L&T and HAL. The government is promoting satellite launches in collaboration with startups, which have increased to over 440. Narayanan emphasized the importance of building more space assets for communication and navigation.

stories.title: Rajiv Gandhi's security withdrawn to get him killed, says Rahul
stories.summary: In a recent family conversation about Sonia Gandhi's latest book, Rahul Gandhi accused the government of intentionally removing his father Rajiv Gandhi's security, suggesting it fostered the conditions for his assassination. Following his exit from office in 1989, Rajiv's protection was significantly reduced. Furthermore, Rahul is poised to address the political victimization and humiliation Sonia endured during her career.

stories.title: 6 years after split, Akalis & BJP tie up for Punjab assembly polls
stories.summary: 'Big brother' SAD to get CM post if NDA wins: Shah

stories.title: Amit Shah: Kartarpur corridor to open after review
stories.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah expressed that the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor will only reopen after addressing prevailing security issues. This corridor, which offers hassle-free access for pilgrims, was shut down following security alerts linked to Operation Sindoor. Shah highlighted the need to keep national security discussions free from political influences, while also pointing out that the corridor's placement in Pakistan stemmed from Congress party oversights during partition.

stories.title: ICMR: Over 50 per cent of women of reproductive age anaemic
stories.summary: 'Two-thirds of adolescents deficient in Vitamin B12'

stories.title: NSA Ajit Doval, Maldives defence minister discuss security ties at Colombo meet
stories.summary: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Maldives defense minister Hassan Rasheed discussed security cooperation at the Colombo Security Conclave. This meeting marked the first high-level interaction between the two countries since President Mohamed Muizzu's recent visit to Pakistan. During that visit, Maldives signed 20 agreements with Pakistan related to defense and maritime issues. Additionally, Muizzu called for resuming the Saarc summit process to enhance regional cooperation.

stories.title: Utah banker mailed 37 tons of bricks to build a bank, forcing postal rule changes
stories.summary: In 1916, the directors of the Bank of Vernal needed bricks for a new building project. They faced high transportation costs due to poor road conditions in rural Utah. A director discovered that shipping bricks by postal service was a cheaper option, allowing many small packages to be sent. This unique approach led to changes in postal regulations regarding large shipments.

stories.title: PM Modi, Merz say India-EU FTA will unlock new opportunities
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently engaged in discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, focused on enhancing the India-Germany Strategic Partnership. The conversation covered various critical areas including trade, investment, defence, and cutting-edge technologies, underscoring both nations’ dedication to global peace. As they commemorate 75 years of diplomatic ties, they aim to bolster cooperation across essential sectors while sharing insights on regional issues of common interest.

stories.title: From ghat to gallery, Banaras set for brush with art
stories.summary: The CII Banaras Biennale is set to commence on November 27, culminating on December 31. This unique event aims to intertwine the ancient and modern art scenes, presenting the vibrant culture of Banaras. Activities will unfold at numerous venues, including the distinguished Bharatiya Kala Bhavan. By fostering partnerships between cultural institutions and industry, the Biennale aspires to spark rich dialogues, bridging diverse artistic expressions with their historical narratives.

stories.title: Government may link motor insurance premiums to traffic violations
stories.summary: The road transport ministry is gearing up to introduce initiatives to lower the incidence of uninsured vehicles on Indian roads. Key proposals include establishing a unified insurance premium for different vehicle types. Furthermore, traffic violations recorded against vehicle owners could potentially affect their insurance costs. A trial of the 'no insurance, no fuel' strategy will be initiated at select fuel stations.

stories.title: Dalai Lama, office allotted bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi
stories.summary: The Centre has assigned a government bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama. This official accommodation aims to facilitate his visits to the national capital and provide comfort. Members of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile have welcomed this arrangement as a supportive gesture towards their community. Gaden Phodrang, the Dalai Lama's office, was registered as a private trust in India in 2011.

stories.title: Wedding seating row sparks £400,000 inheritance battle between two brothers

A North Carolina family donated the development rights over their 55-acre farm straddling two counties, protecting pasture and forest in a fast-growing region where most of the soil is considered prime farmland.
stories.summary: In North Carolina, Jennifer and Lane Tredway donated development rights to protect their 55-acre farm. This conservation easement will ensure the land remains agricultural and untouched by future development. The farm, known as Two Paths Farm, is situated in an area experiencing rapid urban expansion. Both Johnston and Wake counties are involved in preserving the agricultural character of the region.

stories.title: Woman's claim to abandoned Philadelphia house she lived in since 2003 rejected
stories.summary: A Philadelphia woman who claimed she had occupied an abandoned house since 2003 has lost her appeal seeking ownership through adverse possession. The Pennsylvania Superior Court dismissed her case on November 20, citing inadequate legal arguments and missing references in her appeal.

stories.title: West Virginia town sues to save 12 historic buildings from demolition in national park
stories.summary: Thurmond, a historic railroad town in West Virginia, is in a legal battle against the National Park Service. The lawsuit aims to halt the planned demolition of 12 historic buildings scheduled for November 30. Officials argue the agency violated federal laws and failed to consider preservation options. Concerns have also been raised regarding road safety and equipment weight limits. The court's decision will determine the future of these historic structures.

stories.title: Meet Yash Patil, Indian-origin entrepreneur who took leave from Stanford to work with Open AI, founded his own startup and then sold it for $4.5 billion
High-profile Colorado attorney who set own house on fire and apologized to wife and children for domestic violence dies of accidental drug overdose
Sydney medical student identifies 5 relatives in forgotten 1965 film after social media appeal
stories.summary: A 1965 film uncovered in Melbourne became a bridge connecting a Sydney medical student to previously unknown relatives. This discovery showcased three generations of his family outside their residence in Mitcham. After British director Karen Walsh endeavored to uncover the family's identity, the medical student recognized his great-grandmother among the footage shared online. With the help of ABC Melbourne, the quest for family links successfully culminated.

stories.title: BSF constable dies by suicide in Arnia
stories.summary: In a tragic incident, Deva Nand Majhi, a young BSF constable stationed in Jammu and Kashmir, reportedly took his own life at a security camp. The shocking event unfolded in the Arnia border region late Monday night when he allegedly utilized his service weapon. Originally from Katsa in Bihar's Saran district, his remains have been sent to GMC Jammu's mortuary for autopsy.

stories.title: Sofia Hernandez Mejia's arrest by ICE from Seattle airport: Husband says he feels useless as a US citizen
Cops stop Mehbooba‘s Sheshnag trek amid BRO construction row
stories.summary: Concerns are mounting among political leaders, notably PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, regarding the construction activities near Sheshnag Lake. Environmental advocates and Congress members underscore the area's ecological sensitivity. The Border Roads Organisation defends its initiatives as critical for ensuring safety for pilgrims on the Amarnath Yatra route. Detractors warn that development could endanger local ecosystems, revealing a broader conflict between aspirations for growth and the need for environmental conservation.

stories.title: WestJet ordered to pay Canadian couple $2,000 after 16-hour delay blamed on wind
stories.summary: After a grueling 16-hour delay, a Canadian couple finally made it to Vancouver, only to find themselves stuck overnight in Regina due to a missed connection. WestJet cited strong winds as the reason for the delay but could not substantiate their claim. Ultimately, the Civil Resolution Tribunal held the airline liable and awarded the couple $2,226.92 for their inconvenience, which included their legal expenses.

stories.title: Colorado man freed after 27 years for infant's murder seeks $2m, but family calls claim a joke
stories.summary: Stephen Martinez has filed a $1.9 million claim for state compensation following his wrongful imprisonment of 27 years, a conviction now overturned. However, the family of the baby involved contests this request, deeming it inappropriate under the current circumstances. Under Colorado law, Martinez must demonstrate actual innocence to qualify for state compensation, and a judge will decide if he meets this necessary legal standard in a forthcoming ruling.

stories.title: Rijiju heaps praise on J&K Waqf Board led by BJP man
stories.summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju praised the Jammu & Kashmir Waqf Board for its remarkable contributions across various sectors, particularly citing the development projects at the Hazratbal and Baba Reshi shrines. Rijiju remarked that this waqf board serves as a role model for similar entities nationwide. He also pledged to aid in skill development and training programs aimed at empowering the youth of Kashmir.

stories.title: Former Texas teacher admits stealing $520,000 in tax refunds as $4m more is stopped
stories.summary: In a shocking turn of events, former Texas teacher Jeremy Jarod Jackson confessed to orchestrating a scheme that siphoned off $520,000 in tax refunds. He masterfully altered his company's mailing address to funnel cheques into his own hands, triggering extensive financial wrongdoing. Luckily, IRS Criminal Investigation agents intervened, blocking Jackson from cashing in on an additional $4 million in fraudulent cheques.

A Texas cliff has yielded evidence that Indigenous communities drove bison over its edge repeatedly
stories.summary: Recent archaeological discoveries have uncovered that Indigenous peoples utilized cliffs as bison jumps for millennia. The Nighthawk site in Texas showcases bison remains from various hunting events, demonstrating the importance of these communal hunts in shaping social and political dynamics within communities. Evidence also indicates that hunters revisited this site across generations, refining their tools and strategies, challenging previous assumptions about bison hunting in the Southern Plains.

stories.title: 'Hold serious discussions with us': Akhilesh's public message to Congress on UP seat-sharing
Huang in there! Trump's bra-zen tribute to tech bro he rescued
Rodin's The Thinker jumps from $192,500 to $7.928m after 41 years off market
stories.summary: The auction at Christie's on November 17 witnessed a remarkable highlight with the sale of Rodin's 1955 sculpture, Le Penseur, for a staggering $7.928 million, reflecting a dramatic price increase since its 1985 auction. This notable sculpture, which had not changed hands in 41 years, underscores the strong appetite for fine art in a week when total sales at Christie's neared $974 million.

stories.title: Indians among 13 killed in UAE bus-truck crash, 14 injured
stories.summary: In a heartbreaking incident in Ras Al Khaimah, thirteen lives were tragically lost, including several Indian nationals, as confirmed by the Indian consulate in Dubai. A bus with 41 passengers collided with a parked truck, resulting in this devastating accident. Emergency teams quickly responded, transporting the injured to local hospitals for care. The consulate has established a helpline for those seeking further information and support regarding this unfortunate event.

Birmingham teen wins Alibaba's $200,000 prize for his self-taught robotics business
stories.summary: Suleymaan Khan, a brilliant self-taught robotics engineer hailing from Birmingham, has made waves at CoCreate Europe by securing a prestigious award. As the founder of SuleyNova Robotics, he created innovative educational robotics kits aimed at teaching coding and engineering concepts. Out of 20,000 competitors globally, the top 20 were chosen to pitch their inventions.

stories.title: Centre allots Delhi bungalow to Dalai Lama, Tibetan parliament-in-exile hails gesture
Ohio court protects homeowners' lakeside peninsula from a company's land claim after a 2019 survey
stories.summary: An Ohio court has definitively ruled that homeowners can retain their claim to a lakeside peninsula amid contentious property disputes. This decision followed a challenge from 1643 Limited LLC, which sought to redefine its property borders based on a 2019 survey. Although the appeals court confirmed the company's ownership of the adjacent beach, it firmly denied its rights over the peninsula itself, requiring a narrowed property description for the LLC.

stories.title: 'Udta Punjab' to 'Ubharta Punjab': BJP's Tarun Chugh pitches drug-free, gangs-free state
stories.summary: BJP leader Tarun Chugh has affirmed the alliance's determination to eliminate drug issues and reduce crime in Punjab. Both BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are collaborating to tackle organized crime and restore public safety. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has set an ambitious goal to achieve a drug-free Punjab by 2029, while also condemning the Aam Aadmi Party for failing to fulfill its drug eradication commitments.

Florida woman dies mysteriously on Antarctic cruise despite 'excellent health', family sues company a year later
San Diego 60-apartment project stalled; appeals court allows property owners' lawsuit to proceed
stories.summary: In San Diego, a family-owned auto-repair business encounters legal turmoil over an apartment development project that has stalled. The conflict arose from financial disagreements and allegations of misrepresentation between the original property owners and the developer. E&N, Inc. has taken legal action against Daniel Haas and his associates, and the court has determined that the case must proceed in litigation rather than arbitration, keeping E&N's claims alive for future resolution.

stories.title: Mike Alstott's foundation delivers Thanksgiving meals to firefighters
stories.summary: As the Thanksgiving holiday approached, Mike Alstott's Family Foundation distributed meals to firefighters in Hillsborough County. This annual gesture aims to make their holiday shift less lonely and more special. Each meal package included traditional Thanksgiving foods such as turkey, stuffing, and dessert for shared celebrations. Alstott emphasized the importance of thanking first responders who dedicate their time to community safety.

stories.title: ‘If I were Nirav Modi, I would get a red carpet’: Saurav Das attacks Centre over UK travel block
California woman wins half of ex-husband's pension earned during 10 years before marriage
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, California resident Lisa Seiwald has successfully claimed half of her ex-partner Nicholas Irias's pension benefits accrued during their years together. This ruling, affirmed by a California appeals court, reinforces her legal rights concerning shared financial assets despite Irias's arguments related to pension protections under state law. The case underscores the importance of recognizing arrangements made by couples in domestic partnerships.

stories.title: 'Sanghi monkeys disappointed': Congress hails Karthigai Deepam lighting at traditional spot
'Crime over decades': Judge unseals heavily redacted records on Ilhan Omar's home search. Did her father misrepresent her birth year so that she could become US citizen as a minor?
Cost Assessment: Heat pumps add $12,526 upfront; officials weigh changes before 2029
stories.summary: In California's Bay Area, homeowners will face steeper expenses when upgrading from natural gas heating systems due to stringent new emissions regulations. Transitioning to electric heat pumps is projected to cost around $12,526 for an average single-family residence. Although this adjustment aims to curtail nitrogen oxide emissions from gas furnaces, effective January 1, 2029, long-term energy savings may offset the initial investment.

stories.title: The OGs reunite: SAD gets 'bada bhai' tag in Punjab, but BJP has bigger ambitions
stories.summary: The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal have revived their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, six years after splitting over the Centre’s farm laws. The reunion restores a partnership that governed Punjab for 15 years, but the political arithmetic has shifted. The BJP has grown in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. With AAP and Congress still in contention, the alliance faces questions over farmer trust, Panthic support and seat-sharing.

stories.title: American tourist killed in Bangkok hotel brawl with MMA fighter ‘Frank the Tank’
stories.summary: An argument over hotel noise in Bangkok turned fatal after American tourist Kalif Edward Harper confronted Italian former MMA fighter Frank Eric Marques. Security footage reportedly shows Harper initiating the physical confrontation before Marques overpowered him. Harper later died, while Marques was arrested on suspicion of murder and maintains that he acted in self-defence. Police are continuing their investigation.

Ohio man ordered to repay ex-wife $101,723 for Colorado property costs after divorce dispute
stories.summary: Ohio's appellate court has ordered Willard H. Sturt to pay his ex-wife Diane F. Sturt over $101,000 due to his neglect of home expenses mandated in their divorce settlement. Willard's financial oversight left Diane responsible for property taxes, insurance, utilities, and repairs since 2020. The court also indicated a need to reevaluate attorney fees for Diane in light of this decision, reinforcing the importance of adhering to divorce agreements.

'Joined NCPI following all norms': Rebel TMC MPs respond to Lok Sabha Speaker's notice
'Ghosts of Muzaffarnagar riots haunting Azam Khan': BJP's Sanjeev Balyan rejects 'political revenge' charge
Flydubai’s Tel Aviv flights to resume within weeks, 2 months after hijack bid
stories.summary: Flydubai has received approval from Israeli transportation minister Miri Regev to resume its flights to Tel Aviv. The approval came after a meeting where security arrangements were discussed to ensure safe operations. The airline previously suspended services after an incident involving an attempted hijacking by an Omani co-pilot. Services are expected to restart pending clearance from Israel's security establishment in the coming weeks.

stories.title: Devon man regains mobility after being admitted for end-of-life care
6 years after split, BJP and SAD set to reunite in poll-bound Punjab
stories.summary: The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal are expected to announce their alliance for the upcoming Punjab assembly elections on Tuesday, with Amit Shah, Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal attending a joint press conference. The parties are expected to unveil their seat-sharing formula, with the BJP likely to contest more than the 23 seats it contested under their previous alliance.

stories.title: Delaware man loses $125,000 land to neighbour over 20-year-old goat pen
Why court cleared US Army to blow up toxic explosives despite lead contamination fears
Idaho man's $746,000 insurance payout sparks fight between wife and relatives
'Intention behind withdrawing papa’s security': Gandhis revisit concerns before Rajiv killing
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi has alleged that former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s security was deliberately withdrawn to facilitate his assassination. In a conversation with Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi about her book ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, she recalled raising concerns over his safety, including during a Bihar tour. Rahul also alleged that there was an intention behind the decision, saying his mother had left out some details from the book.

stories.title: Nuclear weapon in space? Russia may launch warhead-capable satellite by December
stories.summary: Russia is reportedly preparing to launch a satellite designed to carry a nuclear warhead by December. German intelligence has indicated that the satellite, known as Sputnik-S, has been assembled and stored for years. Dmitry Medvedev cites international law to justify potential nuclear weapon use, asserting state survival rights. He argues that international law permits nuclear usage in dire circumstances that threaten national existence.

stories.title: Ohio golf-cart firms revive tax challenge over $37,500 in 2024 licence fees
stories.summary: In a significant legal battle, two golf-cart rental companies in Ohio took on the Village of Put-in-Bay, disputing what they deemed excessive tax fees imposed on their operations. They contended that these taxes were outside the village's jurisdiction. The Ohio Sixth District Court of Appeals has allowed portions of the challenge to move forward, although refund claims for a certain tax year were dismissed on procedural grounds.

stories.title: ‘No one should be exempted from law’: Congress presses ally Vijay over collector's complaint against TVK MLA
stories.summary: Congress MP Manickam Tagore and DMK MP Kanimozhi have demanded action against TVK MLA C Arun Vignesh after the Kallakurichi district collector filed a police complaint against him over alleged inappropriate behaviour. Kanimozhi questioned Chief Minister Vijay over the delay in acting against his party MLA. Meanwhile, the NCW has sought a fair probe and an action-taken report from the Tamil Nadu DGP within seven days.

stories.title: SP’s ‘Jan-Man Manifesto’: Akhilesh Yadav to unveil 2027 poll roadmap on Constitution Day
Russia claims strikes on Starlink terminals, drone sites in Ukraine's Sumy
stories.summary: Russia's military conducted attacks on military sites in Ukraine's Sumy region using drones and missile strikes. In a separate incident, an overnight attack in Zaporizhzhia resulted in injuries to 11 individuals, including severe cases. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued warnings about impending Russian strike preparations while urging increased military aid from allies. He emphasized the importance of anti-ballistic missile systems for Ukraine's defense against aggression.

stories.title: ‘Unprovoked attack’: 2 Americans jailed for life for killing Canadian tech entrepreneur, partner
stories.summary: Two American men have been jailed for life in Dominica for the 2023 murder of Canadian tech entrepreneur Daniel Langlois and his partner, Dominique Marchand. A court sentenced Jonathan Lehrer and Robert Snyder Jr to two consecutive life terms each, describing the killings as an "unprovoked attack". The murders reportedly followed a long-running dispute over a road leading to Langlois' eco-resort.

stories.title: Sheikh Hasina requests Dec 16 return, picks Bangladesh Victory Day for comeback
stories.summary: Sheikh Hasina has announced her intention to return to Bangladesh on December 16, despite government threats. The current government has warned Hasina will face arrest upon her arrival for her past convictions. Following unrest and a student-led uprising, Hasina fled to India in August 2024, seeking asylum. Bangladesh's government has consistently reiterated its extradition request to India regarding Hasina.

stories.title: ‘Sex sells’: Trump marks Huang's Nvidia return with AI image of CEO holding red bra
'Distorted portrayal': Sonia Gandhi gets legal notice over VD Savarkar's remarks in memoir
stories.summary: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar's grandnephew, Satyaki Savarkar, issued a legal notice to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi about her memoir statements. He demands an unconditional apology and correction regarding her portrayal of Savarkar. The notice contends that the statements are historically inaccurate and prejudicial to Savarkar's legacy. It references historical contexts that allegedly contradict the claims made in her book.

stories.title: ‘Justice is not for sale’: Newsom demands federal reforms to limit presidential pardon powers
stories.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom has accused US President Donald Trump of turning presidential pardons into a business, alleging that wealthy allies and politically connected individuals have benefited from clemency. He called for sweeping federal reforms to limit presidential pardon powers. His remarks came after Trump criticised Newsom for granting clemency to 548 inmates on California's former death row.

stories.title: US probes Iran, Russia link after 50 vessels face cyberattack: Report
stories.summary: Washington is investigating Iran's potential involvement in numerous cyberattacks against energy tankers carrying hazardous materials. This probe includes incidents where vessels received bomb threats alleging possible explosions. Texas inheritance fight over ranches, yacht and millions leads to asset freeze limits
stories.summary: A high-stakes inheritance battle in Texas involves Lonnie K. Ledbetter Jr.'s significant estate, featuring sprawling ranches and luxury cars. Following the Texas Second Court of Appeals ruling, assets have been temporarily frozen, impacting his wife, Tawni Ledbetter. Disputes continue over Lonnie's mental capacity during key document signings, while some assets await judicial clarification. A court-appointed receiver will oversee daily expenses and management as the case progresses.

'He's not America's friend in Ukraine': US spy chief on Putin days after Trump's praise
Bangladesh unrest: Bengal CM Suvendu to write to EAM, may push to extend minority entry cut-off

Adhikari mentioned significant public concern in West Bengal due to the unrest across the border. Meanwhile, the BJP leader has called for protests against the violence in Bangladesh.

stories.summary: Four New York brothers who jointly ran a family farm ended up in court after their business relationship broke down. An appeals court rejected three brothers' demand for a route through their sibling's land, finding they had failed to prove it was essential to reach their gravel pit and timber areas. The court also upheld the decision to award their brother a 1988 Chevrolet Suburban under their property settlement.

stories.title: California drone operator spots great white near swimmer and alerts fisherman to danger
stories.summary: While fishing off the California coast, a fisherman faced a frightening close call with a great white shark. Oblivious to the danger lurking below, he was saved when a drone operator spotted the shark and warned him. The struggling fish near the boat likely caught the predator's interest. Such encounters underline the need for heightened awareness among water enthusiasts in the ocean's depths.

Absence of COP31 cover decision does not pause climate action in India, says Bhupender Yadav
stories.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, Bhupender Yadav, the Union environment minister, articulated India's dedication to climate change initiatives. He shared insights on India’s substantial advancements in solar power and renewable energy. Emphasising equity and climate justice, he voiced regret over the failure to achieve consensus on the cover decision. India’s proactive engagement with other nations showcases its resolve to address climate issues through collaboration.

Terry Farrell’s last home hits the market for £525,000 in historic Kent mansion
stories.summary: Terry Farrell's former apartment in Great Maytham Hall, Kent, is now on the market priced at £525,000. Marty Fox buys A$4.2 million home; says softer conditions favour buyers
stories.summary: Marty Fox, known from The Block, purchased a five-bedroom home in Burleigh Heads for A$4.2 million. The property is set for major renovations and is located near the beach. Fox believes the current market presents an excellent buying opportunity despite declining prices. He emphasizes a new investment strategy that focuses on renting fully renovated homes. His previous home will transition into a luxury holiday rental, contributing to his adjusted approach.

'India cherishes special friendship with Nepal': Jaishankar meets Nepal PM Balen Shah
stories.summary: S Jaishankar met Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah to foster bilateral relations during his visit to India. The discussions will focus on enhancing cooperation in areas such as trade and connectivity. Shah's delegation includes key ministers and a separate business group aiming to strengthen ties. Both leaders are expected to explore new agreements that benefit both nations. Shah's visit marks his first foreign bilateral trip since taking office in March.

'Some people still hesitate': PM Modi takes swipe at opposition over World Bank report on poverty
Luana Lopes Lara built Kalshi into a $40 billion prediction market giant; now faces US gambling law battle
stories.summary: Luana Lopes Lara, 30, became the world's youngest self-made female billionaire after co-founding Kalshi with Tarek Mansour in 2021. The prediction market platform is now valued at $40 billion. Known for working up to 16 hours a day, Lara built the company through years of regulatory battles. Now, Kalshi faces legal challenges over whether its event contracts violate US state gambling laws.

stories.title: Former Oregon interim police chief fired after criticising city leaders wins $935,000 in retaliation case
stories.summary: Sean Lundry, who formerly held the position of interim police chief in Oregon, has been awarded $935,000 by a federal jury. The verdict recognized that city officials penalized him for exercising his First Amendment rights, particularly after he raised concerns about the police chief recruitment process in January 2024. His criticisms included issues related to public records and alleged financial misconduct by the city.

Wife's support during husband's medical training becomes key in divorce asset battle
stories.summary: An Alabama appeals court reversed a divorce property settlement after finding that a lower court wrongly excluded a surgeon's medical-business interests, acquired during his marriage, from marital assets. His wife had supported the household while he completed medical training. The case has been sent back for a fresh valuation and division of the couple's property.

North Carolina farmer Noah Ranells has permanently protected 63 acres of his farm
stories.summary: Noah Ranells has taken a significant step by permanently conserving 63 acres of Fickle Creek Farm in Alamance County, North Carolina. This proactive move comes after a concerning decline in local farmland over the past decade. The farm is dedicated to producing meat, eggs, and vegetables for its community, ensuring a robust connection to local food sources.

stories.title: In the late 1800s, drainage and a new river channel altered Florida's Ocklawaha Prairie
stories.summary: The Ocklawaha Prairie Restoration Area spans 6,301 acres in Florida, focused on revitalizing wetlands and promoting wildlife habitats. Key restoration efforts have led to improved water quality and increased capacity for floodwater storage. Complementing these efforts is a Chornobyl Memorial Forest honoring victims of the 1986 nuclear disaster. Visitors can enjoy hiking, fishing, and primitive camping, while seasonal waterfowl hunting adds to the area's recreational appeal.

Neighbours' safety fears put 100-acre Kansas deer-hunting business under zoning rules
stories.summary: A Kansas appeals court has ruled that a 100-acre deer-hunting business run by a couple cannot be treated as an agricultural operation and must obtain a special-use zoning permit. The ruling followed objections from two neighbouring couples, who raised safety concerns about commercial hunting taking place close to their properties.

stories.title: Wisconsin’s $1.1M Barbie Dream House goes under contract
stories.summary: In Hudson, Wisconsin, a charming pink Victorian house constructed in 1900 has made a remarkable transformation from its original Goth style. Recently listed at $1.1 million, the property is now under contract. Featuring seven bedrooms and four bathrooms, the home boasts inviting spaces for gatherings and rentals. The creative homeowner painted it pink and opened it up for various uses, showcasing its versatility.

stories.title: Historic gold dredging damaged a California river used by salmon and steelhead
stories.summary: Major funding has been secured for restoration initiatives aimed at revitalizing the salmon habitat along the Tuolumne River. The project will reestablish 20 acres at La Grange, improving conditions for salmon and steelhead. With new side channels and a historic floodplain, the area will become conducive for salmon spawning. Collaborative efforts by various organizations since 2020 highlight an ongoing dedication to ecological preservation in this region.

stories.title: Titanic survivor Lucy, Lady Duff Gordon’s diamond ring sells for £150,000 after staying in family for generations
stories.summary: A diamond ring belonging to Titanic survivor Lucy, Lady Duff Gordon, sold for £150,000 at auction. The ring was expected to fetch around £80,000 but achieved a much higher final price. Lady Duff Gordon wore the ring during the sinking of the Titanic, which occurred in 1912. Other Titanic memorabilia, including a rare ticket and a postcard, were also sold at the auction.

Phoenix man's 2015 deed had wrong address; court upheld invalidation of rival deeds
stories.summary: A property dispute arose in Phoenix, Arizona, due to a mistake in a property's street address. Robert Olsen received a quitclaim deed from his father, which included incorrect address details but correct property descriptions. Bonitas Casitas LLC later claimed ownership and filed a lawsuit, leading to competing claims over the property. The Arizona Court of Appeals upheld the lower court's ruling, reaffirming the validity of Olsen's original deed.

stories.title: Chef Jose Andres rescues Baltimore's 45-year-old Thanksgiving food tradition
stories.summary: Cynthia Brooks' efforts to continue her mother Bea Gaddy's 45-year-old Thanksgiving food tradition in Baltimore faced a setback after donations fell short, leaving her with only eight turkeys days before the event. Celebrity chef Jose Andres World Central Kitchen and the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services stepped in with food and resources, helping save the annual dinner that began in 1981.

stories.title: Marshall’s 700 Meals: Family keeps holiday dinners going; her home serves hundreds in need
stories.summary: Carolyn Marshall honors her late mother, Reverend Annie Woodridge, by preparing festive meals for those in need. Overcoming various obstacles, she turned her home into a hub for food prep, drawing support from volunteers who help package and deliver meals. This initiative has blossomed into a cherished family and community effort, reinforcing the values of kindness and remembrance associated with her mother's legacy during the holidays.

stories.title: Adirondack Mountain Rescue: Becky’s arrival triggered search; rescuers found owner alive
stories.summary: When a basset hound named Becky showed up unaccompanied at a mountain lodge, it triggered an urgent search for her owner, a 69-year-old man living with dementia. Spending a night in the frigid wilderness, he was finally located by a hunter. Thanks to Becky's unexpected arrival, the rescue effort commenced quickly, potentially saving her owner's life.

The factory owner indicated that approximately 300 workers were present during the incident, which occurred on Saturday evening. Investigation teams are working to determine the cause of the fire while assessing the damage.

This event took place at the three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum hosted in Purana Qila, India. The BJP's montage highlighted contrasting statements made by Pakistani officials regarding Kashmir and India's culture. During the forum, Malik referenced historical figures associated with the Purana Qila fortress.

stories.title: 'Population up in 40 China-border villages': Amit Shah reaches out to Arunachal amid dam protests
stories.summary: Amit Shah unveiled key development initiatives in Arunachal Pradesh as part of the Vibrant Villages Programme, noting a population increase in 40 border villages that has curbed migration. He highlighted the need for self-reliance in food production while assuring local leaders of the Centre's ongoing support for development projects. Additionally, the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047 was introduced, focusing on future growth strategies.

Maine court upholds $1 million museum donation 14 years after collector's death
stories.summary: A charitable trust from Maine faced a legal battle over a donation intended for another museum. The Supreme Judicial Court determined that this donation did not violate any prior agreements. While the trust was obligated to fulfill its financial duties to the original museum, it could also manage its assets.

stories.title: Delta Seat Lawsuit: Judge lets claims proceed; airlines may face scrutiny over seat descriptions
stories.summary: Passengers have raised concerns, claiming Delta Air Lines sold them window seats that lacked actual windows. A New York federal judge recently gave the green light for a class-action lawsuit against the airline. This issue emerged when a traveler discovered his seat had no window, prompting Delta to argue that seat assignments aren’t guaranteed. United Airlines is facing similar complaints about windowless seating as well.

Galloo Island Conservation Easement: TILT protects 1,410 acres; Patten family retains ownership
stories.summary: A landmark conservation deal has been executed for Galloo Island, safeguarding 1,410 acres of pristine land. The Thousand Islands Land Trust has joined forces with Galloo Island Farms and the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation to enforce permanent land use restrictions aimed at preserving the island's ecological integrity.

stories.title: Carnegie Museum will prepare three sauropods in public; researchers study rare skin samples
stories.summary: Three sauropod fossils from Wyoming, nicknamed Daisy, Lucky, and Lucy, are headed for Pittsburgh. A $5 million donation from Ken Griffin will construct a public fossil preparation laboratory at the Carnegie Museum of Natural History. Visitors will be able to observe the cleaning and studying process of these 150-million-year-old dinosaurs. Additionally, research will focus on rare fossilized skin samples associated with the fossils.

stories.summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin will lead a rally in Hyderabad to counter criticism about the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Union minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar supports this event, claiming it to be historic, and anticipates a large turnout. Kumar accused opposition parties, including Congress and BRS, of collaborating to impede BJP's growth in Telangana. He argued that only Indian citizens should have the right to elect their leaders.

stories.title: Sabarimala pilgrimage: Kerala puts security, transport arrangements in place amid devotee rush
stories.summary: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa Temple has commenced its much-anticipated annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage. This year, the influx of devotees is met with extensive security measures and administrative support. The Kerala government has undertaken significant infrastructure upgrades, enhancing roads and transport services. Throughout the pilgrimage, police will be actively deployed to ensure safety and manage traffic. This first phase will last until December 27, followed by festivities for Makaravilakku.

stories.title: After first-ever foreign office talks, Jaishankar calls for deeper India-Lebanon ties
stories.summary: S Jaishankar, India’s External Affairs Minister, sent heartfelt National Day wishes to Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi and the people of Lebanon. With a focus on deepening diplomatic relations, both countries recently initiated their first foreign office consultations. These discussions emphasized political, security, and economic partnerships, reflecting India's vital contributions to peacekeeping in Lebanon. The intent is to foster stronger ties via consistent high-level dialogues and collaborative efforts.

Authorities are now probing the oversight of such projects in densely populated neighborhoods, questioning the responsiveness to residents' concerns before the tragic incident occurred.

stories.title: Former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
stories.summary: At a recent auction, a rare lock of George Washington’s hair sold for an impressive $4,000. This fascinating artifact once belonged to John Gadsby, who shared a meal with Washington shortly before his passing. Gadsby’s granddaughter later cherished the lock alongside a portrait of the first president, making it a remarkable piece of history. Notably, Washington's hair has previously commanded prices nearing $40,000 at auctions, alongside other treasured memorabilia.

Her mission, not only to restore their health but also to secure safe environments for their future, has brought to light the troubling issue of non-native turtles being wrongfully released into inappropriate habitats.

Despite lacking receipts or photographs, she provided a detailed list with estimated values. The landlord's management company challenged the award, arguing that sufficient proof was missing. The appeals court upheld the ruling, stating that the unique nature of the items justified Davis's valuation.

stories.title: More than 8,000 people applied to be NASA astronauts last time and just 10 were picked
stories.summary: NASA is currently accepting applications until December 3, 2026, for aspiring astronauts who dream of exploring outer space. To qualify, applicants must be U.S. citizens possessing a master's degree and relevant experience. Those with medical certifications or extensive flight backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply. Selected astronauts will undergo rigorous training before embarking on missions to the Moon and Mars, with final candidates expected to be revealed by late 2027.

stories.title: An LA diner that served generations since 1924 shut down in 2025, has reopened under a nonprofit operator
stories.summary: After a lengthy shutdown in 2025 due to property issues, Original Pantry Cafe in Los Angeles has triumphantly reopened! With new management from Hope the Mission, the cafe will utilize its profits to bolster homelessness services. Diners can still indulge in the beloved classic menu while also enjoying fresh additions. Although hours have shifted, there are plans to bring back 24-hour service.

stories.title: As ice receded on a Swiss Alpine pass, archaeologists discovered a 4,000 years old bronze neck ring
stories.summary: A remarkable discovery at Lötschen Pass has unearthed a 4,000-year-old bronze neck ring, making it the first metal artifact found at this significant historical site. While previous discoveries were primarily organic materials preserved in ice, this find suggests that ancient peoples may have practiced mobility through Alpine passes, connecting various regions. Experts speculate that the ring could have served as a ritual offering or token of gratitude.

Asmongold's infamous house controversy returns after GTA 6 livestream with girlfriend Kaise
stories.summary: During a hilarious GTA 6 livestream, Asmongold and Kaise found themselves exploring a disheveled virtual home. Kaise jokingly compared the digital mess to Asmongold's real-life living situation, prompting laughs and nostalgia about Asmongold's cleanliness challenges. Even with improvements noted in 2026, his home remains a hot topic among viewers, fueling the ongoing chatter about his infamous house saga.

stories.summary: IShowSpeed celebrated a remarkable achievement by completing GTA 6's story mode in just 52 hours, far surpassing his initial plan of a 12-hour stream. His enthusiasm led him to extend the session, and upon finishing, he expressed heartfelt thanks and hinted at exciting future plans. Although a PS5 crash presented some obstacles, his progress was secure, keeping fans on the edge of their seats for his next move.

stories.title: Indiana man paid $9,489 towards condo debt after $9,213 judgment, but court says he still owes more
stories.summary: Onnie James Florence Jr. encountered significant legal troubles stemming from his failure to pay homeowners' association fees for his condominium in Indiana. After acquiring the unit, he neglected to keep up with payments while residing in Illinois. The Meridian Arch Owners Association successfully secured a default judgment against him for the overdue fees. Despite making a partial payment later, additional fees remained unpaid, prompting ongoing legal action.

stories.title: Dua Lipa's £6.75 million London home renovation set to finish in 2027
stories.summary: Dua Lipa is making waves with the transformation of her Victorian home in Hampstead, which includes an ambitious plan for a luxurious basement pool. After encountering numerous setbacks, the project received the green light to commence construction in 2024. Local environmental concerns have prompted strict adherence to regulations, pushing the anticipated completion to 2027. With an investment estimated at around £3 million, this renovation underscores its intricate and grand vision.

Scientists flew drones through humpback whales' breath off Canada and sequenced entire genomes
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of St Andrews have pioneered a groundbreaking technique to harness whale DNA through the use of drones. This method captures genetic material from the whales' breath, often referred to as whale snot. Their findings successfully sequenced complete genomes from specimens gathered off the coast of British Columbia.

He allegedly misrepresented his military background, impersonated government officials, and manipulated suppliers to stifle competition. Furthermore, investigators found he sold counterfeit military gear, mislabeling it as American-made but failing to meet specifications. He faces several charges as the investigation proceeds.

stories.title: Beverly Hills penthouse sells for $21M, with rooftop pool and $18,740 monthly dues
stories.summary: In a stunning real estate move, a penthouse in Beverly Hills has shattered local records by selling for $21 million within just 10 days of listing. Initially priced at $27.5 million, the luxe property ultimately changed hands for 24% less, showcasing its many high-end amenities and hotel-style services for residents. The fortunate buyer also saved over $1 million in transfer taxes by opting for Beverly Hills over Los Angeles.

stories.title: New York couple give 77 acres to protect drinking water and preserve wildlife
stories.summary: Jerry and Joanne Braun donated approximately 77 acres of land to the Town of Newburgh. This land donation aims to protect the drinking water supply sourced from the Chadwick Lake Reservoir. The couple requested reimbursement for subdividing the land, not seeking payment for it. Residents will still have access for passive recreational activities like hiking and enjoying nature.

stories.summary: Tŷ Hafan, a remarkable children's hospice located in Wales, has triumphed by surpassing its fundraising goal during the Every Precious Life campaign. stories.summary: In a noteworthy real estate transaction, a luxurious mansion in Glenvar Heights has been sold for an impressive $13.25 million, nearly doubling its original price. Jose Dans Jr. had acquired the property for $7.3 million just in 2024, transforming it into a lavish estate complete with a main house, guesthouse, and cabana.

stories.title: NASA is offering $1 million to anyone who can solve one big problem standing in the way of building a human settlement on the Moon
stories.summary: NASA has launched the Moon Base Challenge, encouraging students to develop solutions for lunar habitation. The initiative offers $1 million in prizes to student teams from high schools and universities. Teams will focus on areas like power generation, life-support systems, and astronaut safety to address the complexities of lunar living. Registration for the competition is open until January 25, 2027, to eligible educational institutions.

stories.title: Humayun, Sher Shah and ‘one fort’: Pakistan minister highlights Purana Quila’s layered history at SCO forum
stories.summary: At the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, hosted at Delhi's Purana Quila, Pakistan's minister Musadik Malik elaborated on the site's historical relevance, paying tribute to Mughal emperor Humayun and Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri. Judge blocks Trump's 250-foot arch near Arlington over lack of congressional approval
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a federal judge has barred the construction of a controversial monument near Arlington National Cemetery. This decision follows an earlier temporary injunction from another judge, with local government and community members expressing strong concerns regarding the monument's potential effects. The Trump administration aims to appeal this ruling, defending their vision for the monument amidst ongoing debates over presidential authority regarding national landmarks.

stories.title: 94 acres in Massachusetts approved for 26 homes may become a $2 million wildlife conservation area
stories.summary: In Gloucester, Massachusetts, a 26-home housing initiative is meeting resistance from environmental groups. The Essex County Greenbelt intends to purchase the 94-acre woodland to preserve the area's natural environment. Future objectives include establishing walking trails to connect this space with adjacent conservation properties. Though most funding is secured, necessary approvals from the local council are still pending, alongside the open wetlands application by the Conservation Commission.

stories.title: Hilma af Klint painting expected to fetch SEK 8m sells for record SEK 128.9m
stories.summary: A rare painting by Hilma af Klint just sold for a jaw-dropping 128.9 million Swedish kronor at auction! It blew past its original estimate of 6 to 8 million kronor. Painted in 1920 and titled Ser III No. 5, this piece had been with a family for over 30 years and shows off af Klint's unique style and spirituality.

stories.title: 'Goondaism isn't a bug': BJP, BRS attack Congress over Meta office vandalism
stories.summary: Youth Congress workers caused a commotion at the Meta office in Hyderabad, protesting account suspensions affecting their leaders. This vandalism was denounced by leaders from both the BJP and BRS, who claimed it jeopardized the city's business-friendly image. N Ramchander Rao, president of Telangana BJP, criticized Congress for promoting such destructive behavior. Meanwhile, K T Rama Rao of BRS articulated that such incidents erode trust in companies like Meta.

stories.title: 'Modi ji should apologise': Congress alleges PM's Lucknow event led to cancellation of four weddings
'His visa wasn't immediately renewed': Prince Harry's reported US immigration trouble behind UK move; is it resolved now?
N-safety regulator AERB grants criticality nod to Rajasthan’s N-plant unit-8, reactor moves closer to power generation
In 2025, a 24-year-old Montreal woman died mysteriously at an Istanbul hotel; food poisoning was suspected. A year later, investigation now points to deadly pesticide used to kill bedbugs
US judge blocks Trump's bid to redirect $1.3 billion in homelessness funding to temporary housing
stories.summary: A federal judge ruled against the Trump administration's plan to change homelessness funding priorities. The judge determined the changes exceeded the authority granted to the Department of Housing and Urban Development. Additionally, the ruling requires the agency to reopen grant applications for organizations seeking funding support. HUD Secretary Scott Turner expressed dissatisfaction with the decision, citing potential disruptions to funding processes.

stories.title: Arizona parents win appeal after HOA blocks gate change for disabled son's golf cart access
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, an Arizona couple, Kevin and Jennifer LoPresto, sought to replace their single gate with a wider double gate to accommodate their disabled son's golf cart. The Wigwam Creek South Community Association rejected their request and pushed for arbitration. However, an appeals court sided with the LoPrestos, allowing their lawsuit against the HOA to continue and awarding them reasonable legal fees for the appeals process.

stories.title: 'Working to suppress India’s rise': US panel report flags China's support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor
stories.summary: In May 2025, China's military support for Pakistan intensified India's security dilemmas. This report reveals Beijing's ongoing strategies aimed at stifling India's strategic advancements through both military and economic tactics. With Pakistan receiving advanced weaponry, India's concerns over a dual-threat scenario have been amplified. The evolving military alliance between China and Pakistan poses greater risks for India moving forward, showcasing a troubling shift in regional security dynamics.

stories.title: 'When you promote rakshasas': BJP MP Nishikant Dubey takes swipe at Meta amid youth Congress protests
'Country's character remains the same': PM Modi praises people for heeding call to not buy gold
MEA clears Taj Mahal visit for Pakistan delegation, no nod for Nizamuddin dargah
stories.summary: A Pakistani delegation, led by Musadik Masood Malik, is in India for the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum. They have been permitted to visit the Taj Mahal, Humayun's Tomb, and Dilli Haat. However, their visit to Nizamuddin dargah has not been security cleared. This visit marks the first by a Pakistani minister to India in three years. The programme emphasizes shared civilizational heritage and cross-cultural engagement among SCO member countries.

stories.title: 'India not a rogue state': Wangchuk claims police deployment withdrawn after court hearing
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk accused the Ladakh administration of effectively placing him under house arrest since November 11. He appealed to President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to uphold constitutional values. Wangchuk expressed concerns about government misuse of police for actions that compromise their duties. He opposed the timing of Hill Council elections, arguing that many residents would be unable to participate.

stories.title: 'Census-related delimitation should be put on hold for 25 years': CPM general secretary MA Baby
'Voices carry no weight': Wangchuk warns Ladakh's alienation could hurt national security during war
Evening newswrap: BJP targets Rahul as Trump hails India's GDP growth; PM Modi recreates 'gamcha' wave in Bihar and more
stories.summary: Donald Trump lauded India's remarkable 7 percent GDP growth recently, allowing the BJP to take jabs at Rahul Gandhi. Meanwhile, PM Narendra Modi unveiled the Nitish Setu in Bihar, evoking memories of past election celebrations. On the global stage, Mexican authorities arrested Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, an FBI's most-wanted fugitive, amid escalating clashes.

stories.title: ‘Thank you Singh Sb’: Sonia Gandhi acknowledges Sikh man's effort to preserve her childhood home
stories.summary: Acquiring Sonia Gandhi's old home in Italy, Sukhdev Singh Kang aspires to establish a museum in her honor. He received public acknowledgment from Sonia Gandhi on social media, expressing his gratitude. The post sparked varied responses, blending admiration with light political humor, and highlighted the Sikh community's fondness for her. Kang considers her recognition of his efforts deeply meaningful and transformative.

stories.title: 'Third contender has arrived': Owaisi says new UP alliance has unsettled Yogi, Akhilesh
stories.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi expressed that the emergence of the 'Samajik Parivartan Morcha' has notably unsettled both Yogi Adityanath and Akhilesh Yadav. With a strategy to become a formidable alternative for the upcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, Owaisi challenged the assertions of vote-splitting, highlighting the Samajwadi Party's mixed performance across different states.

stories.title: Italy's ex-police chief dies amid probe into mafia case cover-up; suicide suspected
'Judgment will create confusion': TN consulting legal experts on SC ruling in Karthigai Deepam row
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government is currently consulting legal experts about the Supreme Court's recent ruling. The judgment allows a one-time lighting of a lamp atop Thirupparankundram hill during Karthigai Deepam. Officials are deliberating on whether to comply with this ruling or challenge it legally. Social justice minister Vanni Arasu has expressed strong opposition to the judgment.

stories.title: PM Modi launches projects worth Rs 34,000cr in Bihar; says state now known for development, not scams
Prove you're alive with a selfie: What pensioners need to know about Jeevan Pramaan
stories.summary: The Digital Life Certificate system in India provides a hassle-free way for pensioners to verify their identities annually through a simple selfie. Utilizing Aadhaar authentication via the Jeevan Pramaan and UIDAI’s AadhaarFaceRD apps, this initiative especially helps elderly and physically challenged individuals avoid travel difficulties. As part of a broader campaign to promote this service among pensioners, they must verify their information's accuracy before submission.

stories.title: NY woman’s 20-year apartment fight continues after court rejects landlord’s commercial lease claim
stories.summary: A landlord's attempts to reclaim a Manhattan apartment are hindered due to ongoing claims about rent stabilization. E. Terese Carpenter has resided in the unit for over 20 years, despite the existence of a commercial lease. The appeals court identified unresolved issues regarding the actual use of the apartment and the landlord's awareness of the situation.

stories.title: 'First violence, now poisonous liquor': Rahul Gandhi accuses Manipur BJP govt of negligence over spurious alcohol deaths
HC pulls up UP govt over registration of FIRs under law declared 'stillborn' by SC
Trump, Xi, Putin agree on UN reforms: What it means for India's permanent UNSC seat bid
Bangladesh wage protests: Clashes erupt between garment workers and police, dozens of factories shut
stories.summary: Tensions soared in Ashulia as garment workers rallied for higher wages, leading to confrontations with law enforcement. To maintain control, the police deployed tear gas to break up the protest after production was halted. Reports revealed that more than 50 factories chose to close temporarily amid the unrest, with indefinite shutdowns and sit-ins occurring in various industrial areas. This turmoil highlights the ongoing struggle for improved pay and working conditions.

stories.title: Pennsylvania county sold home for $109,000 after notices went to dead owner; court sets sale aside
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania appeals court recently ruled to cancel a tax sale of a home in Garnet Valley. The tax sale occurred due to the county's failure to notify the correct property owner about unpaid taxes. Bonnie Wilson's home was sold despite her and her son Kevin both being deceased. The appeals court emphasized the need for tax bureaus to investigate further when notices are returned.

stories.title: China-Pakistan ties raise two-front conflict risk for India: US report
stories.summary: A US congressional commission has warned that China's growing military support for Pakistan could heighten the risk of a two-front conflict for India. In its report, it urged Washington to deepen defence cooperation with New Delhi, particularly in the Indian Ocean, including intelligence sharing and joint tracking of Chinese naval and submarine movements. It also flagged Beijing's expanding strategic presence in the region.

stories.title: 'Nitish conceived the project': Prashant Kishor's rare praise for former Bihar CM with a jibe at BJP, RJD
Ex-Trump press secretary Katie Zacharia under probe for posing as lawyer without passing bar
'Will find way forward through dialogue': Amit Shah assures Arunachal locals amid Siang dam protests
7 killed as tribal feud over forest ownership triggers gunfight in Pakistan
stories.summary: Seven people were killed in a gunfight between the Gilal and Kaloch tribes over a decades-old forest ownership dispute in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, PTI reported, quoting police. The clash took place in Battagram district on Thursday night, leaving four members of the Gilal tribe and three from the Kaloch tribe dead. Repeated efforts to resolve the dispute have failed.

stories.title: Congress vs Congress over Siraj: Party MP tells Imran Masood to 'not interfere'
stories.summary: Congress MP Ranjeet Ranjan advised fellow MP Imran Masood to keep politics and sports separate. Masood had criticized the selection process after Mohammed Siraj was excluded from the Test squad. Siraj, India's top wicket-taker in the current World Test Championship cycle, was notable for his performance.

stories.title: Bangladesh violence: Fresh arson attacks reported as unrest continues amid Sheikh Hasina's return plans
stories.summary: Tensions continue to rise in Bangladesh as fresh arson attacks erupt in response to Sheikh Hasina's anticipated return. In an effort to restore peace following violent incidents that claimed multiple lives, paramilitary forces have been mobilized. Communication services in her hometown have resumed after disruptions caused by the unrest, while over a hundred Awami League members have been arrested in Dhaka.

stories.title: PM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu in Bihar, recreates 'poll victory' moment with 'gamcha' wave
More than 100,000 strangers have shared handwritten stories anonymously
stories.summary: More than 100,000 anonymous handwritten stories have been shared in The Strangers Project since its inception. Individuals recount personal experiences centered on themes such as love, loss, and hope. Brandon Doman founded the project in 2009 to create a space for these shared experiences. The Strangers Project is currently located at the World Trade Center Oculus in New York City.

stories.title: NJ appeals $11.25M verdict for woman handcuffed during stroke by trooper
stories.summary: In a tragic turn of events, Cheryl Lynn Rhines suffered a severe stroke while driving and was mistakenly arrested for intoxication. The responding trooper overlooked the critical nature of her medical emergency, causing significant delays in her treatment. This negligence resulted in lasting brain injuries and communication issues for Rhines.

stories.title: CBI Recovers Cash and jewellery from CGST Superintendent home
Balochistan shutdown: Markets shut across Quetta as alliance protests rising inflation, insecurity
stories.summary: A significant shutdown swept across Quetta and several districts in Balochistan on Thursday, driven by widespread protests led by the All Parties Alliance. The strike aimed to highlight urgent issues such as deteriorating law and order, soaring unemployment rates, and rampant inflation. Major commercial hubs faced complete shutdowns, resulting in major disruptions.

stories.title: Taj Mahal, Humayun's Tomb on wish list as Pakistan minister visits India; what Centre said on travel curbs
stories.summary: Pakistan minister Musadik Malik, in India for the SCO meeting, expressed a desire to visit the Taj Mahal and other historic landmarks. The Centre clarified that visiting ministers faced no travel restrictions. Malik also stressed the importance of cultural exchanges and dialogue in improving regional ties amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.

stories.title: 'Look beyond what an image shows': Hindu seer's open letter to Rahul, Priyanka over Shiva-Parvati post
Army jawan found dead near Jammu bus stand under suspicious circumstances; probe launched
Florida battles historic flooding as storms move further north
stories.summary: In Central Florida, residents face rising water levels from recent heavy rain, prompting evacuation alerts. Authorities urge those living by the St. Johns River to brace for potential evacuations as flooding disrupts Thanksgiving festivities. Emergency responders are tirelessly aiding those stranded in waterlogged neighborhoods, while meteorologists predict that both heavy rainfall and flooding risks will persist for the foreseeable future.

stories.title: 'Trampling Sikh sentiments': Congress questions naming of Bihar bridge as Nitish Setu
'Main chunauti ko chunauti diye bina reh nahi sakta’: PM Modi at IIT Kharagpur’s 75th anniversary
'PM-HM jodi still searching for majority': Congress takes dig at Centre over delimitation bill
Pregnant at 34 weeks, New York nurse completes all seven major marathons
stories.summary: Deirdre Keane, an inspiring nurse practitioner from New York, achieved a remarkable feat in 2026 by completing all seven World Marathon Majors while pregnant. Approaching her training thoughtfully after learning about her pregnancy, she ran the New York City Marathon at 34 weeks, pushing boundaries she once thought were fixed.

stories.title: Mexican cartel leaders, 19 others indicted in US over drug and arms trafficking
stories.summary: In a significant legal move, a federal grand jury has charged leaders of the La Nueva Familia Michoacana cartel along with 19 associates. Key allegations against them include drug trafficking and weapons smuggling. Prominent figures Johnny Hurtado Olascoaga and Jose Alfredo Hurtado Olascoaga are on the run, purportedly using violence and bribery to grow their criminal empire and engage in human smuggling.

stories.title: After his wife Susan died, Warren Lewis learned her body cannot be donated to science because of this
stories.summary: Susan Lewis's noble desire to donate her body to science was thwarted by a miscommunication. After her passing, her husband, Warren Lewis, tirelessly advocated for revisions to the university's body donation policy. This advocacy birthed a collaboration with Macquarie University, enabling weekend donations and ensuring that future donors' wishes are honored, despite bureaucratic hurdles. Susan's journey underscores the complexities surrounding body donations in Australia.

stories.title: Federal Lawsuit: Maine family challenges rooster fines; alleges free-speech violations
stories.summary: David and Sara LeBlanc have taken legal action against Ogunquit, Maine, after being penalized for setting up rooster sculptures outside their home. These sculptures symbolize support for their daughter Pyper, who is autistic and adores roosters. The town has classified the sculptures as commercial advertising for their restaurant, Omelette Factory, and although the couple has removed them, local residents have rallied to display the sculptures in unity.

stories.title: Air Niugini plane makes emergency landing in Philippines, all 146 safe
stories.summary: An incident occurred involving an Air Niugini aircraft with 146 individuals on board that indicated possible engine fire. The flight performed an emergency landing at Davao International Airport shortly after midnight. Passengers and crew were safely evacuated via emergency slides, with no injuries reported. Other flights at the airport were briefly suspended for safety checks and to assist those on the aircraft.

stories.title: Negligence Lawsuit: Mother seeks $8.7 million after son loses eye; Oregon age rules face scrutiny
stories.summary: A negligence lawsuit has emerged following a tragic e-bike accident involving a 14-year-old boy during a birthday sleepover hosted by Tessa and Matthew Cohen. The allegations claim that the Cohens provided electric bikes without adequate supervision or safety protocols. As a result, the boy sustained life-altering injuries, requiring significant medical attention. The lawsuit demands $8.7 million in damages to address his painful recovery and its long-term consequences.

stories.title: 'Apologise for 1962 humiliation': Rijiju fires 4 questions at Rahul over 'compromised PM' jibe
Himalayan marmot droppings could help track climate change
Illinois couple loses appeal over fence installed after trespassing and car theft
NMC hikes appeal fee for medical colleges up to six-fold; private institutions to pay Rs 3.54 lakh
stories.summary: Medical colleges in India will face significantly higher appeal fees to challenge National Medical Commission's decisions. Government institutions must now pay Rs 1.77 lakh for appeals, while private institutions will pay Rs 3.54 lakh. The new fee structure is effective for appeals relating to the 2026-27 academic year onwards. The previous uniform fee of Rs 59,000 has been revised to these new amounts.

stories.title: NMC plans to simplify rules for Indians who study medicine abroad
India, France condemn Pahalgam, Red Fort terror attacks at counter-terror meet
Amit Shah: PM used govt instruments to improve lives
Pakistan attending SCO event won't dilute IWT stand: Govt
stories.summary: Denies Claims Of Movement Curbs On Pak Minister Malik, Others

stories.title: Florida man admits $42M medicare fraud, bought yacht and luxury cars
No China input yet on GoPro cam used during Pahalgam attack: NIA
stories.summary: NIA director general Rakesh Aggarwal reported that a GoPro camera linked to the Pahalgam attack, which resulted in 26 fatalities including 25 tourists, remains unclaimed by China. This camera was lost in July 2025 when authorities neutralized the terrorists. Meanwhile, allegations by Mathew VanDyke regarding his treatment in custody haven’t been addressed in court. The investigation into the camera's origins continues as officials await China's response.

stories.title: PM Modi’s remark on jobs & wages a confession: Congress
North Carolina couple noticed kitchen floor dipping weeks after moving in; court rejects their claims
stories.summary: After moving into their new home, Nate and Christine Holton noticed troubling dips in their kitchen floor. Despite reaching out to the builder, concerns about their foundation emerged again over time. In January 2025, they pursued a lawsuit claiming construction defects, but the court deemed their claims time-barred. Ultimately, their assertions of negligence and deceit went unproven, as they couldn't establish additional financial harm.

stories.summary: India Announces 1st Official Trip To Start Tomorrow
